docs.title: WitFoo Analytics Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for WitFoo Analytics — a security operations platform that transforms raw security data into actionable intelligence.

docs.title: Platform Overview
docs.text:
WitFoo Analytics ingests security artifacts from your infrastructure, correlates them into incidents, and provides comprehensive reporting, compliance tracking, and threat intelligence capabilities.

  • Signals

    Search, classify, and enrich security artifacts with lead rules and automated classification.

    User Guide

  • Graph

    Visualize relationships between network nodes and edges for threat mapping and asset management.

    User Guide

  • Observer

    Monitor work units, collections, and observations with customizable MO definitions.

    User Guide

  • Reporter

    Executive summaries, compliance readiness, tool effectiveness analysis, and cost/savings reports.

    User Guide

  • CyberGrid

    Subscribe to and publish threat intelligence feeds across organizations.

    User Guide

  • Health

    Monitor container health, system resources, and configure alerting thresholds.

    User Guide

docs.text: The Admin Guide covers system configuration and user management for WitFoo Analytics administrators.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: Create, edit, disable and enable user accounts.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Understand the permission system: 108 permissions across 22 categories. The full list is in the Permissions Reference.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Configure business metrics, compliance frameworks, authentication, notifications, and certificates.

docs.title: Conductor
docs.text: Manage the Conductor signal pipeline for log collection.

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text:
The Settings menu is the gear icon in the page header.

Task Location Create a user Settings > User Management > Create User Disable or enable a user Settings > User Management > Disable or Enable on the user's row Change a role Settings > Role Management Set primary framework Settings > General Settings > Frameworks Configure SMTP Settings > General Settings > Notifications Upload TLS cert Settings > General Settings > Certificates Configure AI and MCP Settings > General Settings > AI Setup

User Management and Role Management appear only for users who hold the admin permission (the built-in Admin and Platform Admin roles).

docs.title: Conductor
docs.text: Conductor is WitFoo's signal pipeline for collecting, parsing, and exporting security logs to WitFoo Analytics.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    S[Syslog/Beats/NetFlow Sources] --> SS[Signal Server]
    V[Vendor APIs] --> SC[Signal Client]
    SS --> SP[Signal Parser]
    SC --> SP
    SP --> AF[Artifact Filter]
    AF --> AE[Artifact Exporter]
    AE --> AI[Analytics Artifact Ingestion]

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service Port Description Signal Server 514/udp, 514/tcp, 5044, 5045, 6514, 7514, 2055/udp Receives syslog, Beats and NetFlow/IPFIX input Signal Client Internal Polls vendor APIs (pull connectors) Signal Parser Internal Parses raw signals into structured data Artifact Filter Internal Filters and normalizes artifacts Artifact Exporter Internal Sends artifacts to Analytics via HMAC-authenticated HTTP Broker 4223 NATS JetStream for inter-service messaging

On a WFA appliance running WFA 2.5.1 or later:

  • The broker (4223) is published on 127.0.0.1 only.
  • 2055/udp is published on Conductor and AIO + Conductor nodes and opened in the host firewall. The NetFlow/IPFIX listener stays off until you enable it under Log Servers in the Conductor UI. See Log Server Configuration.

The Conductor sends artifacts to the Analytics receiver at https://<analytics-host>:8443/v1/conductor/artifacts/batch, or the internal port 8090 on an AIO + Conductor appliance. See Conductor API.

docs.title: HMAC Authentication
docs.text:
The Artifact Exporter authenticates with Analytics using HMAC-SHA256:

  1. Body hash: hex(SHA256(body))
  2. Message: timestamp + "." + bodyHash
  3. Signature: hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, message))

Configured via ANALYTICS_SECRET on both Conductor and Analytics.

docs.title: Start/Stop
docs.text:
A Conductor appliance is managed with the WFA CLI:

sudo wfa start
sudo wfa stop
sudo wfa restart
sudo wfa status

See WFA CLI Reference.

docs.title: Conductor UI
docs.text:
Access the Conductor UI through the Analytics reverse proxy. Requires conductor:read permission. The UI uses JWT auth bridge — Analytics JWT tokens are validated and mapped to Conductor roles.

On a standalone Conductor node, the Conductor UI serves its own sign-in page. From 1.2.0, its SAML sign-in signs in only accounts whose Auth Source is SAML (SSO). See User Management & Authentication.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Upgrade every Conductor, including separate or remote Conductor nodes, at the same time as Analytics or before it. A Conductor on 1.1.5 or older sending to 1.2.0 Analytics keeps only about one record per page or poll for several pull connectors. See Upgrading to 1.2.0.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: WitFoo Analytics 1.2.0 uses a granular permission system with 108 permissions across 22 categories. Every permission is listed, with its label and description, in the Permissions Reference.

docs.title: Permission Categories
docs.text: Category Permissions Description Signals read, write, delete, export, manage Signal Search and artifact data Graph - Nodes read, write, delete, export, manage Graph nodes Graph - Edges read, write, delete, export, manage Graph edges Graph read, write The whole graph surface (nodes and edges) Work Units read, write, delete, export, manage Work units (incidents) Observer work_definitions:*, observations:*, collections:read, collections:write Work Definitions, observations and work collections Reporter reports:read, reports:write, reports:generate, reports:export, frameworks:read, frameworks:write, frameworks:manage Reporter pages and compliance frameworks CyberGrid publications, subscriptions, jobs, library, queue, directory, manage Threat-intelligence sharing Settings settings:read, settings:write, settings:products:read, settings:products:write, settings:manage System and business settings, product catalog Administration users:read, users:write, roles:read, roles:write, admin User and role administration Health Dashboard health:read, health:manage, metrics:read, metrics:export System health and metrics AI Assistant ai:read, ai:write, ai:manage, ai:export, mcp:manage, mcp:connect The in-app assistant, AI providers and MCP Conductor read, write, admin Conductor pipeline management Dashboards read, write, delete, manage Custom dashboards Playbooks read, write, delete, manage Playbooks Tasks read, write, delete, manage Tasks Responders read, write, delete, manage Responder jobs Platform Administration platform:read, platform:write, platform:manage, platform:conductor:admin, platform:users:admin, platform:switch Cross-tenant administration Auditor read, write, delete, execute, manage Auditor findings, runs and connectors Certifications read, write Certify packages Chat read, write, manage, chat:ai Chat rooms Attachments read, write, delete, manage File attachments

docs.title: Permission Hierarchy
docs.text:
admin → (all permissions)
resource:manage → resource:* (write, read, delete, export, ...)
resource:write → resource:read
  • admin grants every permission in every category.
  • {resource}:manage grants every {resource}:* permission. mcp:manage grants mcp:connect.
  • {resource}:write grants {resource}:read.

The platform-administrator flag and platform:manage do not grant mcp:connect.

docs.title: Service-Level Rules
docs.text:
• A route that requires a permission answers 403 when the caller lacks it.
  • The admin permission (label Administrator) gates user and role administration. users:write, roles:read and roles:write are reserved for it.
  • The api reads permissions from the user's session token, which is issued at sign-in. A role change reaches a user at their next sign-in, and a cached decision can last up to 5 more minutes. MCP connections read the user's roles on every request. See When role changes apply.

docs.title: Permissions that changed in 1.2.0
docs.text: Permission Change mcp:connect (Connect MCP) New. Needed to connect an MCP client, create personal MCP keys and approve app sign-ins mcp:manage (Manage MCP) Sets the organization's MCP mode and manages every MCP key and connected app in it. It can no longer create organization-wide keys, which are retired ai:read, ai:write Now gate the in-app AI assistant. Every built-in role holds both, and every custom role that existed at the upgrade was given both once dashboards:write Now needed to create, update, delete and clone a dashboard. Marking a favorite still needs only dashboards:read signals:read, signals:manage Now checked on classification rules and enrichment settings frameworks:read, frameworks:write Now checked on the compliance frameworks API CyberGrid permissions Now checked on every CyberGrid route

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Roles define what users can access in WitFoo Analytics. A user can hold one or more roles, and holds the permissions of all of them together.

docs.title: Built-in Roles
docs.text:
WitFoo Analytics 1.2.0 ships 9 built-in roles. They cannot be edited or deleted.

Role Description Key Permissions Admin Full system access - all permissions admin (every permission) Analyst Read-only access to all data, plus the AI chat assistant Read access to signals, the graph, work units, Observer, reports, frameworks, Auditor, Certifications and CyberGrid; the AI assistant ReadOnly Read-only access to all data, plus the AI chat assistant The same as Analyst, without Auditor and Certifications Report Viewer View and export reports, plus the AI chat assistant Read and export reports; read frameworks, Auditor and Certifications; the AI assistant Report Admin Full reporter module administration Reports, frameworks, Certifications, business settings and the product catalog; read Auditor; the AI assistant CyberGrid Viewer View CyberGrid resources, plus the AI chat assistant Read CyberGrid publications, subscriptions, queue and directory; the AI assistant CyberGrid Admin Full CyberGrid administration cybergrid:manage; the AI assistant Framework Manager Compliance framework administration Frameworks, read reports, business settings; the AI assistant Platform Admin Cross-tenant platform administrator with full platform management capabilities admin and every platform: permission

These descriptions are the ones 1.2.0 seeds for new installs and new tenants. An appliance installed earlier keeps the descriptions it already has. The full permission matrix is in the Roles Reference.

docs.title: Permission Inclusion Rules
docs.text:
• The admin permission grants every other permission.
  • {resource}:manage grants every {resource}:* permission, so mcp:manage grants mcp:connect.
  • {resource}:write grants {resource}:read.

The platform-administrator flag and platform:manage do not grant mcp:connect.

docs.title: MCP access
docs.text: No built-in role is seeded with Connect MCP (mcp:connect). Admin and Platform Admin can connect an MCP client because they hold admin, and so can any role that holds Manage MCP (mcp:manage). To let anyone else connect an AI client, give them a custom role that holds mcp:connect. Each tool still needs its own permission. See MCP Authentication.

docs.title: Custom Roles
docs.text:
1. Open Settings > Role Management (the gear icon in the page header).
  2. Click Create Role.
  3. Enter a role name and, optionally, a description.
  4. Select permissions from the list.
  5. Click Save.

Role Management opens only for users who hold the admin permission (label Administrator). It marks Write Users, Read Roles and Write Roles as reserved for that permission.

docs.title: What custom roles need in 1.2.0
docs.text:
Some actions now check a permission they did not check before. If your administrators or analysts use custom roles, check these:

Action Permission the role needs The setup wizard's AI step Manage AI (ai:manage) together with Manage Settings (settings:manage) The setup wizard's DNS step Manage Signals (signals:manage) together with settings:manage The setup wizard's frameworks step Write Frameworks (frameworks:write) together with settings:manage The setup wizard's CyberGrid step Manage CyberGrid (cybergrid:manage) together with settings:manage Create, update, delete or clone a dashboard Write Dashboards (dashboards:write). Marking a dashboard as a favorite still needs only Read Dashboards See a dashboard widget's data The read permission of the widget's data: Work Units read for Work Units widgets, Signals read for artifact widgets, any of Graph, Nodes or Edges read for node and edge widgets, Reports read for report widgets, Frameworks read or Reports read for framework widgets, Health read for health widgets Use the in-app AI assistant Read AI (ai:read) to read your sessions, Write AI (ai:write) to send messages and start, rename or delete sessions Connect an MCP client Connect MCP (mcp:connect) Read classification rules signals:read or settings:manage. Changing them needs signals:manage or settings:manage Read enrichment settings signals:read. Changing them needs signals:manage Read compliance frameworks frameworks:read or reports:read. Changing them needs frameworks:write

A user without a widget's read permission sees "You do not have access to this widget's data." on that widget. The dashboard's other widgets are unaffected.

When an appliance first starts 1.2.0, every custom role that exists at that moment receives Read AI and Write AI once. Removing them afterwards sticks. Custom roles created later do not get them automatically.

docs.title: When role changes apply
docs.text:
• A permission change reaches a user at their next sign-in, or when an API client refreshes its token.
  • After that, the server may reuse an earlier allow or deny decision for up to 5 minutes.
  • MCP connections read the user's roles on every request, so they see a change on the next request.
  • A session that began before a role gained a permission does not carry it. The user signs in again to get it.

docs.title: Role Assignment
docs.text: Assign roles to a user from Settings > User Management: open the user's row actions and choose Assign Roles.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Manage user accounts for your WitFoo Analytics deployment. Open Settings > User Management (the gear icon in the page header).

User Management opens only for users who hold the admin permission (label Administrator), such as the built-in Admin and Platform Admin roles.

docs.title: User Properties
docs.text: Field Description Username Account name Email Sign-in address (unique) Name First and last name Roles Assigned roles; the user holds the permissions of all of them Status Active or disabled Last Login Most recent sign-in

docs.title: Creating Users
docs.text:
1. Open Settings > User Management.
  2. Click Create User.
  3. Enter the username, email, first and last name, and a password.
  4. Select one or more roles.
  5. Click Save.

docs.title: Email addresses
docs.text:
An email address typed for an account must be one plain address. This applies when an administrator creates or updates a user, at registration, at first-administrator setup and at tenant provisioning. These are refused with a clear message:

  • a comment or display name wrapped in extra text
  • two addresses
  • a trailing comma or semicolon
  • a second @
  • an embedded space or tab
  • a mailto: prefix
  • an IPv6-literal domain
  • a DOMAIN\user form

A pasted mailbox of the form Name <user@example.com> is still reduced to the address. Existing accounts keep signing in and editing as before.

docs.title: Editing Users
docs.text:
Click a user row to edit. You can change:

  • First and last name, and email
  • Assigned roles (Assign Roles)
  • The password (Reset Password)

A user's status is not changed by an edit. Use Disable or Enable instead.

docs.title: Disabling and Enabling Users
docs.text:
Users are disabled, not deleted. In 1.2.0, Delete is replaced by Disable, and there is no way to delete a user permanently.

  • Disable keeps the account and its data. A disabled user cannot sign in.
  • Enable lets a disabled user sign in again.
  • You cannot disable or enable your own account. The page says "You cannot disable your own account. Ask another administrator." Another administrator must do it.

Confirmation dialogs with a red confirm button, such as Disable, do not run on Enter. Click the confirm button.

docs.title: What a disable ends
docs.text:
Disabling a user, or suspending or deleting a tenant, ends that user's existing sessions:

  • requests are refused within seconds
  • open live connections (Conductor, the graph and event streams, and idle MCP connections) close within a minute

Resetting or changing a user's password ends their sessions in the same way.

docs.title: MCP keys
docs.text:
• Disabling a user revokes their personal MCP keys.
  • Enable revokes any of the user's remaining keys first. If it cannot, the user is not enabled and the page asks you to try again. Keys are never restored: the user creates new ones.
  • Resetting or changing a password makes the user's personal MCP keys stop working. The keys are not revoked, so the user's key card keeps listing them as Active until they expire or are revoked.

docs.title: Platform administrator accounts
docs.text: Only a platform administrator can edit, disable, enable, re-role or reset the password of an account that carries the platform-administrator flag or holds a role with a platform: permission. Anyone else is refused, and the page says "Only a platform administrator can change this user's status."

docs.title: Signed out at upgrade
docs.text: Upgrading to 1.2.0 signs every user out once. Users sign in again.

docs.title: Self-registration
docs.text: Public self-registration is off by default. When an operator turns it on, accounts are created inactive, and an administrator must use Enable before the person can sign in. See Authentication.

docs.title: Default Admin Account
docs.text:
Field Value Email admin@witfoo.com Password F00theN0ise!

Change Default Password

Change the default admin password immediately after first login.

On a WFA-managed appliance where this account still has the default password, WFA 2.5.1 and later may set it from the Admin Account step of wfa configure. See Upgrading to 1.2.0.

The default platform user is created only when the users table is empty. Restarting the database leaves existing users as they are.

docs.title: Locked out?
docs.text:
If nobody can sign in — a forgotten password, a mistyped email at setup, or a deactivated account — reset the initial admin account from the appliance command line:

sudo wfa user-reset

It shows the existing account, optionally changes the login email, and sets a new password. The change takes effect at the next login with no service restart. Run it on an Analytics appliance (aio, aio-conductor, processing, or data); see wfa user-reset for the full reference.

docs.title: Conductor UI and Console UI
docs.text:
The Conductor UI and the Console UI manage their own accounts, with their own rules:

  • Conductor UI: saving a user as Inactive deactivates the account and ends its sessions. Only a Superuser can give an account the Administrator or Superuser role, or deactivate an Administrator or Superuser account. No one can deactivate their own account. See Conductor UI users.
  • Console UI: the Users page still offers Delete. Only a Superuser can give an account the Org Admin or Superuser role, or delete an Org Admin or Superuser account. No one can delete their own account.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: System-wide configuration for WitFoo Analytics.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Open Settings (the gear icon in the page header) > General Settings. The settings pages are listed down the left side: System Settings, Incident Naming, Authentication, Notifications, Notification Rules, Certificates, Branding, Business Metrics, Frameworks, AI Setup and Onboarding Wizard.

The API behind these pages needs settings:read to read a setting and settings:manage to change it. Some pages check more: AI Setup needs ai:manage, and changing which frameworks are enabled needs frameworks:write.

docs.title: Business Metrics
docs.text: Configure financial and operational metrics used by the Reporter module. Saving changes only the figures you send: per-product costs and the language of AI responses are kept.

docs.title: Frameworks
docs.text: Enable compliance frameworks and set the primary framework.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Configure LDAP, SAML, and local authentication settings. SAML and LDAP settings are saved only on this page.

docs.title: SAML SSO
docs.text: Step-by-step guide for enabling SAML 2.0 SSO with Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and other IdPs.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Set up email, Slack, and webhook notification channels.

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text: Manage TLS certificates for HTTPS and internal service communication.

docs.title: AI Setup
docs.text: Configure AI providers, routing, the AI profile and response automation, and MCP. The MCP sections of this page (MCP Authentication, MCP Server Settings and the relay card) are described in MCP Configuration.

docs.title: How the settings pages behave
docs.text:
• Read failures are shown. When a page cannot read its settings, it shows an error, a dash or a notice instead of default values or zeros. System Settings and AI Setup offer Retry and keep Save disabled until a retry succeeds. Business Metrics shows an error with Retry, and no Save, until the figures can be read.
  • Confirmation dialogs do not run on Enter. A dialog with a red confirm button (Delete, Disable, Remove, Reset, Reboot Now and similar) does not submit on Enter, even while Cancel has focus. Click the confirm button to run the action.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Configure authentication methods for WitFoo Analytics. Open Settings (the gear icon in the page header) > General Settings > Authentication. Requires the settings:manage permission.

SAML and LDAP settings are saved and read only on this page. The general system settings API (PUT /api/v1/settings) neither saves nor returns them.

Encryption Required

LDAP bind passwords and SAML private keys are encrypted at rest with XChaCha20-Poly1305, under a per-organization key derived from AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Values written by releases before the cipher change were sealed with AES-256-GCM and are still read. On a WFA-managed appliance WFA supplies the key; do not edit it. On Docker Compose or a standalone stack the key is required from 1.2.0: see Upgrading to 1.2.0.

docs.title: Local Authentication
docs.text:
Default method using username/password stored in Cassandra with bcrypt hashing. No external dependencies required.

  • Users are created and managed within the WitFoo Admin panel
  • Passwords must meet minimum complexity requirements
  • Supports password reset via admin action

docs.title: LDAP
docs.text:
Connect to an LDAP directory (Active Directory, OpenLDAP) for centralized authentication.

Setting Description Server URL LDAP server address (ldap:// or ldaps://) Bind DN Distinguished name for LDAP queries Bind Password Password for the bind account Search Base Base DN for user searches User Filter LDAP filter for matching users (e.g., (uid=%s))

Secure LDAP

Use ldaps:// with a valid TLS certificate for production deployments. WitFoo uses ldap.DialURL() which supports TLS configuration.

docs.title: SAML
docs.text: SAML 2.0 single sign-on integration for enterprise identity providers.

docs.title: Core Settings
docs.text: Setting Description Entity ID Service provider entity ID (unique identifier for WitFoo) SSO URL Identity provider SSO endpoint SLO URL Identity provider Single Logout endpoint (optional) Certificate IdP X.509 certificate for signature validation SP Private Key Service provider private key (for signed requests) SP Certificate Service provider certificate (for signed requests) Attribute Mapping Map SAML attributes to WitFoo user fields (email, name, role)

docs.title: SAML Provider Wizard
docs.text: The SAML configuration wizard guides administrators through a 7-step setup process with provider-specific presets that pre-populate common settings.

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text:
Provider Pre-populated Settings Azure AD / Entra ID Entity ID format, claim names (http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/...), logout URL pattern Okta SSO URL pattern, attribute mapping (firstName, lastName, email), name ID format OneLogin Issuer URL format, SLO endpoint, certificate location guidance PingIdentity Connection URL pattern, attribute contract mappings Manual No defaults -- full manual configuration for any SAML 2.0 IdP

Each provider preset reduces configuration to entering your organization-specific values (tenant ID, app ID, etc.) while the wizard handles protocol-level defaults.

docs.title: Wizard Steps
docs.text:
1. Select Provider -- Choose your identity provider or Manual
  2. IdP Configuration -- Enter SSO URL, Entity ID, and IdP certificate
  3. SP Configuration -- Configure service provider settings (auto-generated or manual)
  4. Attribute Mapping -- Map SAML attributes to WitFoo user fields
  5. Authentication Mode -- Choose SAML-only or Mixed mode
  6. Key Pair -- Generate or upload SP signing key pair
  7. Review & Test -- Validate configuration before saving

docs.title: Authentication Modes
docs.text:
Mode Value Description SAML Only saml All users authenticate via the identity provider. Local login is hidden. Mixed (SAML + Local) mixed_saml SAML is primary, but local authentication remains available as a fallback. Users see both login options.

Mixed Mode Recommendation

Use mixed_saml mode during initial SAML deployment. This ensures administrators can still log in with local credentials if SAML configuration issues arise.

docs.title: SP Key Pair Generation
docs.text:
WitFoo can automatically generate a service provider key pair for SAML request signing:

  • Algorithm: RSA 2048-bit
  • Output: PEM-encoded private key and self-signed X.509 certificate
  • Endpoint: POST /api/v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/generate-keypair (the request names the entity_id)
  • Usage: The generated key pair is used to sign SAML authentication requests sent to the IdP

The generated certificate can be uploaded to your identity provider's service provider configuration.

docs.title: IdP Metadata Fetch
docs.text:
If your identity provider publishes a metadata URL, WitFoo can automatically fetch and parse it:

  • Endpoint: POST /api/v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/fetch-metadata
  • Input: IdP metadata URL
  • Output: Extracted SSO URL, SLO URL, and X.509 certificate

This eliminates manual copy-paste of IdP configuration values.

docs.title: SAML Configuration Test
docs.text:
Before saving, validate your SAML configuration using the built-in test endpoint. The test performs 4 checks:

Check Description certificate_valid The IdP certificate is PEM, parses as X.509, and has not expired key_pair_match The SP private key matches the SP certificate (or the IdP certificate when no SP certificate is given) metadata_fetchable The IdP metadata URL answers 200; skipped when no metadata URL is set sp_build_successful A service provider can be built from the configuration
  • Endpoint: POST /api/v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/test
  • Response: an overall status (success, partial or failed) and a pass/fail result with a message for each check

Test Before Save

Always run the SAML configuration test before saving. A misconfigured SAML setup can lock all users out of the system if running in SAML-only mode.

docs.title: SAML Auth Fallback
docs.text:
WitFoo includes automatic redirect loop detection to prevent SAML misconfigurations from locking users out.

How it works:

  1. On each failed SAML login attempt, a saml_redirect_count cookie is incremented (MaxAge: 60 seconds)
  2. After 3 failed redirects within 60 seconds, the system detects a loop
  3. The user is redirected to the login page with ?auth_fallback=true
  4. When auth_fallback=true is present, the local authentication form is displayed regardless of the SAML-only setting

This fallback mechanism is implemented consistently across all three UI backends (analytics UI, conductor-ui, console-ui).

Fallback URL

If SAML is completely broken, navigate directly to:

https://your-instance/ui/login?auth_fallback=true

This forces the local login form to appear, allowing administrators to log in and fix the SAML configuration.

docs.title: Common SAML Errors
docs.text:
Error Cause Solution Redirect loop IdP rejecting authentication requests Check IdP certificate expiry; verify Entity ID matches IdP configuration Invalid signature Certificate mismatch Re-download IdP certificate; ensure no whitespace corruption in PEM Attribute not found Missing attribute mapping Verify IdP sends required attributes (email at minimum); check claim URIs Clock skew Server time difference > 5 minutes Synchronize NTP on both WitFoo and IdP servers SP key pair mismatch Private key doesn't match certificate Regenerate the key pair using the built-in generator "SAML SSO is not configured properly. Contact your administrator." The login flow could not load an enabled SAML config for the appliance's organization. Most often: SAML is saved but disabled, the SP secret was overwritten by the redaction placeholder on a re-save, or the appliance predates the org-aware SSO-login resolution Confirm SAML is enabled (auth mode saml or mixed_saml) and saved; re-save without re-typing the secrets (the ***REDACTED*** placeholder is preserved server-side); run the diagnostic at the bottom of the Authentication page; ensure the appliance is on a build with org-aware SSO login (see the note below) Conductor SSO wizard "Invalid request body" at Test Connection A freshly-built wizard config sent empty server-managed timestamps (created_at/updated_at) the backend could not parse Update conductor to a build where the SAML config tolerates empty timestamps, then re-run the wizard

SSO login binds to the appliance's primary organization

The diagnostic validates the SAML config for the signed-in administrator's organization, while the unauthenticated "Sign in with SSO" button resolves the appliance's primary organization (WF_ORG_ID). On a single-tenant appliance these are the same, so configure SAML while signed in as an administrator of the primary organization. If the diagnostic passes but SSO login reports "not configured", the appliance likely predates the org-aware login resolution — update to the latest build.

docs.title: Recovering from Lockout
docs.text:
If all users are locked out due to SAML misconfiguration:

  1. Access the login page with ?auth_fallback=true parameter
  2. Log in with a local administrator account
  3. Open Settings > General Settings > Authentication
  4. Switch to mixed_saml mode or fix the SAML configuration
  5. Run the configuration test to validate before saving

docs.title: Platform administrators and single sign-on
docs.text:
From 1.2.0, an organization's SAML identity provider and LDAP directory cannot sign in a platform administrator by default. A platform administrator is an account with the platform-administrator flag, or with a role that holds a platform: permission, such as the built-in Platform Admin role. A refused SAML sign-in returns to the login page with "Your account cannot sign in right now. Contact your administrator." Local password sign-in is not affected.

The appliance operator can exempt one organization, normally their own, with a file on the node that runs analytics-api-svc:

Setting Value File /witfoo/configs/operator-identity-org Owner and mode root:root, 0644 Content One organization ID and nothing else Read Once, when analytics-api-svc starts

To set it, as root on that node:

printf '%s\n' <org-id> > /witfoo/configs/operator-identity-org
chown root:root /witfoo/configs/operator-identity-org && chmod 0644 /witfoo/configs/operator-identity-org
docker restart analytics-api-svc
docker logs --since 5m analytics-api-svc 2>&1 | grep 'Operator identity organization'

When the file is valid, the api logs Operator identity organization in force with the organization's ID. A file it cannot use exempts nothing and logs [ERROR] /configs/operator-identity-org cannot be used. To remove the exemption, delete the file and restart analytics-api-svc.

What the exemption allows:

  • SAML: the organization's identity provider can sign in its platform administrators, whatever the organization ID is.
  • LDAP: only when the organization ID equals the first label of the account's mail domain. For example, holder@example.com signs in to the organization example. For any other organization ID, use SAML for these accounts.
  • While the file names an organization, only a platform administrator can change that organization's SAML or LDAP settings. Anyone else is refused with 403 platform_admin_required.

docs.title: When a person has no account
docs.text: The analytics server does not create accounts at the first SSO sign-in. A person who signs in through SAML and has no account here, or whose identity provider sends a different email address than the account holds, is told that an administrator must create the account first and that the address must match. Create the account under Settings > User Management with the same email address the identity provider sends.

docs.title: Public self-registration
docs.text:
Public self-registration is off by default. Two environment variables on the api control it:

Variable Default Description AUTH_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION_ENABLED false Turns on POST /api/v1/auth/register. It gives the same answer whether or not an account is created, and allows 10 requests an hour per client AUTH_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION_DOMAINS (empty) Comma-separated <email-domain>=<org_id> pairs, for example example.com=acme,corp.example.org=globex

How registration behaves in 1.2.0:

  • An account is created only when AUTH_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION_DOMAINS maps the address's domain to an organization. Domains are matched exactly, with no subdomain or wildcard match.
  • The organization a registration request names is ignored. The email domain chooses the organization.
  • Fail-closed: one malformed entry rejects the whole map. The api logs one [ERROR] naming the entry's position, and registration creates no account until the map is fixed.
  • The address is not verified, so every account created this way is inactive. An administrator must enable it (Settings > User Management > Enable) before the person can sign in.

docs.title: Business Metrics
docs.text: Configure financial and operational parameters used by the Reporter module for cost/savings analysis.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Default Description Annual Revenue $0 Organization's annual revenue Annual Security Spend $0 Total security budget FTE Count 3 Security team headcount Investigation Time 1.5 hours Average investigation time per incident Restore Time 0.75 hours Average remediation time per incident FTE Hourly Rate $75 Average analyst hourly rate

docs.title: Product Costs
docs.text:
Configure annual costs for each security product. Products appear in the Tool Effectiveness report.

  1. Click Add Product
  2. Enter product name and annual cost
  3. Default cost: $100,000 if not specified

docs.title: How Settings Are Used
docs.text:
• FTE Needed = (Incidents * (Investigation + Restore Time)) / 2,080 hours
  • Security Spend % = Annual Security Spend / Annual Revenue * 100
  • Cost per Incident = (Personnel + Product Costs) / Total Incidents

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Navigate to Admin > Settings > Business Metrics. Requires settings:manage permission.

Financial Defaults

Financial fields intentionally default to zero. The system does not auto-fill these values because organizations may set them to zero deliberately.

docs.title: Certificates
docs.text: Manage TLS certificates for HTTPS access and internal service communication.

docs.title: Upload Certificate
docs.text:
1. Open Settings (the gear icon in the page header) > General Settings > Certificates
  2. Click Upload Certificate
  3. Provide the certificate file (PEM format) and private key
  4. Click Save

docs.title: Certificate Validation
docs.text:
Uploaded certificates are validated before acceptance:

  • X.509 format verification
  • Key pair matching (certificate + private key)
  • Expiration date check

docs.title: Hot-Reload
docs.text: The reverse proxy supports certificate hot-reload. When a new certificate is uploaded, it takes effect immediately without restarting services. This uses the tls.Config.GetCertificate callback pattern.

docs.title: Self-Signed Certificates
docs.text: For development and testing, WitFoo Analytics generates a self-signed certificate on first boot. Replace it with a trusted certificate for production use.

docs.title: Certificate Storage
docs.text:
• Certificates are stored in Cassandra
  • Private keys are encrypted at rest with XChaCha20-Poly1305, under a per-organization key derived from AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY (values written before the cipher change were sealed with AES-256-GCM and are still read)
  • File permissions: private keys 0600, certificates 0644

Set one framework as Primary for default selection in compliance views:

  2. The primary framework is auto-selected in Reporter compliance views

docs.title: Localization
docs.text: WitFoo Analytics supports multiple languages for the user interface, notifications, and AI-generated content.

docs.title: Supported Locales
docs.text:
Locale Code Language Direction Status en English LTR Default es Spanish (Español) LTR Complete fr French (Français) LTR Complete de German (Deutsch) LTR Complete ja Japanese (日本語) LTR Complete ar Arabic (العربية) RTL Complete mi Te Reo Māori LTR Complete

All 7 locales have consistent translation keys with matching parameter placeholders, validated by automated tests.

docs.title: Changing Your Locale
docs.text:
Users can change their display language from the profile menu:

  1. Click your user avatar in the top-right corner
  2. Select Profile
  3. Under Language, choose your preferred locale from the dropdown
  4. The page reloads automatically with the selected language applied

The locale preference is stored per user and persists across sessions.

docs.title: AI Language Awareness
docs.text: WitFoo's AI features automatically respond in the user's selected locale:

docs.title: Interactive Features
docs.text:
When a user interacts with AI-powered features (summaries, chat), the frontend passes the user's current locale to the backend. The AI system appends a language instruction to the end of its system prompt, ensuring responses are generated in the appropriate language.

  • AI Summaries: Work unit and incident summaries are generated in the requesting user's locale
  • AI Chat: Chat responses match the user's display language
  • English default: When the locale is English, no additional language instruction is added (English is the base language for all prompts)

docs.title: Background AI Tasks
docs.text:
For automated AI tasks that run without a user session (such as playbook analysis), the system uses the organization's Default Locale setting:

  1. Navigate to Admin > Settings > Business Metrics
  2. Set the Default Locale field to the preferred language for background AI output
  3. All automated playbook analyses and AI-generated reports will use this locale

Default Locale Scope

The Default Locale setting in Business Metrics applies only to background AI tasks (e.g., automated playbook analysis). Interactive AI features always use the individual user's locale preference.

docs.title: Translation Coverage
docs.text:
All user-facing strings in the application are internationalized, including:

  • Navigation menus and page titles
  • Form labels, buttons, and validation messages
  • Notification titles and descriptions
  • Signal search facets and filter labels
  • CyberGrid publications, subscriptions, and modals
  • Reporter chart titles and data labels
  • Admin settings pages
  • Error messages and status indicators

Reporting Translation Issues

If you encounter untranslated text or incorrect translations, report the issue through the WitFoo support channel. Include the locale, the page where the issue appears, and the text in question.

docs.title: Email (SMTP)

docs.title: Testing Channels
docs.text: Click Test on any channel to send a test notification and verify connectivity.

docs.title: Notification Rules
docs.text:
Create rules that trigger notifications on specific events:

  • incident.created — New incident detected
  • incident.status_changed — Incident status updated
  • incident.severity_changed — Severity escalation/de-escalation
  • incident.assigned — Incident assigned to analyst
  • incident.note_added — Note added to incident

docs.title: Cooldown
docs.text: Each rule has a cooldown period (default: 15 minutes) preventing duplicate notifications for the same condition.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Open Settings (the gear icon in the page header) > General Settings > Notifications. Rules are on the Notification Rules page, listed beside it. Requires the settings:manage permission.

Encryption

Notification-channel configurations are encrypted at rest with XChaCha20-Poly1305, under a per-organization key derived from AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY. On a WFA-managed appliance WFA supplies the key. On Docker Compose or a standalone stack the key is required: see Upgrading to 1.2.0.

Rule-driven notifications in 1.2.0

Before 1.2.0, rule-driven notifications (a work unit created or its status changed) could not open their channel, so they were never delivered and wrote no history. 1.2.0 fixes this: after the upgrade, rules that never delivered start delivering, beginning with the first matching event. The NOTIFICATION_ENCRYPTION_KEY setting and its startup warning are removed; channels use AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

docs.title: Microsoft Sentinel
docs.text: Integrate WitFoo Analytics with Microsoft Sentinel to ingest security incidents and alerts from your Azure environment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Microsoft Sentinel connector pulls security incidents from your Sentinel workspace via the Azure Management REST API. Incidents are imported as work units in WitFoo Analytics, enabling correlation with data from other security tools.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Active Azure subscription with Microsoft Sentinel enabled
  • Azure App Registration with appropriate API permissions
  • Sentinel workspace deployed in a resource group
  • Network connectivity from WitFoo to https://management.azure.com

docs.title: Azure App Registration
docs.text:
Create an app registration in Azure AD (Entra ID) to authorize WitFoo API access.

  1. Navigate to Azure Portal > App registrations > New registration
  2. Name: WitFoo Analytics Integration
  3. Supported account types: Single tenant
  4. Register the application
  5. Note the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID
  6. Under Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret and note the value

docs.title: Required API Permissions
docs.text:
Permission Type Description SecurityIncident.Read.All Application Read security incidents from Sentinel

Admin Consent

An Azure AD administrator must grant admin consent for application permissions after they are added.

docs.title: Role Assignment
docs.text:
The app registration also needs the Microsoft Sentinel Reader role on the Sentinel workspace:

  1. Navigate to your Sentinel workspace > Access control (IAM)
  2. Add role assignment: Microsoft Sentinel Reader
  3. Assign to the app registration created above

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Navigate to Admin > Settings > Connectors > Microsoft Sentinel in WitFoo Analytics.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Description Example Tenant ID Azure AD directory (tenant) ID a1b2c3d4-e5f6-... Client ID Application (client) ID from app registration f6e5d4c3-b2a1-... Client Secret Client secret value (encrypted at rest) *** Subscription ID Azure subscription containing the Sentinel workspace 12345678-abcd-... Resource Group Resource group name where Sentinel is deployed rg-security-prod Workspace Name Log Analytics workspace name for Sentinel sentinel-workspace

Secret Rotation

Azure client secrets expire. Set a reminder to rotate the secret before expiry and update the value in WitFoo settings.

docs.title: Connection Testing
docs.text:
After entering all configuration values, use the Test Connection button to validate:

  1. Authentication -- Confirms the client credentials can obtain an OAuth2 token from Azure AD
  2. Workspace Access -- Verifies the app registration can reach the specified Sentinel workspace
  3. Incident Read -- Attempts to list recent incidents to confirm permissions

A successful test returns a green status indicator. If the test fails, review the error message for guidance on which setting needs correction.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
graph LR
    Sentinel[Microsoft Sentinel] -->|REST API| WitFoo[WitFoo Analytics]
    WitFoo --> WU[Work Units]
    WitFoo --> Correlation[Cross-tool Correlation]

Incidents are polled at a configurable interval (default: 5 minutes). Each Sentinel incident maps to a WitFoo work unit with:

  • Severity mapping (High/Medium/Low/Informational)
  • Incident timeline and alerts
  • Entity extraction (IPs, users, hosts)
  • Status synchronization

docs.title: AI & MCP
docs.text: WitFoo Analytics includes an in-app AI assistant and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector that lets AI clients work with your appliance's data.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configure AI providers, models, and API keys.

docs.title: Chat Interface
docs.text: Use the AI chat panel for security analysis assistance.

docs.title: MCP Connector
docs.text: Connect AI clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor to your appliance.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The AI assistant helps analysts with:

  • Incident investigation and triage guidance
  • Artifact analysis and enrichment interpretation
  • Report generation and summary
  • Compliance mapping assistance

docs.title: MCP
docs.text:
AI clients connect to the appliance over MCP. Every connection acts as a real user, with that user's live permissions, and an administrator can see and end any of them.

  • Users connect with a personal MCP key they create under Profile > Security > MCP connections.
  • Apps can sign in through the appliance's own authorization server. See App sign-in (OAuth 2.1).
  • An optional relay, off until an operator turns it on, reaches the appliance's MCP endpoint without an inbound port.
  • MCP is included with Analytics Pro, Analytics Max and Reporter Pro. See Licensing.

Connections by personal key, by app sign-in and over HTTP /mcp are off by default. See MCP Configuration and the tool reference.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permission Name Access ai:read Read AI View AI features and read chat assistant sessions ai:write Write AI Send messages; start, rename and delete chat sessions ai:manage Manage AI Configure AI providers and their API keys, and open the AI Setup page ai:export Export AI Export chat history and conversations mcp:connect Connect MCP Create, rotate and revoke your own personal MCP keys, approve and revoke the apps that connect as you, and open an MCP session that runs with your own permissions mcp:manage Manage MCP Set the organization's MCP mode, list and revoke any MCP key in the organization, and manage app sign-in clients and connected apps
  • Every built-in role holds ai:read and ai:write, directly or through Administrator.
  • A user with Read AI but not Write AI can open their chat sessions but cannot send or change anything.
  • No built-in role is seeded with mcp:connect. Admin and Platform Admin hold it through Administrator, and any role that holds mcp:manage holds it too. Grant it to anyone else through a custom role.
  • The AI Setup page opens for ai:manage. Its MCP Authentication section is shown to holders of mcp:manage, so an administrator who manages MCP in the UI needs both.

Custom roles and the assistant at upgrade

On the first start of 1.2.0, existing custom roles receive ai:read and ai:write once. Removing them afterwards sticks. Custom roles created later do not get them automatically.

Permission changes reach a user at their next sign-in, and the server may reuse a decision for up to 5 minutes after that. MCP connections read a user's roles on every request and see a change on the next one.

See Permissions for the full catalog.

docs.title: Chat Interface
docs.text: The AI chat panel provides conversational access to AI-powered security analysis within WitFoo Analytics.

docs.title: Accessing Chat
docs.text:
• Chat Panel — Click the chat icon in the page header, or press Ctrl+/ (Cmd+/ on a Mac), to open the side panel
  • Chat Page — Open the dedicated chat page for full-screen conversations

The panel's AI tab appears when the user holds ai:read and at least one AI provider is enabled. See AI Configuration.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Context-aware — The AI has access to your current page context (incidents, nodes, reports)
  • Multi-session — Maintain multiple chat sessions for different investigations
  • Tool-augmented — The AI can look up data through a set of read-only tools, with your own permissions
  • History — Chat sessions are kept and can be resumed

docs.title: Chat Panel
docs.text:
The chat panel slides in from the right side of the screen (400px wide). It can be maximized, or detached into its own window.

The panel can also hold the team chat tabs, Channels and Direct Message, for users who hold a chat permission.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
Shortcut Action Ctrl+/ Open the panel on the AI tab, or close it Ctrl+Shift+C Open the panel on the Channels tab, or close it

On a Mac, use Cmd in place of Ctrl.

docs.title: Create a Session
docs.text: Click New chat to start a fresh conversation. Each session maintains its own context and history.

docs.title: Resume a Session
docs.text: Click any session in the session list to resume the conversation.

docs.title: Rename or Delete a Session
docs.text: Use the rename and delete controls on a session. Deleting a session removes it and its message history.

docs.title: How long history is kept
docs.text:
Chat history is kept for 90 days.

Known limitation

A chat session still in use after its 90th day can show as a blank entry in the session list, with its title and creation time gone.

docs.title: Tools the assistant uses
docs.text:
The assistant looks up data with five read-only tools: search_nodes, search_artifacts, search_observations, get_audit_remediation and search_directory. Each call is checked against your own permissions, so the assistant can only read what you can read. See In-app AI assistant.

The in-app assistant does not use an MCP connection, so it does not need mcp:connect.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Action Required Permission Open your chat sessions and read them ai:read Send a message, or start, rename or delete a session ai:write

A user with ai:read but not ai:write can open their sessions but cannot send or change anything. Every built-in role holds both.

docs.title: Opening AI Setup

docs.title: Provider Setup
docs.text: The AI Providers section lists the configured providers. Click Add Provider to add one. Each row can be enabled, disabled, edited or deleted.

Project ID IBM watsonx.ai only Region IBM watsonx.ai only. Leave it blank for us-south. Base URL Ollama only. Default: http://localhost:11434 Max Tokens Maximum response length (256 to 100,000) Temperature Response creativity (0 to 2)

Stored URLs are shown without credentials

The settings pages show a configuration's base URL without its user information, query or fragment. To remove a credential from a stored URL, clear the field, save, and enter the URL again.

docs.title: Other sections
docs.text: AI Setup also holds the Model Profile, Response Jobs and Summaries settings.

docs.title: When a setting cannot be read
docs.text: When AI Setup cannot read a setting, it shows an error and a Retry instead of default values. Save stays disabled until a retry succeeds, so a failed read can never be saved over your settings.

docs.title: MCP Authentication
docs.text: The MCP Authentication section of AI Setup decides who can connect over MCP. It is shown to holders of mcp:manage. See MCP Configuration.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Action Required Permission Open AI Setup and change providers ai:manage Change the MCP mode and manage keys mcp:manage

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text: WitFoo Analytics lets AI clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor and Claude Code connect to your appliance over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and every connection acts as a real user with that user's permissions.

docs.title: What is MCP?
docs.text: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard for connecting AI clients to external data and tools. WitFoo's MCP server exposes 44 tools that an AI client can call during a conversation: 28 read-only tools and 16 that change state. See Tools for the full list.

docs.title: How MCP works in 1.2.0
docs.text:
• Every connection is a real user. An AI client connects with a credential that belongs to one user. It reaches only the tools, and the actions, that user's own permissions allow, and those permissions are checked live on every request.
  • Administrators see and end connections. An administrator can list and revoke every personal key and every connected app in the organization.
  • Off by default. Connections by personal key, by app sign-in and over HTTP /mcp are off until you turn them on. See Turning MCP On.
  • Air-gapped appliances are supported. The MCP server runs on the appliance itself and needs no outside service.

docs.title: Two transports
docs.text:
Transport Path Credentials accepted Streamable HTTP (opt-in) POST /mcp A personal MCP key or, when the organization's mode is app sign-in (oauth), an access token the appliance issued to an app WebSocket /ws/chat A personal MCP key, or a browser session

/ws/chat never accepts an app's access token, and /mcp never accepts a browser session.

docs.title: What changed since 1.1.x
docs.text:
Area 1.1.x 1.2.0 Credentials Optional org-wide wfmcp_ keys Personal keys (wfmcpu_) that each user creates, and app sign-in with OAuth 2.1. Org-wide keys are retired. Permissions Org-wide identity The connected user's own permissions, checked on every request. A new Connect MCP (mcp:connect) permission controls who may connect. Tools 51 tools listed 44 tools, each marked read-only or state-changing. Seven tools that always failed are removed. Licence Not licensed separately Included with Analytics Pro, Analytics Max and Reporter Pro Reaching the appliance Main listener only Main listener, an optional exposure listener on port 8444, or the optional AI-connector relay

Org-wide keys no longer work

Keys that start wfmcp_ stop authenticating after the upgrade. Each user creates a personal key instead. See Authentication & Permissions.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Check that your licence includes the MCP connector: Analytics Pro, Analytics Max or Reporter Pro. See MCP Licensing.
  2. For HTTP clients, turn on the HTTP transport on the appliance ("mcp_http_enabled": true in node.json, then restart WFA). See Turning MCP On.
  3. Choose who can connect: under Settings > General Settings > AI Setup > MCP Authentication, select Browser chat sessions and personal keys (or Browser chat sessions, personal keys and app sign-in) and click Save Authentication.
  4. Give each user who should connect the Connect MCP (mcp:connect) permission through a custom role. Administrators already hold it. See Authentication & Permissions.
  5. Each user creates a personal key under Profile > Security > MCP connections. See Personal MCP Keys.
  6. Add the appliance's /mcp address and the key to the AI client. See Connecting AI Clients & Marketplaces.

docs.title: Pages in this section
docs.text:
• Architecture: where the MCP server runs and the checks every request passes.
  • Turning MCP On: the organization mode, the HTTP transport switch and allowed origins.
  • Authentication & Permissions: the three kinds of credential, mcp:connect and mcp:manage, retired org-wide keys and revocation.
  • Personal MCP Keys: creating, using, rotating and revoking your own keys.
  • App Sign-in (OAuth 2.1): letting apps sign in through the appliance's own authorization server.
  • MCP Licensing: which licences include MCP and what a refusal looks like.
  • Exposure Listener (Port 8444): a separate listener for marketplace clients.
  • AI-Connector Relay: reaching the appliance through WitFoo without an inbound port.
  • Connecting AI Clients & Marketplaces: configuration for Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT and other clients.
  • Tools: the 44 tools and the permission each one needs.
  • Errors: the responses MCP clients can receive and what they mean.

docs.title: MCP Architecture
docs.text: The MCP server runs in the analytics dispatcher, behind the appliance's reverse proxy, and checks every request against the connected user's live permissions.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Container Role Reverse proxy analytics-reverse-proxy-svc Receives client connections on :443 (and on the optional exposure listener and relay tunnel), refuses keys sent in a URL, and forwards MCP traffic to the dispatcher Dispatcher analytics-dispatcher-svc Serves POST /mcp and /ws/chat, authenticates the credential, admits the request and authorizes each tool call Incident engine — Answers most tool calls. It checks its own route permission for each call. API — Hosts the self-service key routes, the administrator routes and the app sign-in endpoints

docs.title: How a request reaches the MCP server
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    client[AI client] -->|"HTTPS :443"| rp[Reverse proxy]
    client -->|"Port 8444 (optional)"| rp
    client -->|"Relay address (optional)"| relay[WitFoo relay]
    relay -->|"Outbound tunnel opened by the appliance"| rp
    rp -->|"/mcp, /ws/chat"| disp[Dispatcher MCP server]
    disp -->|"Tool calls"| ie[Incident engine]
  • The main listener (:443) serves the UI, the API and the WebSockets as well as /mcp.
  • The exposure listener on port 8444 is optional. It serves /mcp and the app sign-in endpoints and nothing else.
  • The AI-connector relay is optional. The appliance opens one outbound connection to WitFoo's relay, and requests to the relay address travel down it to the reverse proxy.

Every route applies the same authentication, admission and authorization.

docs.title: The three checks on every request
docs.text: door (per connection or HTTP request)  →  admission (per request)  →  authorization (per tool call)

docs.title: Door
docs.text:
The door reads the credential and identifies the user:

  • Personal key: the key's own record, its owner and its expiry.
  • Browser session: the session token.
  • App access token: its signed claims (user, organization, app, grant, scope, and when it was issued and expires). The check is by computation alone and reads no storage.

docs.title: Admission
docs.text:
Admission re-reads, with no cache, everything that can revoke access:

  1. The credential's own record. A key must be present, not revoked, not expired, with the same owner. An access token's grant must be present and not revoked, and the app must still be allowed.
  2. The organization's MCP mode: personal keys need Browser chat sessions and personal keys or Browser chat sessions, personal keys and app sign-in. Access tokens need app sign-in. Browser sessions work in every mode.
  3. The tenant is not suspended or deleted.
  4. The user exists, is active and belongs to the credential's organization.
  5. The credential was issued after the user's last password reset or deactivation.
  6. The user's roles, resolved in their home organization.
  7. The user holds mcp:connect.
  8. The appliance licence includes the MCP connector, or no licence has been learned yet. See MCP Licensing.

Admission runs on every request except ping and notifications/* on an open WebSocket. It runs for tools/list too. A transient database error denies that one request and does not close the connection.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Authorization checks the permission the tool needs, or, for the eight manage_* tools, the permission of the requested action, against the permissions admission just resolved. Anything ambiguous is denied. For an app approved with read access only (mcp:read), the user's permissions are narrowed to their :read permissions. See Tools for the permission each tool needs.

When a tool calls the incident engine, the dispatcher sends a short-lived token that carries only the one permission it just checked, and the incident engine checks it again where its route carries a permission.

docs.title: The HTTP transport is stateless
docs.text: POST /mcp holds no session between requests. It issues no Mcp-Session-Id header, and GET /mcp answers 405. Each request is authenticated and admitted on its own, so a change to a key, a grant, a user, a role or the organization's mode applies to the next request.

docs.title: The in-app assistant
docs.text: The product's own chat assistant does not use /ws/chat. It calls tools through a bridge in the API, and each tool call is authorized against the caller's own permissions by the same decision as an MCP tools/call. Reading chat sessions needs ai:read, and sending a message needs ai:write. See Tools.

docs.title: Upgrade order
docs.text:
Upgrade the incident engine and the dispatcher together

Upgrade the incident engine and the dispatcher together, or the incident engine first. While they run different versions, most MCP tool calls can fail with an unexpected status 401 error. See Upgrading to 1.2.0.

docs.title: Authentication & Permissions
docs.text: Every MCP connection runs as a user, with that user's live permissions, and an administrator can list and revoke the credentials that make those connections.

docs.title: Three kinds of credential
docs.text:
Credential Used by Accepted on Details Browser session The analytics UI in a signed-in browser /ws/chat See Browser sessions below Personal MCP key (wfmcpu_…) A developer tool or a desktop client that a user configures /mcp and /ws/chat See Personal MCP Keys App access token An app that the user approved through app sign-in /mcp only See App Sign-in (OAuth 2.1)

A personal key and an app connection are separate credentials. They are listed and revoked separately.

docs.title: Browser sessions
docs.text:
The browser session path on /ws/chat is kept, with four changes in 1.2.0:

  • The session token must carry the aud and exp claims. Tokens without them are refused, so a token issued before the upgrade does not work. Upgrading signs everyone out once anyway.
  • The token's own list of permissions is ignored. The session is admitted live, from the user's current roles.
  • The user must hold mcp:connect.
  • The session closes at the first 60-second check at or after the token expires. A request after expiry is refused at once.

docs.title: Who can connect: mcp:connect
docs.text:
Connect MCP (mcp:connect) is new in 1.2.0. A user can use MCP only while they hold it, and it is checked live on every request, so granting or removing it takes effect on the user's next call.

  • No built-in role is seeded with it. Admin and Platform Admin hold it through admin, which grants every permission.
  • mcp:manage implies it. A custom role that holds mcp:manage can connect too, by the rule that {resource}:manage grants every {resource}:* permission.
  • The platform-administrator flag and platform:manage do not grant it.
  • Everyone else needs a custom role that holds mcp:connect. See Permissions.

A gate, not a grant

mcp:connect lets a user connect. It does not grant any data. A connected user reaches only the tools, and the manage_* actions, whose permissions they also hold. The two tools that need no other permission, mcp_info and get_system_health, need only mcp:connect. See Tools.

With mcp:connect a user can:

  • create, rotate and revoke their own personal keys, while the organization's mode allows personal keys;
  • approve and revoke the apps that connect as them, when the organization's mode includes app sign-in;
  • open an MCP session whose tools run with their own permissions.

Holding mcp:connect does not let a user see anyone else's keys.

docs.title: Who manages MCP: mcp:manage
docs.text:
Manage MCP (mcp:manage) governs the organization's MCP settings. Its holder can:

  • set the organization's mode under AI Setup > MCP Authentication;
  • list and revoke any MCP key in the organization;
  • with the organization in app sign-in mode, register, edit and revoke OAuth clients, and list and revoke the organization's connected apps.

mcp:manage cannot create an org-wide key, and cannot create a key for another user. It implies mcp:connect, so its holder can create their own personal key. mcp:manage and Manage AI (ai:manage) are separate permissions, and neither implies the other. The AI Setup page opens only for holders of ai:manage, so an MCP administrator needs both to use the page.

docs.title: What needs admin itself
docs.text:
These actions need the admin permission, not only mcp:manage:

  • marking an OAuth client as trusted;
  • changing the return addresses of a trusted client;
  • reading or changing the client policy for apps that publish a client metadata document.

See App Sign-in (OAuth 2.1).

docs.title: Administering keys
docs.text:
The MCP Authentication card of AI Setup lists every key in the organization for holders of mcp:manage.

Method and path Purpose GET /api/v1/ai/mcp/keys Every key in the organization, with type, owner (email), prefix, created, expires and last used DELETE /api/v1/ai/mcp/keys/:id Revoke any key in the organization. Answers 404 if the key does not exist. POST /api/v1/ai/mcp/keys/revoke-legacy Revoke every retired org-wide key that is not yet revoked POST /api/v1/ai/mcp/keys Retired. Answers 410.

The page notes: "Administrators can revoke any key but cannot create one for someone else." The owner column names a key's owner only when that user belongs to the administrator's organization.

docs.title: Org-wide keys are retired
docs.text:
The org-wide wfmcp_… keys of earlier releases are retired in 1.2.0.

  • They no longer authenticate. Presenting one returns 401 with the message: "Org-wide MCP keys were retired in 1.2.0. Create a personal MCP key under Profile → Security."
  • They cannot be created. POST /api/v1/ai/mcp/keys answers 410 with the code org_keys_retired.
  • They stay listed as Org-wide (retired), so you can clean them up. The 90-day removal of inactive personal keys never removes them.
  • Clean them up with Revoke all legacy keys in the key table, or with POST /api/v1/ai/mcp/keys/revoke-legacy.

Revoke retired keys before a downgrade

Upgrading does not revoke org-wide keys. A 1.1.x build accepts them again, so if you might downgrade, click Revoke all legacy keys first.

docs.title: When revocation takes effect
docs.text:
Transport When a revocation applies HTTP (/mcp) On the next request. Each request is authenticated and admitted on its own. WebSocket (/ws/chat) On the next request on the socket. An idle socket is re-checked every 60 seconds, so it closes within a minute.

A refused WebSocket closes with code 1008 and the reason "MCP credential is no longer valid".

So revoking a key, disabling a user, removing mcp:connect, suspending the tenant or turning off personal keys stops an active client on its next request, and an idle one within a minute. For an app, revoking its grant or the app, removing mcp:connect or leaving app sign-in stops it at its next request, whatever time its access token has left.

docs.title: Ending every session on an install
docs.text:
Disabling a user is the control for one account: the account is refused on every request, including its personal keys and app connections.

To end every signed-in session on an install at once:

  • Docker Compose or self-managed install: give every service a new JWT_SECRET (and WF_JWT_SECRET where it is set), then recreate the containers. Browser sessions and the 15-minute access tokens of connected apps stop working, and every user signs in again.
  • WFA appliance: WFA supplies this secret. Do not set it by hand.

What rotating the secret does not end

Rotating JWT_SECRET does not revoke personal MCP keys, and does not end app connections: an app's refresh token does not depend on the secret, so the app gets a new access token at its next refresh. Revoke keys under AI Setup > MCP Authentication, and revoke app connections under Connected apps in this organization.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Personal MCP Keys
  • App Sign-in (OAuth 2.1)
  • Permissions
  • Errors

docs.title: Turning MCP On
docs.text:
MCP connections by personal key, by app sign-in and over HTTP /mcp need two switches, and both are off by default: the organization's mode, and the HTTP transport on the appliance.

Switch Who sets it Where Default Organization mode An administrator with mcp:manage AI Setup > MCP Authentication Browser chat sessions only HTTP transport The appliance operator node.json (mcp_http_enabled), or WF_MCP_HTTP_ENABLED on Docker Compose Off

A WebSocket client on /ws/chat needs only the organization mode. An HTTP client on /mcp needs both.

docs.title: Switch 1: the organization mode
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Settings > General Settings > AI Setup.
  2. In MCP Authentication, under Who can connect over MCP, choose a mode.
  3. Click Save Authentication.
Choice Stored auth_mode Personal keys App sign-in Browser chat sessions Browser chat sessions only (default) off Cannot be created, and existing keys are refused Refused Work, for users who hold mcp:connect Browser chat sessions and personal keys api_key Can be created and used Refused Work, for users who hold mcp:connect Browser chat sessions, personal keys and app sign-in oauth Can be created and used Allowed Work, for users who hold mcp:connect

The same change through the API:

PUT /api/v1/ai/mcp   {"auth_mode": "api_key"}

docs.title: Who can change it
docs.text:
• Changing the mode needs the Manage MCP (mcp:manage) permission. A platform administrator also passes this check.
  • The AI Setup page itself opens only for users who hold Manage AI (ai:manage), and the MCP Authentication card is shown only to holders of mcp:manage.
  • Any signed-in user of the organization can read the stored mode with GET /api/v1/ai/mcp.

docs.title: What each change does
docs.text:
• Back to Browser chat sessions only. Personal keys cannot be created (409 personal_keys_disabled), and existing keys are refused on their next request. An idle WebSocket closes within a minute.
  • App sign-in can be chosen only when the appliance's MCP_PUBLIC_URL and MCP_OAUTH_UI_URL settings are both valid. Otherwise the save is refused with 409 oauth_unavailable, and the page says that app sign-in is not available on this appliance. See App Sign-in (OAuth 2.1).
  • Leaving app sign-in revokes every connected app in the organization before the new mode is saved. If that revocation fails, the save answers 500 and the mode stays as it was.
  • Licence. On a licence that does not include the MCP connector, a save that turns something on is refused with 403. Turning MCP off always works. See MCP Licensing.

docs.title: Switch 2: the HTTP transport
docs.text: Claude Desktop, Cursor and Claude Code use Streamable HTTP, so most clients need POST /mcp. Without this switch the route is not registered at all, and /mcp answers 404.

docs.title: WFA appliance
docs.text:
1. Add the field to /witfoo/configs/node.json (WFA 2.5.1 or later; install WFA 2.5.4, the current release):

    {
  "mcp_http_enabled": true
}

  2. Restart WFA:

    wfa restart

WFA sets WF_MCP_HTTP_ENABLED=true on the dispatcher container, analytics-dispatcher-svc.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text: Set WF_MCP_HTTP_ENABLED=true in the environment. Every compose file that builds a dispatcher passes it through, with a default of false.

docs.title: Check that it took effect
docs.text:
If mcp_http_enabled: true appears to do nothing:

  1. Check the running WFA version with wfa version, or with rpm -q wfa or dpkg -s wfa.

  2. Check that the dispatcher has the variable:

    docker inspect analytics-dispatcher-svc | grep WF_MCP_HTTP_ENABLED

Never run wfad --version

wfad --version starts a second WFA daemon. Use wfa version, rpm -q wfa or dpkg -s wfa to read the version.

The transport switch is separate from the organization mode on purpose: an organization that allowed keys for a WebSocket client does not silently gain an HTTP endpoint that can be reached from outside.

docs.title: Browser origins
docs.text:
A headless AI client sends no Origin header and needs no origin configuration. When a request does carry Origin, the origin must be allowed, for personal keys, access tokens and browser sessions alike. There is no bypass.

Path Who decides Setting /ws/chat, /ws/graph and /ws/events through the reverse proxy The reverse proxy, before it contacts the dispatcher The reverse proxy's WF_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. The appliance's own origin is always accepted. POST /mcp The dispatcher The dispatcher's WF_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

Behind the reverse proxy the dispatcher sees its own internal host name, so a browser page that calls POST /mcp must be listed in the dispatcher's WF_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, even when the page is served by the appliance itself. A refused origin gets 403 with {"error":"Origin not allowed"}. See Environment Variables.

docs.title: MCP Server Settings
docs.text:
The MCP Server Settings section of AI Setup saves four values with PUT /api/v1/ai/mcp.

Known limitation

Of the four MCP Server Settings fields, only the rate limit has an effect, and only for apps that use app sign-in. Who can connect over MCP under MCP Authentication decides who is admitted, and WF_ALLOWED_ORIGINS decides browser origins.

Field Saved as Effect in 1.2.0 MCP Server Enabled enabled Saved and shown. It does not change which clients are admitted. Allowed Origins (comma-separated) allowed_origins Saved and shown. No origin check uses it: origins come from WF_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. Rate Limit (requests/min) rate_limit_per_min 1 to 10,000, default 60. Applies to apps that use app sign-in only. A personal key or a browser session is not limited by it. Max Concurrent Connections max_concurrent Saved and shown. Nothing limits connections by it.

To stop personal-key and app clients, choose Browser chat sessions only under MCP Authentication.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Authentication & Permissions: grant mcp:connect to the users who should connect.
  • Personal MCP Keys: create a key.
  • Exposure Listener (Port 8444) or AI-Connector Relay: reach the appliance from a hosted marketplace client.

docs.title: Connecting AI Clients & Marketplaces
docs.text: Connect an AI client to your appliance with a personal key, or let an app sign in through the appliance's own OAuth 2.1 server.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• MCP is turned on for the organization, and the HTTP transport is on for HTTP clients. See Turning MCP On.
  • You hold Connect MCP (mcp:connect). See Authentication & Permissions.
  • The appliance licence includes the MCP connector. See MCP Licensing.

docs.title: Choose a route
docs.text: Where the client runs Route Address On your network, such as a desktop client or Claude Code on a laptop The main listener https://<appliance>/mcp On a vendor's servers, such as claude.ai or ChatGPT, with an inbound port you can open The exposure listener on port 8444 https://<published name>/mcp, through the proxy or load balancer in front of port 8444 On a vendor's servers, with no inbound port The AI-connector relay https://mcp-relay.witfoo.com/h/<handle>/mcp An air-gapped appliance The main listener, from clients on your own network only https://<appliance>/mcp

docs.title: Connect with a personal key
docs.text:
Create a key under Profile > Security > MCP connections first. See Personal MCP Keys. The card shows the snippets below filled in with your key right after you create it.

Replace <appliance> with your appliance's address and wfmcpu_xxxxxxxx with your key.

Claude CodeClaude DesktopCursorWebSocket client 
claude mcp add --transport http witfoo https://<appliance>/mcp \
  --header "X-MCP-Key: wfmcpu_xxxxxxxx"

Add the server to claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "witfoo": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://<appliance>/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-MCP-Key": "wfmcpu_xxxxxxxx" }
    }
  }
}

Add the server to .cursor/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "witfoo": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://<appliance>/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-MCP-Key": "wfmcpu_xxxxxxxx" }
    }
  }
}

Connect to wss://<appliance>/ws/chat and send the same header on the upgrade request:

X-MCP-Key: wfmcpu_xxxxxxxx

Send the key in a header

Never put a key in a URL. A key in a URL is refused with 400.

docs.title: A hosted connector for a whole organization
docs.text: A hosted connector that takes one static credential for everyone in the organization shares that credential between all of them. Give it the personal key of a dedicated user who holds only the permissions the connector needs, never an administrator's.

docs.title: Connect with app sign-in
docs.text:
App sign-in needs the appliance set up for it and the organization in Browser chat sessions, personal keys and app sign-in mode. See App Sign-in (OAuth 2.1). The app is given the connector URL, MCP_PUBLIC_URL, for example https://mcp.example.com/mcp.

Claude and Claude CodeCursor and MCP Inspector

Claude and Claude Code publish a client metadata document, so they do not need to be registered.

  1. An administrator (admin) opens AI Setup > MCP Authentication > Client policy, uses Add to the allow list to add Claude or Claude Code, and clicks Save policy.
  2. The user adds the connector URL in the app and starts the sign-in.
  3. The user signs in to WitFoo if asked, reviews the consent page, and clicks Approve.
  4. The connection appears under Profile > Security > Connected apps.

Claude can also be registered as a client with the Claude preset, as for Cursor.

  1. An administrator with mcp:manage opens AI Setup > MCP Authentication > OAuth clients, clicks Add client, and uses Fill in from a known app to choose Cursor or MCP Inspector.
  2. The administrator saves the client and gives the user its Client ID (wfmcpc_…).
  3. The user enters the connector URL and the Client ID in the app and starts the sign-in.
  4. The user signs in to WitFoo if asked, reviews the consent page, and clicks Approve.
  5. The connection appears under Profile > Security > Connected apps.

Check a preset's return addresses against what the app actually sends. Apps that need a custom-scheme return address such as cursor:// cannot be registered.

For a hosted app, the vendor's servers must reach /mcp, the discovery documents and /oauth/token, and the approving user's browser must reach the analytics UI.

docs.title: ChatGPT
docs.text:
