docs.title: Incidents
docs.text:
• search_incidents and get_incident_details return results.
  • search_incidents returns up to limit incidents (default 50, at most 100), newest first. limit plus offset may not exceed 10,000. Use a result's next_offset to continue.
  • A search result carries no node or edge count. The detail's node_count and edge_count are the numbers of node ids and edge ids the incident carries.
  • To read who is assigned, call manage_incident_assignments with the action list.

docs.title: Optional arguments
docs.text:
Optional arguments are optional. search_nodes does not require limit, search_incidents does not require limit or offset, and search_artifacts does not require only_alarms, limit or offset.

Time arguments are RFC 3339 timestamps. The node_type filter of search_nodes includes file. execute_responder_job takes a trigger_type of manual, playbook or mcp.

docs.title: search_artifacts
docs.text:
search_artifacts reads one page and does not count every match. Its answer says what that page can claim:

Field Meaning total The number of artifacts in this answer, not a count of every match. When capped is true it is a floor. capped true when the answer filled limit, so more artifacts may match. next_offset Present only when capped is true. Pass it as offset to continue. incomplete true when matches may be missing from this answer, whatever its size. capped: false means complete only when incomplete is false too. incomplete_reason Present only when incomplete is true. partial: part of the read failed for a moment, and a re-run may find more. rows: the read stopped at its row bound, so narrow the time range or add a filter. time: a read time budget ran out.
  • limit plus offset may not exceed 10,000. A deeper request is refused with a tool error.
  • The time window may not be wider than the organization's search window, the same limit Signal Search uses. A wider window is refused before anything is read.
  • Each missing time bound is filled on its own: the start defaults to 24 hours before now, and the end defaults to now. So a lone time_start 30 days back is a 30-day window and can be refused. A call with neither bound reads the last 24 hours.

docs.title: search_nodes
docs.text:
• ip and hostname are exact lookups. They find a host by any IP address or hostname it has, not only the one it was first seen with.
  • A lookup returns at most one node. With neither ip nor hostname, node_type filters a scan.
  • capped is always present. It is true when a scan filled limit (default 50, at most 1,000), so more nodes may match. An ip or hostname lookup is never capped.
  • A lookup that cannot be completed is an error ("the node lookup could not be completed; this does not mean no such node exists"), never an empty list.

docs.title: get_audit_remediation
docs.text: get_audit_remediation returns the check's resource_type when it is called with a check_id, as it does when it is called with a finding_id.

docs.title: Report tools
docs.text:
• get_executive_summary, get_compliance_status, get_cost_savings and get_tool_effectiveness read the latest stored snapshot.
  • A snapshot that is empty or cannot be read is an error that names the report date, never a report of zeros.
  • Each answer carries the snapshot's confidence flag. low_confidence_inputs_not_ready means the figures may be understated.
  • get_executive_summary takes no inputs. It refuses start_date and end_date.

docs.title: generate_report
docs.text:
generate_report regenerates the report snapshots for the caller's organization and answers when the pass has finished. It holds the call open for up to five minutes.

HTTP requests close at 120 seconds

The reverse proxy in front of HTTP /mcp closes a request at 120 seconds. Over HTTP /mcp, a pass that takes longer ends in a transport error instead of the tool's answer. A pass that fails is an error result.

docs.title: Dashboards and attribution
docs.text: Dashboard tools work for holders of the dashboards:* permissions. Tools that record who acted record the connected user.

docs.title: In-app AI assistant
docs.text:
The in-app AI assistant uses the same tool handlers through a bridge. It does not connect over /ws/chat. It offers five read-only tools:

Tool Permission search_nodes graph:read search_artifacts signals:read search_observations observations:read get_audit_remediation auditor:read search_directory cybergrid:publications:read
  • Each tool call is authorized with the caller's own permissions, by the same rule as an MCP tools/call.
  • The permissions come from the caller's signed-in session. A permission removed from a role stops working for the assistant when the caller's session token is next replaced.
  • A limit larger than 200 is run at 200.
  • search_artifacts is held to the organization's search window.

In an AI analysis of a work unit, search_artifacts answers "artifact search is not available on this service". search_nodes works there as usual.

See Chat Interface.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: For the responses a client can receive at connection and on each request, see MCP Errors.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: WitFoo Analytics exposes a RESTful API for all platform operations. The API follows consistent patterns for authentication, request/response format, pagination, and error handling.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
https://<appliance>/api/v1

Call the API through the reverse proxy on port 443. The endpoint tables write paths from /v1, so /v1/artifacts is https://<appliance>/api/v1/artifacts.

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text:
Browser/Client → Reverse Proxy (:443) → API (:8080) → Incident Engine (:8082) → Cassandra

The API service acts as a gateway adding JWT authentication, permission checks, and request routing. The Incident Engine contains all business logic.

In 1.2.0 the API's own port is not reachable from outside the appliance: a WFA appliance does not publish it, and on Docker Compose it listens on INTERNAL_LISTEN_IP (127.0.0.1 by default). See Published addresses.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• Authentication — JWT token management
  • Standards — Request/response conventions
  • Errors — Error codes and handling
  • Endpoints — Full endpoint reference

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: WitFoo Analytics uses JWT (JSON Web Tokens) with HS256 signing for API authentication.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/auth/login

Request:

{
  "email": "admin@witfoo.com",
  "password": "password"
}

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "token": "eyJhbG...",
    "user": {
      "id": "uuid",
      "email": "admin@witfoo.com",
      "role": "admin"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Using Tokens
docs.text:
Include the JWT in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer eyJhbG...

docs.title: Token Contents
docs.text: Claim Description sub User ID email User email org_id Organization ID role User role name permissions Array of granted permissions exp Expiration timestamp

docs.title: Token Refresh
docs.text: Tokens expire after the configured duration (default: 24 hours). Obtain a new token by logging in again.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: API errors follow standard HTTP status codes with descriptive messages.

docs.title: Error Response Format
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Human-readable error description"
}

docs.title: Status Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 200 Success 201 Created 400 Bad Request — invalid input 401 Unauthorized — missing or invalid token 403 Forbidden — insufficient permissions 404 Not Found — resource doesn't exist 409 Conflict — duplicate resource 422 Unprocessable Entity — validation error 500 Internal Server Error

docs.title: Common Errors
docs.text: Error Cause Fix "token expired" JWT has expired Login again to get new token "permission denied" Insufficient role Contact admin for role change "invalid UUID" Malformed UUID parameter Use valid UUID v4 format "not found" Resource doesn't exist Verify the resource ID

docs.title: API Standards
docs.text: All API endpoints follow consistent conventions.

docs.title: Response Format
docs.text:
Every response uses this envelope:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Optional message",
  "data": { }
}

Error responses:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Error description"
}

docs.title: HTTP Methods
docs.text: Method Usage GET Retrieve resources POST Create resources PUT Update resources (full replacement) DELETE Remove resources

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
List endpoints support pagination:

Parameter Default Description limit 25 Items per page (max 100) offset 0 Number of items to skip

docs.title: Content Type
docs.text: All requests and responses use application/json unless otherwise noted (e.g., CSV export uses text/csv).

docs.title: Date Formats
docs.text: All timestamps use ISO 8601 format: 2026-01-15T10:30:00Z

docs.title: Admin Roles
docs.text: Manage role definitions and permission assignments.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/roles admin List all roles GET /v1/roles/:id admin Get role details POST /v1/roles admin Create role PUT /v1/roles/:id admin Update role DELETE /v1/roles/:id admin Delete role

docs.title: Role Object
docs.text:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "name": "analyst",
  "permissions": ["signals:read", "signals:write", "observer:read"],
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

docs.title: Admin Users
docs.text: Manage user accounts, roles, and account status.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Every /v1/admin/users route needs the admin permission.

Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/admin/users admin List the organization's users POST /v1/admin/users admin Create a user GET /v1/admin/users/:id admin Get a user and their roles PUT /v1/admin/users/:id admin Update a user's name or email DELETE /v1/admin/users/:id admin Disable a user (the account and its data stay) POST /v1/admin/users/:id/enable admin Enable a disabled user POST /v1/admin/users/:id/roles admin Assign roles POST /v1/admin/users/:id/reset-password admin Reset a user's password PUT /v1/admin/users/:id/locale admin Set a user's locale GET /v1/users users:read List users, for assignment pickers

docs.title: Disable and enable
docs.text:
DELETE /v1/admin/users/:id is a soft disable: the account and its data stay, with active set to false. There is no hard delete in 1.2.0. POST /v1/admin/users/:id/enable enables the account again, and is a no-op for an active user.

Status Code When 200 The user was disabled or enabled 400 The user ID is not valid 403 platform_admin_required The account carries the platform-administrator flag or holds a role with a platform: permission, and the caller is not a platform administrator 404 No such user in the caller's organization 409 cannot_disable_self The caller tried to disable their own account 409 cannot_enable_self The caller tried to enable their own account 503 Enable only: the user's earlier personal MCP keys could not be revoked, so the user was not enabled. Try again

Disabling a user revokes their personal MCP keys and ends their sessions. Enabling revokes any remaining keys first; keys are never restored.

docs.title: Update a user
docs.text:
PUT /v1/admin/users/:id changes first_name, last_name and email. A request that changes active is refused with 400 and the code active_not_updatable; use the disable and enable routes instead. A request that repeats the current status is accepted.

An email address must be one plain address. A request with an address that is blank or not one plain address is refused with 400.

docs.title: User Object
docs.text:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "username": "jsmith",
  "email": "analyst@example.com",
  "first_name": "Jane",
  "last_name": "Smith",
  "role_ids": ["uuid"],
  "org_id": "example",
  "active": true,
  "created_at": "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "last_login": "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "locale": "en"
}

GET /v1/admin/users and GET /v1/admin/users/:id also return roles (the role objects) and permissions (the union of the roles' permissions).

docs.title: Create a user
docs.text:
{
  "email": "analyst@example.com",
  "username": "jsmith",
  "password": "a-strong-password",
  "first_name": "Jane",
  "last_name": "Smith",
  "role_ids": ["uuid"],
  "active": true
}

email, username, password (8 to 72 characters), first_name, last_name and at least one entry in role_ids are required.

docs.title: AI
docs.text:
AI provider configuration, chat sessions, and MCP administration.

Paths in the tables below are relative to /api unless they start with /oauth or /.well-known, which are served at the root of the appliance.

docs.title: AI Configuration
docs.text: Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/ai/configs Any signed-in user List AI provider configurations. The API key is never returned, and base_url is shown without its user information, query or fragment. GET /v1/ai/configs/:id Any signed-in user Get one configuration POST /v1/ai/configs ai:manage Create a configuration PUT /v1/ai/configs/:id ai:manage Update a configuration DELETE /v1/ai/configs/:id ai:manage Delete a configuration PUT /v1/ai/configs/:id/enable ai:manage Enable or disable a configuration. The body must state the value, for example {"enabled": false}. GET /v1/ai/configs/:id/models ai:manage List the models a stored configuration can use GET /v1/ai/providers ai:manage List the supported providers POST /v1/ai/providers/:provider/models ai:manage List a provider's models before the configuration is saved GET /v1/ai/purpose-routing Any signed-in user Read which configuration serves each purpose PUT /v1/ai/purpose-routing ai:manage Change the purpose routing GET /v1/ai/response-automation Any signed-in user Read the response automation settings PUT /v1/ai/response-automation ai:manage Change the response automation settings GET /v1/ai/profile ai:manage Read the model profile PUT /v1/ai/profile ai:manage Change the model profile

docs.title: Chat Sessions
docs.text: Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/ai/chat/sessions ai:read List your chat sessions POST /v1/ai/chat/sessions ai:write Create a chat session GET /v1/ai/chat/sessions/:id ai:read Get a session GET /v1/ai/chat/sessions/:id/messages ai:read Get a session's messages POST /v1/ai/chat/sessions/:id/messages ai:write Send a message PUT /v1/ai/chat/sessions/:id/title ai:write Rename a session DELETE /v1/ai/chat/sessions/:id ai:write Delete a session

docs.title: MCP Configuration
docs.text:
Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/ai/mcp Any signed-in user Read the organization's MCP settings, including auth_mode PUT /v1/ai/mcp mcp:manage Change the MCP settings, for example {"auth_mode": "api_key"} GET /v1/ai/mcp/relay mcp:manage Read the MCP relay status shown on AI Setup

auth_mode is off (the default), api_key or oauth.

  • PUT answers 409 with the code oauth_unavailable when oauth is chosen on an appliance that is not set up for app sign-in.
  • Moving the organization out of oauth revokes every app grant first. If that revocation fails, the PUT answers 500 and the mode stays as it was.
  • On a licence that does not include MCP, a PUT that turns something on answers 403 with feature_not_available.

See MCP Configuration.

docs.title: MCP Keys (administration)
docs.text:
Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/ai/mcp/keys mcp:manage List every key in the organization, with type, owner email, prefix, created, expires and last used DELETE /v1/ai/mcp/keys/:id mcp:manage Revoke any key in the organization. 404 if it does not exist. POST /v1/ai/mcp/keys/revoke-legacy mcp:manage Revoke every retired org-wide key that is not yet revoked POST /v1/ai/mcp/keys mcp:manage Retired. Answers 410 with the code org_keys_retired.

An administrator can list and revoke any key, but cannot create a key for someone else.

docs.title: Personal MCP Keys
docs.text:
Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/users/me/mcp-keys mcp:connect List your keys. Never returns a secret. POST /v1/users/me/mcp-keys mcp:connect Create a key: {"name": "…", "expires_in_days": 90}. The response secret is shown once. POST /v1/users/me/mcp-keys/:id/rotate mcp:connect Rotate an active key. The response carries the new secret. DELETE /v1/users/me/mcp-keys/:id mcp:connect Revoke one of your keys

Responses that carry a secret send Cache-Control: no-store. See Personal MCP Keys.

docs.title: App Sign-in Administration
docs.text:
These routes answer 404 unless the appliance is set up for app sign-in and the organization's auth_mode is oauth. A caller without the permission is refused first.

Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/ai/mcp/grants mcp:manage List every live app grant in the organization DELETE /v1/ai/mcp/grants/:grant_id mcp:manage Revoke one grant GET /v1/ai/mcp/oauth-clients mcp:manage List the registered clients POST /v1/ai/mcp/oauth-clients mcp:manage; also admin to set trusted Register a client: {"name": "…", "redirect_uris": ["…"], "trusted": false}. The response carries its Client ID. PATCH /v1/ai/mcp/oauth-clients/:id mcp:manage; also admin to change trust or a trusted client's return addresses Change a client's name, return addresses or trust DELETE /v1/ai/mcp/oauth-clients/:id mcp:manage Revoke a client and every grant held for it GET /v1/ai/mcp/oauth-policy admin Read the client policy for apps that publish a client metadata document PUT /v1/ai/mcp/oauth-policy admin Replace the client policy. A save that denies an app revokes that app's grants. GET /v1/users/me/mcp-grants mcp:connect List the apps connected as you DELETE /v1/users/me/mcp-grants/:grant_id mcp:connect Revoke one of your app connections POST /v1/oauth/authorize/describe mcp:connect Used by the consent page to describe a request POST /v1/oauth/authorize/decision mcp:connect Used by the consent page to approve or deny a request

See App Sign-in (OAuth 2.1).

docs.title: OAuth Endpoints
docs.text:
These are served at the root of the appliance once MCP_PUBLIC_URL and MCP_OAUTH_UI_URL are both set to valid values. The two protected-resource paths also need the HTTP transport (WF_MCP_HTTP_ENABLED) on; without it they answer 404, while the authorization-server document and /oauth/token are still served.

Method Path Description POST /oauth/token Token endpoint. A form POST of at most 8 KiB. Every response sends Cache-Control: no-store. GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource Protected-resource metadata GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp Protected-resource metadata for /mcp GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server Authorization-server metadata

There is no registration endpoint.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: For MCP-specific responses, see MCP Errors.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text: Artifacts represent raw security signals ingested into the analytics pipeline. They include IDS alerts, authentication events, firewall logs, DNS queries, and other telemetry collected from security tools and infrastructure.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /v1/artifacts Search artifacts with filters GET /v1/artifacts/histogram Timeline counts for a search GET /v1/artifacts/facet-counts Facet counts for a search GET /v1/artifacts/facets Facet counts for the Signal Search sidebar GET /v1/artifacts/stats Artifact statistics for a window GET /v1/artifacts/:id Get one artifact

Every request carries the bearer token of a signed-in user and reads only that user's organization.

Ingesting artifacts

POST /v1/artifacts is removed and has no replacement. Artifacts reach the appliance through the artifact receiver.

docs.title: GET /v1/artifacts
docs.text: Search and filter ingested artifacts, newest first.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description time_start string Start of the time range (RFC 3339) time_end string End of the time range (RFC 3339) limit integer Results per page. Absent or zero means the default of 100. offset integer Results to skip. offset plus limit may not exceed 10,000. search string A word or phrase the message must contain, ignoring upper and lower case. At least three bytes. stream_name string Stream name (exact match) message_type string Message type action string Action (exact match) client_ip string Client IP address server_ip string Server IP address user_name string User name vendor_code string Vendor code node_id string Artifacts that reference a graph node file_name_like string File name pattern severity_min integer Minimum severity (1-10) severity_max integer Maximum severity (1-10) only_alarms boolean Only artifacts that matched a lead rule matched_lead_rules string Comma-separated lead rule IDs (any of them) stix_indicator_ids string Comma-separated STIX indicator IDs attack_technique_ids string Comma-separated MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs tags string Tag; repeat the parameter for more than one filters JSON A list of {"field", "operator", "value"} conditions. Operators: =, !=, : (contains), >, >=, <, <=.

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -G "https://analytics.example.com/api/v1/artifacts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "time_start=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z" \
  --data-urlencode "time_end=2026-11-02T00:00:00Z" \
  --data-urlencode "stream_name=ids" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=50"

docs.title: Search Time Window
docs.text:
GET /v1/artifacts, /v1/artifacts/histogram and /v1/artifacts/facet-counts serve a bounded time window. The limit is set per organization.

Source of the limit Limit The organization's Retention > Search setting That many days (1 to 365) No setting, or a setting that cannot be read The appliance's artifact retention, 30 days by default A retention with no expiry 7 days
  • Every successful search carries the limit in meta.max_window_seconds. Read it from the response; never hardcode it.
  • A wider window is refused with 400 and the code search_window_too_wide. details.limit_seconds is the organization's limit.
  • A half-open window is checked too. Each missing bound is filled on its own: the start defaults to 24 hours before now, and the end defaults to now. So time_start alone, far in the past, can be refused. Only a request with neither bound reads the default window.
  • A window whose end is before its start is refused with the code search_window_inverted.
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Time range exceeds the maximum supported search window",
  "error": "search window of 739h28m39.977s exceeds the maximum of 168h0m0s",
  "code": "search_window_too_wide",
  "details": { "limit_seconds": 604800, "requested_seconds": 2662119 }
}

GET /v1/artifacts/stats keeps its own 30-day limit.

docs.title: Partial Reads (meta.scan)
docs.text:
Some filters are applied while the server reads the window, newest first: contains (:), not-equal (!=), comparisons on a number field, a Client IP or Server IP match on an IPv6 address, the location filter, and the search word.

Such a read is bounded. The result list and the timeline also stop after 10 seconds and answer with what they have read. When a read stopped early, the response carries meta.scan:

"meta": { "scan": { "scanned": 10000, "cap": 10000, "incomplete": true, "reason": "rows" } }
reason Meaning rows The read reached its row limit. A re-run reads the same rows. Narrow the time range or add a filter. time The 10-second read limit ran out. partial Part of the range could not be read just now. A re-run may find more.

When incomplete is true, matching records may be missing. Do not show a short or empty result as if the whole window was read. A client that meets a reason it does not know should treat the read as incomplete.

The facet counts carry their own estimated flag instead of meta.scan.

docs.title: Request Limits
docs.text:
A request the server cannot run as sent is refused with 400 and the code invalid_parameter. details.parameter names the parameter. The body never repeats the value.

Limit Value A free-text value matched exactly 8,192 bytes A value matched with :, != or a comparison, and file_name_like 65,535 bytes A list parameter (tags, matched_lead_rules, stix_indicator_ids, attack_technique_ids) 100 values The filters parameter 128 entries The query string 256 parameters search At least 3 bytes client_ip, server_ip Must be an IP address offset plus limit At most 10,000 limit, offset Not negative

docs.title: IP Address Parameters on the Timeline and Facet Counts
docs.text:
On the histogram and the facet counts, the client_ip and server_ip parameters apply an IPv6 address but not an IPv4 address. The result list applies both. To apply an IPv4 address on all three, send the condition in filters:

filters=[{"field":"client_ip","operator":"=","value":"10.9.9.9"}]

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text: Status Description 400 A parameter the server cannot use (invalid_parameter), or a time window that is too wide or inverted 401 Missing or invalid token 499 The client went away before the answer 500 The artifact store could not be read. A search never answers an empty result in its place. 503 The read passed its deadline

docs.title: Authentication Settings
docs.text: Configure LDAP, SAML, and local authentication.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Permission Description GET /v1/admin/settings/auth settings:manage Get the organization's auth configuration (secrets redacted) PUT /v1/admin/settings/auth settings:manage Update the auth configuration POST /v1/admin/settings/auth/ldap/test settings:manage Test an LDAP connection POST /v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/test settings:manage Test a SAML configuration (4 checks) POST /v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/generate-keypair settings:manage Generate an SP signing key pair POST /v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/fetch-metadata settings:manage Fetch and parse IdP metadata from a URL GET /v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/diagnostics settings:manage Check the stored SAML configuration GET /v1/settings/auth none The sign-in options the login page shows (public)

SAML and LDAP settings are saved and read only through these routes. PUT /v1/settings (the general system settings) neither saves nor returns them.

Operator identity organization

When the appliance operator has named an organization in /witfoo/configs/operator-identity-org, only a platform administrator can change that organization's SAML or LDAP configuration. Anyone else gets 403 with the code platform_admin_required. See Authentication.

docs.title: Auth Config Object
docs.text:
{
  "org_id": "example",
  "auth_mode": "mixed_saml",
  "ldap": {
    "enabled": false,
    "server_url": "ldaps://ldap.example.com:636",
    "bind_dn": "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com",
    "bind_password": "***REDACTED***",
    "base_dn": "dc=example,dc=com",
    "user_filter": "(uid=%s)",
    "group_filter": "(memberUid=%s)",
    "tls_enabled": true,
    "tls_skip_verify": false,
    "group_role_map": {}
  },
  "saml": {
    "enabled": true,
    "entity_id": "https://analytics.example.com",
    "sso_url": "https://idp.example.com/sso",
    "slo_url": "https://idp.example.com/slo",
    "certificate": "***REDACTED***",
    "private_key": "***REDACTED***",
    "sp_certificate": "***REDACTED***",
    "name_id_format": "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress",
    "attribute_mappings": {
      "email": "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress",
      "first_name": "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/givenname",
      "last_name": "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/surname"
    },
    "allow_idp_initiated": false,
    "sign_requests": true,
    "want_assertions_signed": true
  }
}

auth_mode is one of local, ldap, saml, mixed (local and LDAP) or mixed_saml (local and SAML).

Note

Secrets are encrypted at rest. Responses replace the LDAP bind password, the SAML private key, both SAML certificates and inline IdP metadata with ***REDACTED***. A PUT that sends a secret back as ***REDACTED*** keeps the stored value; if nothing is stored to keep, the request is refused with 400 and asks you to enter the secret.

docs.title: SAML Test Endpoint
docs.text: Test a SAML configuration before saving. It runs 4 checks.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
POST /v1/admin/settings/auth/saml/test
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "saml": {
    "entity_id": "https://analytics.example.com",
    "sso_url": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/saml2",
    "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
    "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
    "sp_certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
    "idp_metadata_url": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/federationmetadata/2007-06/federationmetadata.xml"
  }
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The result is in the response's data:

{
  "status": "success",
  "checks": [
    { "name": "certificate_valid", "passed": true, "message": "Valid until 2027-03-15T00:00:00Z" },
    { "name": "key_pair_match", "passed": true, "message": "Private key matches certificate" },
    { "name": "metadata_fetchable", "passed": true, "message": "Metadata URL is accessible" },
    { "name": "sp_build_successful", "passed": true, "message": "Service Provider configuration is valid" }
  ]
}

status is success, partial or failed. The metadata check is skipped, and passes, when no idp_metadata_url is given.

An organization holds at most 1,000 pending feeds, and a pending feed expires after 7 days. A decision on a feed that has expired answers 404. See Integration Management.

docs.title: Artifact Receiver
docs.text:
Conductors send artifacts directly to the Analytics artifact receiver (artifact-ingestion), not through the reverse proxy:

Method URL Authentication Description POST https://<analytics-host>:8443/v1/conductor/artifacts/batch HMAC-SHA256 signature, checked when ANALYTICS_SECRET is set on the receiver Receive a batch of artifacts from a Conductor

On an AIO + Conductor appliance the local Conductor uses the internal port 8090. WFA sets the endpoint when it provisions the Conductor.

The /ingestion/ path is removed

The reverse proxy no longer serves the /ingestion/ path. A Conductor whose artifact endpoint was typed by hand with an /ingestion/ prefix now receives 404. Point it at https://<analytics-host>:8443/v1/conductor/artifacts/batch. Who may reach the receiver's ports (8090 and 8443) is decided by your firewall and network placement.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Limit Value Artifacts in one batch 1,000. A larger batch is answered 400 with batch size exceeds maximum of 1000 artifacts Largest artifact 9.5 MiB (9,961,472 bytes) Request line and headers 12,288 bytes in all. Over it, the receiver answers 431 TLS port HTTP/1.1 only. A client that offers only HTTP/2 fails its handshake Receiver busy 503 with Retry-After: 1. The exporter waits and sends again Body over the limit 413

docs.title: Proxy Routes
docs.text:
Conductor UI requests are proxied through the Analytics reverse proxy at /conductor/. JWT tokens are validated and mapped to Conductor roles via the ConductorAuth middleware.

Analytics Permission Conductor Role conductor:admin Superuser conductor:write Admin conductor:read Staff

Content-Type: application/json

{
  "idp_metadata_url": "https://idp.example.com/metadata",

}

Response (200):

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "SAML configuration is valid",
  "idp_entity_id": "https://idp.example.com",
  "sso_url": "https://idp.example.com/sso"

POST /api/auth/saml/generate-keypair

{
  "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...",
  "generated_at": "2026-03-12T00:00:00Z"

docs.title: Incidents
docs.text: Incidents represent correlated security events that require investigation. The UI shows them as work units. The incident engine aggregates related artifacts, nodes, and observations into actionable incidents with severity ratings and status tracking.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description Permission GET /v1/incidents List incidents with filters work_units:read GET /v1/incidents/:id Get incident details work_units:read GET /v1/incidents/:id/artifacts Get the incident's artifacts Read access to the incident GET /v1/incidents/:id/graph/edges Get the incident's graph edges Read access to the incident GET /v1/incidents/:id/notes List notes work_units:read POST /v1/incidents/:id/notes Add a note work_units:write GET /v1/incidents/:id/audit Get the audit log work_units:read PUT /v1/incidents/:id/status-audit Update the status and record it in the audit log work_units:write

docs.title: Status Values
docs.text: ID Name Classification 1 New -- 2 Investigating -- 3 Resolved True Positive 4 Closed False Positive 5 Disrupted True Positive

docs.title: GET /v1/incidents
docs.text: List incidents for the organization, with optional filtering and pagination.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description status_id string No One status ID, or a comma-separated list of them (status_id=4,5). The parameter can also be repeated. suspicion_level string No low, medium or high, or a comma-separated list of them (suspicion_level=low,high). The parameter can also be repeated. severity_level integer No Severity level (1-10) min_suspicion number No Minimum suspicion score max_suspicion number No Maximum suspicion score node_id string No Incidents that include a graph node attack_technique_id string No Incidents that include a MITRE ATT&CK technique client_ip string No Incidents that include a client IP address limit integer No Max results (default 100, max 500) offset integer No Pagination offset. limit plus offset may not exceed 10,000.
  • A list of status IDs or suspicion levels returns incidents in any of them.
  • An empty entry (4,,5), a value that is not a positive integer, or a suspicion level other than the three is refused with a 400 that names the parameter.
  • A list of two or more statuses is read over the newest 10,000 incidents of the organization. When that read comes back full, the response sets meta.capped: true, a sign that older matches exist.
  • A node_id, attack_technique_id or client_ip filter reads only that item's newest incidents, up to limit, and total counts only those. Beside a status, severity or work definition filter, meta.capped is true when that read comes back full.
  • time_start and time_end are not filters of this route.

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X GET "https://analytics.example.com/api/v1/incidents?status_id=1,2&suspicion_level=high&limit=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: GET /v1/incidents/:id
docs.text: Retrieve full details for a single incident.

docs.title: Path Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description id UUID Incident ID

curl -X GET "https://analytics.example.com/api/v1/incidents/d290f1ee-6c54-4b01-90e6-d701748f0851" \

docs.title: GET /v1/incidents/:id/artifacts
docs.text:
Return the incident's artifacts, oldest first. The work-unit detail page reads them once for its histogram, table and timeline.

Parameter Type Description limit integer Page size (default 500, max 1,000) page integer 1-based page number (default 1)

The incident is read first, so a caller can read only the artifacts of an incident it can already read. An unknown or another organization's ID answers 404.

docs.title: GET /v1/incidents/:id/graph/edges
docs.text:
Return the incident's graph edges with their time fields, ordered by when they started. Work-unit Replay uses this endpoint.

Parameter Type Description limit integer Page size (default 500, max 1,000) page integer 1-based page number (default 1)

The response carries meta.truncated when the edge set is incomplete: a very busy node, or an incident of more than 2,000 nodes, made the read stop short. The Replay view shows at most 600 nodes and says so when it leaves some out.

docs.title: PUT /v1/incidents/:id/status-audit

docs.title: Work Collections
docs.text:
POST and PUT on /v1/work-collections change only what the request states.

  • Every member (name, description, criteria or criteria_json, enabled, assigned_to, status_id) is optional.
  • A member the body leaves out, or sets to null, keeps its stored value. A member it states, empty included, replaces it.
  • Members the server owns (counts, dates, creator, organization, ID) are ignored.
  • A collection created without enabled is stored disabled.
  • A request that states nothing, that states both criteria and criteria_json, or whose collection does not validate is a 400.

Reading collections needs collections:read; creating and changing them needs collections:write.

docs.text: Status Description 400 A malformed parameter, ID or JSON body, or a negative limit or offset. The code is invalid_parameter and the response names the parameter. 401 Missing or invalid token 403 Insufficient permissions 404 Incident not found 500 Internal server error

docs.title: Partial updates
docs.text:
From 1.2.0, PUT /v1/settings/business changes only the keys the request body carries. A key the body leaves out keeps its stored value. In 1.1.5 a missing key was stored as zero or empty.

  • A product_costs object in the body replaces the whole map. An explicit null or {} clears it.
  • If the stored settings cannot be read, nothing is written and the request answers 500.
  • A body that is not a JSON object is refused with 400.

Scripts that send a partial body to clear values must now send those keys with the values they want.

docs.title: Routes that switch one setting
docs.text:
From 1.2.0, a route that turns a single thing on or off answers 400 when the request body does not state the value. An empty body no longer means off. The web interface always states the value.

This applies to the switch routes of lead rules, AI provider configurations, classification rules, CyberGrid subscriptions, node enrichment settings, the compliance framework switch, observations, Work Definitions, playbooks, MOS detection and incident-naming words, and to the CyberGrid library settings, the AI profile and response automation settings, the onboarding CyberGrid step and the publication update.

To turn off Send Any of the routes above {"enabled": false} The Console organization update the is_active field The Conductor appliance-configuration update enabled on every update element The licensing administrator-flag update the is_admin field

docs.title: WitFoo Conductor Overview
docs.text: WitFoo Conductor is a high-performance security signal processing pipeline that serves as the primary data ingestion point for the WitFoo Analytics platform. Conductor collects, parses, filters, and exports security log data from hundreds of sources, transforming raw signals into structured, actionable artifacts.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Conductor follows a microservice architecture where all inter-service communication flows through a NATS JetStream message broker. Data moves through a linear pipeline: ingestion → parsing → filtering → export.

graph LR
    subgraph Sources
        A[Syslog UDP/TCP] 
        B[Beats/Logstash]
        C[Secure Syslog TLS]
        D[Cloud APIs]
    end

    subgraph Conductor Pipeline
        SS[Signal Server] --> BE[Broker Edge<br/>NATS JetStream]
        SC[Signal Client] --> BE
        BE --> SP[Signal Parser]
        SP --> AF[Artifact Filter]
        AF --> AE[Artifact Exporter]
    end

    subgraph Destinations
        WA[WitFoo Analytics]
        SH[Splunk HEC]
        OS[OpenSearch]
        MS[Microsoft Sentinel]
        OT[Other Destinations]
    end

    A --> SS
    B --> SS
    C --> SS
    D --> SC

    AE --> WA
    AE --> SH
    AE --> OS
    AE --> MS
    AE --> OT

docs.title: Service Map
docs.text:
Conductor consists of 7 core services, each running as an independent Docker container managed by the WFA (WitFoo Agent) daemon:

Service Container Name Purpose Ports Broker Edge broker-edge-svc NATS JetStream message broker 4223 (on 127.0.0.1 only under WFA 2.5.1 and later) Signal Server signal-server-svc Push-based log and flow ingestion 514/tcp, 514/udp, 5044-5045, 6514, 7514, 2055/udp, 8008 (2055/udp and 8008 are off on a new node; see Log Servers) Signal Client signal-client-svc Pull-based API log collection — Signal Parser signal-parser-svc Log parsing and normalization — Artifact Filter artifact-filter-svc Deduplication and enrichment — Artifact Exporter artifact-exporter-svc Export to external systems — Conductor UI conductor-ui-svc Web management interface 443 (8000 internal)

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 200+ Log Parsers — Comprehensive coverage for firewalls, IDS/IPS, authentication systems, DNS, cloud platforms, endpoints, email security, and network infrastructure
  • API Integrations — Pull-based collection from Microsoft, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, Proofpoint, Okta, Cloudflare, cloud flow logs and many more; the Integration Catalog counts them for this release
  • Export Destinations — WitFoo Analytics, Splunk, OpenSearch, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, USM Anywhere, S3, Azure Blob and Google Cloud Storage, SCP Transfer, UDP Syslog and Local Filesystem; see Exporter Configuration
  • NetFlow and IPFIX — A flow collector on UDP 2055 for NetFlow v5, v7, v9 and IPFIX, off until enabled under Log Servers
  • OCSF Export — The object-storage and OpenSearch exporters can write OCSF 1.8.0 class objects
  • Real-Time Dashboard — WebSocket-driven monitoring with pipeline throughput, service health, and container metrics
  • ProtoGraph Deduplication — 11-tuple artifact matching reduces noise while preserving security-relevant event variations
  • STIX Enrichment — Optional threat intelligence enrichment from STIX feeds
  • High Throughput — Sustained processing at >2000 messages per second with optimized serial parser pipeline

docs.title: Deployment Model
docs.text:
Conductor is deployed as a WitFoo Appliance — a dedicated Linux server (physical or virtual) running the WFA daemon. WFA manages the complete container lifecycle: pulling images, creating containers, starting services in dependency order, and handling updates.

Minimum Hardware Requirements

Conductor requires a minimum of 2 CPUs and 8 GB RAM. The wfa configure wizard will warn if the system does not meet these requirements.

For deployment instructions, see the Deployment Guide. For CLI management, see the WFA CLI Reference.

docs.title: Artifact Exporter
docs.text: The Artifact Exporter delivers finalized artifacts from the artifacts.final NATS stream to one or more external destinations. Each export destination runs as an independent connector with its own batching, retry, and formatting logic.

docs.title: WitFoo Analytics (Reporter)
docs.text:
Exports artifacts to WitFoo Analytics using HMAC-SHA256 authenticated HTTP POST requests. This is the primary export path for organizations using the full WitFoo platform.

Setting Description Analytics URL WitFoo Analytics endpoint Shared Secret HMAC-SHA256 authentication key

docs.title: Splunk HEC
docs.text:
Exports to Splunk via the HTTP Event Collector protocol.

Setting Description URL Splunk HEC endpoint Token HEC authentication token Index Target Splunk index Source Type Splunk source type for events

docs.title: OpenSearch
docs.text:
Exports to OpenSearch using the bulk indexing API.

Setting Description URL OpenSearch cluster endpoint Index Target index name Auth Mode basic (username/password), apikey, or none

docs.title: Microsoft Sentinel
docs.text:
Exports to Microsoft Sentinel via the Log Analytics Data Collector API.

Setting Description Workspace ID Log Analytics workspace identifier Shared Key Primary or secondary workspace key

docs.title: AlienVault
docs.text:
Exports to AlienVault USM/OSSIM.

Setting Description Server URL AlienVault server endpoint API Key Authentication key

docs.title: SCP Transfer
docs.text:
Exports artifacts as files transferred via SCP to a remote server.

Setting Description Host Remote server hostname or IP Path Remote directory path Credentials SSH key or password authentication Row Limits Maximum rows per file

docs.title: UDP Syslog
docs.text:
Exports artifacts as syslog messages over UDP.

Setting Description Host Destination syslog server Port UDP port number

docs.title: Local FileSystem
docs.text:
Writes artifacts to files on the local filesystem.

Setting Description Output Directory Path for output files

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All exporters are configured via the NATS KV EXPORTERS bucket and managed through the Conductor UI Exporter Configuration page.

Each exporter supports:

  • Enable/disable toggle — Activate or deactivate individual exporters
  • Batch size — Number of artifacts per batch (where applicable)
  • Retry settings — Automatic retry with backoff on transient failures
  • STIX enrichment toggle — Enable threat intelligence enrichment before export

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Each exporter connector exposes pipeline metrics:

Metric Description pipeline_messages_consumed_total Artifacts consumed from artifacts.final pipeline_messages_published_total Artifacts successfully exported pipeline_errors_total Export failures

docs.title: Artifact Filter
docs.text: The Artifact Filter is the quality gate between parsing and export. It deduplicates redundant events, optionally enriches artifacts with threat intelligence, and applies predicate-based filter rules before publishing export-ready artifacts.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
The filter implements a three-stage processing pipeline:

artifacts.parsed → Deduplication → STIX Enrichment → Predicate Filter → artifacts.final

docs.title: Stage 1: ProtoGraph Deduplication
docs.text:
ProtoGraph reduces noise by hashing artifacts using an 11-tuple key. Duplicate artifacts within a configurable sliding window are collapsed into a single event with a count.

Category Fields Host SenderHost Network ClientIP, ServerIP, ServerPort, Protocol Identity UserName Content FileName, StreamName, MessageType, Action Severity SeverityLabel

For example, 1000 identical SSH login failure events from the same source within the deduplication window produce a single artifact with a count of 1000.

Tip

High compression ratios (>5x) indicate effective deduplication. For every 8 raw syslog messages, approximately 1 artifact is exported in typical deployments.

docs.title: Stage 2: STIX Enrichment (Optional)
docs.text:
When enabled, the STIX enrichment stage checks artifact fields (IPs, domains, file hashes) against configured threat intelligence feeds. Matched indicators are added as metadata to the artifact before it continues through the pipeline.

Enriched artifacts are published to the artifacts.enriched subject and re-consumed by the filter for predicate processing.

docs.title: Stage 3: Predicate Filtering
docs.text:
Predicate filters apply rule-based inclusion and exclusion logic:

  • Field matching — Include or exclude based on specific field values
  • Regex patterns — Pattern matching on artifact content
  • Severity thresholds — Filter by severity level
  • Stream-based rules — Filter specific log sources

When no filter rules are configured, all artifacts pass through to artifacts.final.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The Artifact Filter is configured via the NATS KV FILTERS bucket. Configuration includes:

  • Deduplication window duration (default: 10 minutes)
  • STIX enrichment enable/disable and feed URL
  • Predicate filter rules

Configuration is managed through the Conductor UI Exporter page (STIX toggle) and directly via the NATS KV bucket for advanced predicate rules.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Metric Description pipeline_messages_consumed_total Artifacts consumed from artifacts.parsed pipeline_messages_published_total Artifacts published to artifacts.final pipeline_messages_rejected_total Artifacts rejected by predicate filters pipeline_errors_total Processing errors

docs.title: Broker Edge (NATS JetStream)
docs.text: Broker Edge is the central message broker for the Conductor pipeline. All inter-service communication flows through this NATS JetStream server, providing persistent streams for artifact data, configuration distribution via KV buckets, and monitoring endpoints.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Protocol Purpose 4223 NATS Client connections (all pipeline services) 4443 NATS Leaf node and cluster connections 8223 HTTP Monitoring and management API

docs.title: Streams
docs.text:
Broker Edge auto-creates all required streams on first startup. Streams are created with appliance-specific suffixes to isolate data per deployment.

Stream Purpose Consumers DATA Artifact pipeline (raw → parsed → enriched → final → unknown) signal-parser, artifact-filter, artifact-exporter EVENTS System events and status updates WFA, monitoring tools LOGS Centralized service log collection Log aggregators METRICS Pipeline metrics (Prometheus format) Grafana Cloud, local Prometheus STATUSES Service health and status reports WFA orchestration

The DATA stream uses a hierarchical subject pattern for pipeline stages:

{applianceID}.data.artifacts.{stage}

Where {stage} is one of: raw, parsed, enriched, final, unknown.

docs.title: KV Buckets
docs.text:
Runtime configuration for all pipeline services is stored in JetStream KV buckets. The Conductor UI writes configuration to these buckets, and each service watches its respective bucket for changes.

Bucket Purpose Writer Reader SERVERS Push-based listener configuration conductor-ui signal-server INTEGRATIONS Pull-based API collector configuration conductor-ui signal-client PARSERS Parser enable/disable state conductor-ui signal-parser FILTERS Filter and deduplication rules conductor-ui artifact-filter EXPORTERS Export destination configuration conductor-ui artifact-exporter

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
Verify broker health from any container on the Conductor network:

docker exec broker-edge-svc nats server ping --server=nats://127.0.0.1:4223

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
The HTTP monitoring endpoint on port 8223 provides server information, connection details, and stream statistics:

# Stream status
docker exec broker-edge-svc nats stream ls

# Detailed stream info
docker exec broker-edge-svc nats stream info DATA

# Consumer lag (pending messages)
docker exec broker-edge-svc nats consumer info DATA <consumer-name>

# KV bucket contents
docker exec broker-edge-svc nats kv ls

docs.title: Clustering
docs.text:
Broker Edge supports leaf node connections on port 4443 for multi-node deployments. In a clustered configuration, leaf nodes connect to a central broker to form a unified messaging fabric. Clustering is configured through the wfa configure wizard and managed by the WFA daemon.

Warning

If broker-edge fails to start, all downstream services will be unable to communicate. Check docker logs broker-edge-svc for startup errors, and verify that ports 4223 and 4443 are not in use by another process.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Conductor configuration is managed through three layers: the node configuration file, environment variables, and NATS KV buckets for runtime settings.

docs.title: Node Configuration File
docs.text:
Path: /witfoo/configs/node.json

This file is generated by the wfa configure wizard and contains the primary node configuration. It is mounted read-only into all containers at /configs/node.json.

docs.title: Key Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description node_role integer Node role (12 = Conductor) node_hostname string System hostname node_ip string Primary IP address appliance_id UUID Unique appliance identifier org_id string Organization identifier (DNS-valid, lowercase) org_name string Organization display name broker_client_port integer NATS client port (default: 4223) broker_leaf_port integer NATS leaf/cluster port (default: 4443) broker_max_data_mb integer Maximum NATS data size (default: 1024 MB) local_metrics boolean Enable local Prometheus/Grafana stack export_metrics boolean Enable metrics export to Grafana Cloud offline_mode boolean Disable external network access auto_update boolean Enable automatic WFA package updates registry_fqdn string Container image registry hostname registry_namespace string Container image registry namespace branch string Image tag/branch to pull license string WitFoo license key console_fqdn string WitFoo Console hostname (optional) ca_path string Custom CA certificate path cert_path string Custom server certificate path key_path string Custom server key path client_cert_path string Custom client certificate path client_key_path string Custom client key path

Warning

The node.json file is written with permissions 0600 and contains sensitive information including the license key and broker credentials. Do not share this file or commit it to version control.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Each container receives configuration via environment variables set by WFA:

Variable Description WF_NODE_CONFIG_FILE Path to node.json inside the container (/configs/node.json) NATS_URL NATS broker connection URL (nats://broker-edge:4223) SECRET_KEY Session cookie encryption key (conductor-ui only) PORT HTTP listen port (conductor-ui, default: 8000) REVERSE_PROXY_MODE Enable reverse proxy headers (conductor-ui) DISABLE_TLS Disable TLS on the UI server (handled by reverse proxy)

docs.title: NATS KV Bucket Configuration
docs.text:
Runtime configuration for pipeline services is stored in NATS JetStream KV buckets. These are the primary mechanism for dynamic configuration changes without container restarts.

Bucket Service Content SERVERS signal-server Listener enable/disable, masquerading options INTEGRATIONS signal-client API credentials and connector settings, enable/disable PARSERS signal-parser Per-parser enable/disable state FILTERS artifact-filter Deduplication settings, predicate rules, STIX config EXPORTERS artifact-exporter Destination URLs, credentials, batch settings

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Service Protocol Direction 443 conductor-ui HTTPS Inbound (management) 514 signal-server TCP/UDP Inbound (syslog) 4223 broker-edge NATS Internal 4443 broker-edge NATS Inbound (leaf/cluster) 5044 signal-server TCP, or TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node Inbound (Beats) 5045 signal-server TCP (never TLS) Inbound (Beats) 6514 signal-server TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node (the configuration wizard's default); plain TCP otherwise Inbound (syslog) 7514 signal-server TCP; uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the node, as 6514 does Inbound (syslog with RFC 6587 octet counting: each message is sent as its length in bytes, a space, then the message, with nothing between messages) 8223 broker-edge HTTP Internal (monitoring)

docs.title: TLS Certificates
docs.text:
Certificates are stored in /witfoo/certs/ and mounted into all containers at /certs/:

File Purpose ca.crt Customer CA certificate (if provided) witfoo_ca.crt WitFoo embedded CA ca-bundle.crt Combined CA bundle (auto-generated) server.crt / server.key Server certificate and key client.crt / client.key Client certificate and key

docs.title: Production Deployment
docs.text: In production, Conductor is deployed as a WitFoo Appliance — a dedicated Linux server running the WFA (WitFoo Agent) daemon as a systemd service.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 LTS (AMD64)
  • Minimum 4 CPU cores and 8 GB RAM
  • Docker Engine installed
  • Network access to the container registry (or offline image loading)
  • WitFoo license key (or 15-day trial)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Install the WFA package:

    sudo apt install wfa

  2. Run the interactive configuration wizard:

    sudo wfa configure

    See the WFA CLI Reference for details on each configuration step.

  3. Start the WFA daemon:

    sudo wfa start

  4. Enable auto-start at boot:

    sudo wfa enable

WFA will pull container images, create containers, and start all services in dependency order.

docs.title: Service Dependency Order
docs.text:
WFA starts containers in the following order to satisfy inter-service dependencies:

  1. broker-edge — Must be healthy before any other service starts
  2. signal-server, signal-client, signal-parser — Connect to broker on startup
  3. artifact-filter — Consumes from signal-parser output
  4. artifact-exporter — Consumes from artifact-filter output
  5. conductor-ui — Connects to broker for configuration management

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text:
WFA monitors container health using Docker health checks. The broker-edge container includes a built-in health check:

nats server ping --server=nats://127.0.0.1:4223

Downstream services wait for broker-edge to report healthy before starting their connection attempts.

docs.title: Development Deployment
docs.text: For development and testing, Conductor can be deployed using Docker Compose.

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text:
# Build all service binaries
./scripts/conductor-build.sh all

# Build Docker images
docker compose -f docker-compose-conductor.yml build

docs.title: Running with Docker Compose
docs.text:
# Start all services
docker compose -f docker-compose-conductor.yml up -d

docs.title: External Network
docs.text:
The Docker Compose configuration uses an external network (witfoo-analytics-net) for integration with the WitFoo Analytics stack. Create this network before starting:

docker network create witfoo-analytics-net

docs.title: Volume Mounts
docs.text: Host Path Container Path Purpose /witfoo/configs /configs (read-only) Node configuration (node.json) /witfoo/certs /certs (read-only) TLS certificates /data /data Persistent data (NATS, SQLite) /logs /logs Service log files

docs.title: Metrics and Monitoring
docs.text: Monitor WitFoo Conductor pipeline health, performance, and resource usage through built-in metrics and dashboards.

docs.title: Real-Time Dashboard
docs.text:
The Conductor UI dashboard (/) provides real-time monitoring with four tabs:

  • Overview — CPU, memory, and disk usage gauges
  • Pipeline — Message throughput and pipeline stage counts
  • Service Status — Per-service health indicators
  • Container Status — Per-container resource usage

See Dashboard for detailed tab descriptions.

docs.title: Prometheus Metrics
docs.text:
Each Conductor service exposes Prometheus-compatible metrics:

Service Metric Prefix Key Metrics signal-server signal_server_ Messages received, bytes ingested, connection count signal-client signal_client_ API polls completed, records fetched, errors signal-parser signal_parser_ Messages parsed, parse duration, unknown count artifact-filter artifact_filter_ Messages filtered, duplicates detected artifact-exporter artifact_exporter_ Messages exported, batch count, export errors broker-edge nats_ Stream messages, consumer pending, bytes total

docs.title: Pipeline Stage Metrics
docs.text:
The primary throughput metric is pipeline_stage_count with labels:

  • stage: source_client, broker, filter, export
  • status: success, error, dropped

docs.title: Grafana Cloud Integration
docs.text:
Conductor supports metrics export to Grafana Cloud via the grafana-agent service:

  1. Enable "Local Metrics" during wfa configure (Step 10)
  2. Metrics are scraped from all services and forwarded to Grafana Cloud
  3. Pre-built dashboards available for pipeline throughput and service health

docs.title: Local Prometheus/Grafana Stack
docs.text:
For air-gapped or on-premises deployments:

# Prometheus: http://localhost:9090
# Grafana: http://localhost:3001 (admin/admin)

Enable the local metrics stack during wfa configure by selecting "Local metrics" in the optional features step.

docs.title: Key Metrics to Monitor
docs.text: Metric Warning Threshold Description Pipeline throughput < 100 msgs/sec Messages processed per second Parser unknown rate > 10% Percentage of unparsed messages Export error rate > 1% Failed export operations Disk usage > 80% wfa diag warns at this threshold Container memory > 90% of limit Risk of OOM kill

docs.title: Alert Configuration
docs.text:
Configure alerts through:

  1. Grafana Cloud — Alert rules on exported metrics
  2. Conductor UI — Service status warnings on the dashboard
  3. WFA Status — sudo wfa status shows recent errors from the systemd journal

Tip

Run sudo wfa diag regularly to verify all connectivity checks pass. This catches issues before they impact pipeline throughput.

docs.title: Parser Naming Convention
docs.text:
Parsers follow a vendor_product naming convention using lowercase with underscores. Examples:
