docs.title: Enabling and Disabling Parsers
docs.text: Parsers can be toggled on or off through the Conductor UI Parser Management page or by directly updating the NATS KV PARSERS bucket. Changes take effect within seconds without requiring a container restart.

docs.title: Signal Processing Pipeline
docs.text: The Conductor pipeline transforms raw log data into structured, export-ready security artifacts through four stages: ingestion, parsing, filtering, and export. All inter-service communication uses NATS JetStream for reliable, persistent message delivery.

docs.title: End-to-End Data Flow
docs.text:
graph TD
    subgraph Ingestion
        SS[Signal Server<br/>Push: Syslog, Beats, TLS]
        SC[Signal Client<br/>Pull: APIs, OAuth]
    end

    subgraph "NATS JetStream (Broker Edge)"
        RAW["artifacts.raw"]
        PARSED["artifacts.parsed"]
        UNKNOWN["artifacts.unknown"]
        ENRICHED["artifacts.enriched"]
        FINAL["artifacts.final"]
    end

    subgraph Processing
        SP[Signal Parser]
        AF[Artifact Filter<br/>Dedup + Enrich + Predicate]
    end

    subgraph Export
        AE[Artifact Exporter<br/>8 destinations]
    end

    SS --> RAW
    SC --> RAW
    RAW --> SP
    SP -->|matched| PARSED
    SP -->|unmatched| UNKNOWN
    PARSED --> AF
    AF -->|STIX enriched| ENRICHED
    ENRICHED --> AF
    AF -->|filtered| FINAL
    FINAL --> AE

docs.title: NATS JetStream Streams
docs.text:
All pipeline data flows through the DATA stream using a hierarchical subject pattern:

{applianceID}.data.artifacts.{stage}
Subject Stage Publisher Consumer Description artifacts.raw Ingestion signal-server, signal-client signal-parser Raw log messages as received artifacts.parsed Parsing signal-parser artifact-filter Successfully parsed and structured artifacts artifacts.unknown Parsing signal-parser Monitoring only Messages no parser could match artifacts.enriched Enrichment artifact-filter artifact-filter Artifacts with STIX threat intelligence added artifacts.final Filtering artifact-filter artifact-exporter Export-ready artifacts after deduplication and filtering

Additional streams support operational functions:

Stream Purpose EVENTS System events and status updates LOGS Centralized service log collection METRICS Pipeline metrics in Prometheus format STATUSES Service health and status reports

docs.title: Stage 1: Ingestion
docs.text:
Two services handle data ingestion using complementary models:

  • Signal Server (push) — Listens for incoming network connections on syslog, Beats, and HTTP protocols. Buffers incoming data and publishes to artifacts.raw.
  • Signal Client (pull) — Polls external APIs on configurable schedules using OAuth and API key authentication. Publishes collected events to artifacts.raw.

docs.title: Stage 2: Parsing
docs.text:
The Signal Parser consumes from artifacts.raw and runs each message through a three-stage internal pipeline:

  1. Format Detection — Identifies the log format (RFC3164, RFC5424, CEF, LEEF, JSON, Zeek) and extracts standard headers
  2. Parser Matching — Runs the message through the parsers (listed in the Integration Catalog) using fingerprint-based early exit optimization. The first parser whose fingerprint matches processes the message.
  3. Output Routing — Successfully parsed artifacts publish to artifacts.parsed; unmatched messages route to artifacts.unknown

Throughput Characteristics

The serial parser pipeline processes >2000 messages per second with 200+ active parsers. Optimized parsers achieve <2ms per message. The early exit pattern means most messages only test a few fingerprints before finding a match.

docs.title: Stage 3: Filtering
docs.text:
The Artifact Filter applies three processing steps:

  1. ProtoGraph Deduplication — Reduces redundant events using an 11-tuple hash (SenderHost, ClientIP, ServerIP, ServerPort, Protocol, UserName, FileName, StreamName, MessageType, Action, SeverityLabel)
  2. STIX Enrichment (optional) — Checks IPs, domains, and hashes against threat intelligence feeds
  3. Predicate Filtering — Applies rule-based inclusion/exclusion filters

docs.title: Stage 4: Export
docs.text: The Artifact Exporter consumes from artifacts.final and delivers artifacts to one or more configured destinations with batching, retry logic, and connector-specific formatting.

docs.title: Source → Flow → Sink Pattern
docs.text:
All pipeline services follow a consistent architectural pattern from the shared common library:

Component Role Example Source Extract data from an input NATS consumer, TCP listener, API poller Flow Transform data Parse, filter, enrich, format Sink Load data to an output NATS publisher, HTTP POST, file write

Each service implements the module.Connector interface with Setup() for configuration and Start() for the processing loop. Configuration is delivered at runtime via NATS KV buckets, enabling dynamic reconfiguration without container restarts.

docs.title: Signal Client (Pull Ingestion)
docs.text: Signal Client handles pull-based log collection from cloud services and security platforms. It polls external APIs on configurable schedules, collecting events and publishing them to the NATS artifacts.raw stream.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Signal Client follows the same Source → Flow → Sink pattern as Signal Server, but uses pull-based collection instead of push-based listeners:

  • Source — API poller (HTTP client with authentication)
  • Flow — Transform API responses to artifact format
  • Sink — NATS publisher to artifacts.raw subject

Each integration runs as an independent connector with its own polling schedule, credentials, and checkpoint tracking.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Scheduled Polling — Each connector polls on its own built-in schedule (from about once a minute to every few hours); only the Splunk connector has an interval you can set
  • Credential Management — Supports OAuth2, API keys, client ID/secret, and tenant-specific authentication
  • Checkpoint Tracking — Resumes from the last successful position to avoid duplicate collection
  • Rate Limiting — Respects API quotas and implements backoff on rate limit responses

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Signal Client is configured via the NATS KV INTEGRATIONS bucket. Each integration stores its configuration as JSON:

{
  "enabled": true,
  "integration_type": "microsoft_graph",
  "credentials": {
    "client_id": "...",
    "client_secret": "...",
    "tenant_id": "..."
  }
}

Integrations are managed through the Conductor UI Integrations page.

docs.title: Supported Integrations
docs.text:
Signal Client supports all 39 API-based integrations listed on the Integration Management page, spanning endpoint, cloud, network, identity, email, SIEM, infrastructure, and vulnerability management categories.

For vendor-specific setup instructions, see the Integration Guides.

Note

Configuration changes propagate from the Conductor UI to Signal Client within 5–10 seconds via the NATS KV watch mechanism. No container restart is required.

docs.title: Signal Parser Architecture
docs.text: The Signal Parser transforms raw log messages into structured security artifacts. It consumes from the artifacts.raw NATS stream, runs each message through a serial pipeline of parsers (listed in the Integration Catalog), and publishes results to either artifacts.parsed (successful) or artifacts.unknown (unmatched).

docs.title: Serial Parser Pipeline
docs.text:
The parser uses a five-service internal architecture:

  1. InputPipeline — Consumes from NATS, performs format detection (RFC3164, RFC5424, CEF, LEEF, JSON, Zeek), and broadcasts to the parser stage
  2. SerialParserPipeline — Processes messages through parsers serially with early exit optimization. When a parser's fingerprint matches, parsing executes immediately and no further parsers are tested.
  3. OutputPipeline — Routes parsed artifacts to artifacts.parsed and unmatched messages to artifacts.unknown
  4. SvcWatcher — Orchestrates startup: waits for all parsers to initialize before allowing the InputPipeline to consume messages
  5. 249 Connector Services — Configuration watchers that enable/disable individual parsers based on NATS KV state

docs.title: Parser Registry and Fingerprinting
docs.text:
Each parser implements the Parsable interface:

type Parsable interface {
    Fingerprint(draft *artifact.Draft) bool  // Can this parser handle the message?
    Parse(draft *artifact.Draft) error       // Extract structured fields
    LogSamples() []string                    // Test samples for validation
}

Fingerprinting is the key optimization. Each parser defines a fast check (typically a string match or regex on the program name or message prefix) that determines whether it can handle a given message. The serial pipeline tests fingerprints in sequence and stops at the first match, avoiding unnecessary work.

Early Exit Optimization

With several hundred parsers, the serial pipeline with early exit achieves ~99.6% reduction in processing operations compared to running all parsers on every message. Most messages match within the first few fingerprint tests.

docs.title: Worker Pool Configuration
docs.text:
The SerialParserPipeline uses configurable worker pools for parallel processing:

Environment Variable Default Description SERIAL_PARSER_WORKERS 10 Number of serial parser workers FORMAT_MAX_WORKERS 30 Format detection workers OUTPUT_ARTIFACT_MAX_WORKERS 10 Output transformation workers

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Throughput: >2000 messages/second with 200+ active parsers
  • Per-message latency: <2ms for optimized parsers
  • Success rate: 100% deterministic processing (zero message loss)
  • Buffer sizes: 20K event buffers for stable throughput

docs.title: Unknown Message Handling
docs.text:
Messages that no parser can match are published to the artifacts.unknown subject. These messages are available for monitoring and analysis to identify new log formats that need parser development.

# Check unknown message volume
docker exec broker-edge-svc nats stream info DATA | grep unknown

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Parser enable/disable state is managed via the NATS KV PARSERS bucket. Parsers can be toggled through the Conductor UI Parser Management page.

Warning

Parser connectors require valid configuration from the NATS KV bucket to function. If the broker is unavailable during startup, parsers will wait for configuration delivery before processing any messages.

docs.title: Signal Server (Push Ingestion)
docs.text: Signal Server handles push-based log ingestion from network sources. It listens on multiple protocols and ports, buffering incoming data before publishing to the NATS artifacts.raw stream for downstream processing.

docs.title: Listeners
docs.text:
Protocol Port Description Syslog UDP 514 Standard syslog over UDP (RFC3164/RFC5424) Syslog TCP 514 Standard syslog over TCP Beats/Logstash 5044–5045 Elastic Beats and Logstash Lumberjack protocol. 5044 uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node; 5045 never uses TLS Secure Syslog TLS 6514 Syslog over TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node (the configuration wizard's default); plain TCP otherwise TCP 7514 Syslog with RFC 6587 octet counting: each message is sent as its length in bytes, a space, then the message, with nothing between messages. Uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the node, as 6514 does.

Each listener runs as an independent connector following the Source → Flow → Sink pattern:

  1. Source — Network listener accepting connections on the configured port
  2. Buffer — Internal event buffer (5000 event capacity) for backpressure management
  3. Flow — Transforms raw network data into ArtifactRaw format
  4. Sink — Publishes to NATS JetStream on the artifacts.raw subject

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Signal Server is configured via the NATS KV SERVERS bucket. Each listener can be independently enabled or disabled through the Conductor UI Log Server page.

docs.title: Masquerading
docs.text: Signal Server supports protocol masquerading, which allows a listener to accept data in one format and tag it as another. This is useful when network devices send non-standard syslog formats or when protocol conversion is needed at the ingestion point.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• TCP timeout: 60 seconds (industry standard for log collectors)
  • Lumberjack protocol: Payload validation with 10 MB compressed limit and 4096 events per window
  • Non-blocking sends: All framers use non-blocking channel sends to prevent connection hangs
  • Buffer capacity: 5000 events per listener with backpressure management

Tip

When configuring network devices to send syslog to Conductor, use TCP (port 514) or Secure Syslog TLS (port 6514) for reliable delivery. UDP syslog may drop messages under high load since UDP provides no delivery guarantee.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This guide covers common issues, diagnostic procedures, and resolution steps for WitFoo Conductor deployments.

docs.title: WFA Diagnostics
docs.text:
Run wfa diag to verify connectivity and system health:

sudo wfa diag

This checks:

  • Grafana Cloud — metrics endpoint connectivity
  • WitFoo Intel — support and remote jobs
  • WitFoo Library — support pack upload
  • WitFoo Licensing — license validation
  • Docker Registry — container image access
  • Cassandra Seeds — database connectivity (port 9042)
  • Disk Usage — warns if any partition exceeds 80%

docs.title: Support Bundle
docs.text:
Generate a comprehensive support bundle with wfa support:

sudo wfa support

Collects 19 diagnostic categories including Docker state, system logs, Cassandra diagnostics, NATS stream info, network configuration, and extended service logs. Automatically uploads to WitFoo support if a license is configured.

docs.title: Services Not Starting
docs.text:
# Check service status
sudo wfa status

# Check container state
docker ps -a

# Check service logs
docker logs <container-name> --tail=100

docs.title: NATS Connectivity
docs.text:
If services cannot connect to the broker:

# Verify broker-edge is running
docker ps | grep broker-edge

# Check NATS streams
docker exec broker-edge-svc nats stream ls

# Check NATS server info
docker exec broker-edge-svc nats server info

docs.title: Parser Errors
docs.text:
If messages are not being parsed:

  1. Check the unknown stream for unparsed messages
  2. Verify parsers are enabled in the Conductor UI (/admin/settings/processors)
  3. Check signal-parser logs: docker logs signal-parser-svc --tail=200

docs.title: Memory Issues
docs.text:
On constrained nodes (8 GB RAM), containers may experience OOM kills:

# Check container memory usage
docker stats --no-stream

# Check system memory
free -h

Tip

For nodes with limited memory, consider reducing the number of enabled parsers and integrations.

docs.title: Integration-Specific Troubleshooting
docs.text: For issues related to specific data source integrations (authentication errors, rate limiting, missing data), see the per-vendor troubleshooting sections in the Integration Enablement Guides, or the shared Common Integration Troubleshooting page covering connection, authentication, rate limiting, and data flow diagnostics.

docs.title: Log Locations
docs.text: Source Location WFA daemon journalctl -u wfad Container logs docker logs <container-name> Container log files /logs/<service-name>/ NATS logs docker logs broker-edge-svc

docs.title: WFA CLI Reference
docs.text:
The wfa command-line tool manages WitFoo Appliances. All commands require sudo. This page describes WFA 2.5.3, the release that shipped with WitFoo Analytics 1.2.0, and WFA 2.5.4, which has the same commands.

Never run wfad --version

wfad is the WFA daemon, not a command-line tool. Running wfad --version starts a second daemon. To read the installed version, run sudo wfa version, rpm -q wfa or dpkg -s wfa.

docs.title: wfa configure
docs.text:
Interactive setup wizard that generates /witfoo/configs/node.json, and /witfoo/configs/analytics.json for Analytics roles. The wizard walks through these steps:

Step Prompt Details 1 License Configuration Cloud: fetched automatically. On-prem: enter a license key, or request a 15-day trial (company name, contact name, contact email, and acceptance of the EULA). The organization ID and name come from the license 1b Product Selection The WitFoo product and tier your license covers. It decides which roles the next step offers 2 Node Role Selection AIO + Conductor, AIO, Conductor, Processing Node, Data Node or Console. Hardware check warns if the host is below the role's minimum RAM and CPU — Appliance ID Keeps the existing appliance ID, or generates a new UUID 4 Network Configuration Node hostname and node IP (Enter auto-detects the IP) 5 Certificate Configuration Paths for client cert/key, server cert/key and CA cert (defaults under /witfoo/certs/) 6 Web UI Port & Protocol https (default, port 443) or http (port 80). Not asked on a Data Node 7 Admin Account Analytics roles: admin email (default admin@witfoo.com). All roles: a password of at least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes, entered twice 8 Optional Features Local metrics, offline mode, metrics export to WitFoo (no default) and auto-update. Console and Data Node: offline mode and auto-update only — Staff-requested jobs Whether WitFoo support staff may request jobs on this appliance. Default n on a new install — Remote Console URL Optional. Not asked on a Console node — Analytics Endpoint Conductor only: the Analytics receiver URL, for example https://<analytics-host>:8443 — Clustering Configuration Processing Node: data node addresses and the Cassandra password. Data Node: seed node IPs and listen address — Review Display all settings, then Save this configuration? (y/n)

After you confirm, the wizard writes node.json with mode 0600, starts wfad and shows the initialization progress.

sudo wfa configure

Re-running wfa configure keeps the MCP settings in node.json and your staff-jobs choice, but not trusted_proxies. See WFA Configure Wizard.

docs.title: wfa fetch
docs.text:
Claims a configuration built in the Console from a one-time URL, instead of running the whole wizard. It pulls the license, organization, product, role, registry and ports, then asks only for this machine's details (appliance ID, hostname, IP, certificates) and the admin password. The URL works once. With no URL given, the command asks for it.

sudo wfa fetch <console-configuration-url>
Flag Description --url Console configuration URL (may include the token) --token One-time token, if the URL does not include it --insecure Skip TLS verification (self-signed Console certificate)

Like wfa configure, a re-run keeps the MCP settings and drops trusted_proxies.

docs.title: wfa user-reset
docs.text:
Resets the initial administrator account for the Analytics web UI from the appliance command line. Use it when nobody can sign in — a forgotten password, a mistyped email at setup, or an account that was deactivated.

sudo wfa user-reset

The command is interactive. It shows the existing initial admin account (email, username, name, organization, active state, and last login), offers to change the email address, then prompts twice for a new password with masked input:

Prompt Rules Change the admin email address? Optional. The email is the login username. Must contain @ and . and no spaces. An address already used by a different account is refused — the database does not enforce email uniqueness, and a duplicate would silently shadow one account at login New admin password Required. Minimum 8 characters, entered twice

If the account was deactivated, a successful reset also re-activates it.

The change is written directly to the Analytics database and takes effect at the next login — no service restart is required.

Which account this resets

It resets the initial admin account created when the appliance was provisioned — the one seeded as admin@witfoo.com. The account is identified by its fixed internal id rather than its email, so the reset still works if the email was changed earlier. Other user accounts are managed from Admin → Users in the web UI; see User Management.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Analytics roles only — aio, aio-conductor, processing, or data. On any other role the command exits with an explanation, because the Analytics web UI admin account does not exist there.
  • The Analytics stack must be running, since the command connects to the Analytics database using the credentials in /witfoo/configs/node.json. It waits up to 60 seconds for the database. If the database has never been seeded, start the stack once with sudo wfa start and retry.
  • An interactive terminal, because the password prompt is masked. It cannot be scripted or piped.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Message Cause and fix user-reset manages the Analytics web UI admin account, which does not exist on the "<role>" role You are on a Conductor, Console, or other non-Analytics node. Run it on the Analytics appliance error connecting to the Analytics database (is the analytics stack running?) The database is unreachable. Check sudo wfa status and start the stack with sudo wfa start Cassandra authentication failed The cassandra_password in /witfoo/configs/node.json no longer matches the database, or the database started in the last few minutes and has not set it yet. Wait until docker logs analytics-cassandra-svc prints Cassandra schema initialization complete, then retry Cannot resolve the Analytics database address On AIO, AIO + Conductor and Data nodes, WFA writes the database's name into /etc/hosts when wfad starts. Look for a [WARN] /etc/hosts was not updated line in the wfad log. On a Processing node, check the seed node addresses in node.json initial admin account not found — the Analytics database has not been seeded yet First-time appliance whose stack has not completed its first start. Run sudo wfa start, wait for the services to come up, and retry. The message also prints the steps to restore the initial administrator when the stack is already running failed to read password (user-reset requires an interactive terminal) The command was run without a TTY — for example over a non-interactive SSH command. Use an interactive session

Added in WFA 2.4.8. WFA 2.4.9 fixed a failure (Undefined column name theme) on appliances whose Analytics stack predates the per-user theme column — upgrade to 2.4.9 or later if you hit it.

Fixed in WFA 2.5.1 and later

  • wfa user-reset works on appliances whose Analytics database was created by Analytics 1.1.x. It no longer fails with Undefined column name sessions_valid_after.
  • It stops at once on a rejected database credential or an address it cannot resolve.
  • It always writes a password hash the 1.2.0 api can check. If an administrator could not sign in after wfa user-reset was run on a FIPS host under WFA 2.4.14 to 2.4.16, run wfa user-reset again once the appliance runs WFA 2.5.1 or later (install WFA 2.5.3) and the 1.2.0 images.

docs.title: wfa staff-jobs
docs.text:
Shows or changes whether WitFoo support staff can request jobs on this appliance. Staff-requested jobs are support packs, log collection, diagnostics, update-and-reboot and trust reset. Turning them off stops every one of them. Support packs you create and send yourself with wfa support are not affected.

sudo wfa staff-jobs status
sudo wfa staff-jobs off
sudo wfa staff-jobs on
Subcommand Description status Show whether staff-requested jobs are allowed, and which job types the setting covers off Turn staff-requested jobs off on Allow staff-requested jobs again
  • A new appliance starts with staff-requested jobs off. An appliance configured before WFA 2.5.1 keeps what it had.
  • The setting is staff_jobs_opt_out in node.json. Only this command, wfa configure and, on a new install, wfa fetch write it. Re-running wfa configure or wfa fetch keeps your choice.
  • The change takes effect when the wfad-helper service restarts. off and on restart it, unless a job is running in it.

Added in WFA 2.5.1.

docs.title: wfa mcp-relay
docs.text:
Turns the AI-connector relay on, keeps it acknowledged, shows its status, and turns it off. The relay gives an AI marketplace or MCP client an address that reaches this appliance's MCP endpoint through WitFoo, without an inbound port. It is off by default. Read MCP Relay, including the notice, before you turn it on.

Subcommand Description enable Show the notice and register this appliance's relay address. Needs a terminal ack Show the current notice and acknowledge it again after a notice version change. Needs a terminal status Show whether the relay is on, its address, its acknowledgement and what the relay reports off Revoke the relay address and turn the relay off. Asks you to type REVOKE; --yes skips the prompt in a script revoke The same as off

docs.title: Turning the relay on
docs.text:
sudo wfa mcp-relay enable
sudo wfa restart
  1. enable shows the notice. Only typing ENABLE turns the relay on; anything else, or Enter, leaves it off. No flag, variable, file or Console message can turn it on.
  2. enable registers the appliance, writes the address, credential and acknowledgement to node.json, and prints the address.
  3. If mcp_public_url is empty, enable sets it to the relay address.
  4. Run sudo wfa restart. wfad reads node.json only when it starts, so the relay carries nothing until the restart. The restart stops and starts every container on the appliance.

The relay needs the MCP HTTP transport (mcp_http_enabled); enable does not turn it on.

docs.title: Turning the relay off
docs.text:
sudo wfa mcp-relay off
sudo wfa restart

off clears the address only after the relay confirms the revocation. If the relay cannot be reached, the revocation stays pending and the command exits non-zero: run it again. A revoked address is never restored. Turning the relay on again gives a new address.

docs.title: Re-acknowledging the notice
docs.text:
When the relay notice changes version, a relay acknowledged at the old version stops. Run sudo wfa mcp-relay ack, read and acknowledge the new notice, then run sudo wfa restart. The address does not change. The relay accepts three acknowledgements for an address at once and then one a minute.

Offline mode

The relay stops while offline_mode is set, and wfa mcp-relay ack refuses. To resume after you clear offline_mode, run sudo wfa mcp-relay ack if asked, then sudo wfa restart.

Added in WFA 2.5.1.

docs.title: wfa status
docs.text:
Displays WFA version, wfad systemd service state, error count since start, and the last 10 error log entries from the journal.

sudo wfa status

docs.title: wfa diag
docs.text:
Runs connectivity and system diagnostics with formatted output:

Connectivity checks:

Check Target WitFoo Metrics Metrics endpoint reachability WitFoo Intel intel.witfoo.com WitFoo Licensing licensing.witfoo.com Docker Registry Container image registry (if configured) Cassandra Seeds Port 9042 (if configured)

System checks:

Check Description Kafka Topics Topic health (Streamer roles) Disk Usage Warns at >80% utilization

Output is a formatted table with check name, result, and status (pass/fail).

sudo wfa diag

docs.title: wfa support
docs.text:
Generates a comprehensive support bundle with 19 diagnostic categories:

Category Contents Docker Inspect Container configuration details Docker PS Running container list Docker Logs Last 500 lines per container Docker Images Installed image list Journal Last 24 hours of systemd journal Disk Usage Filesystem utilization Hosts File /etc/hosts contents Users System user list Var Log Regular files under /var/log (500 MB limit); what was left out is listed in COLLECTION-MANIFEST.txt Node Config /witfoo/configs/node.json, with credentials masked Cassandra nodetool (describecluster, ring, info, status, tablestats), CQL schema Netstat Network connections IP Route Routing table IPTables Firewall rules Listening Ports ss -tulpn output Docker Networks Network configuration NATS Server info, stream/consumer reports, KV bucket contents Pipeline Metrics conductor-ui API metrics, Docker stats Extended Logs Last 2000 lines per pipeline service

Output: support-{org_id}-{timestamp}.zip

The bundle uploads to WitFoo Intel (intel.witfoo.com) with the appliance's license key. Without a license, the file is saved locally. Support packs mask the MCP relay's handle and credential.

sudo wfa support

docs.title: wfa certs
docs.text:
Displays certificate status in a table format showing CA, server cert/key, and client cert/key with their source type (embedded, customer, or generated).

sudo wfa certs

Force re-extract embedded certificates and regenerate the CA bundle:

sudo wfa certs --refresh

Accept a changed CA fingerprint for a peer:

sudo wfa certs --accept-peer <host:port>

docs.title: wfa images
docs.text:
Offline container image management for air-gapped deployments.

List required images and their local availability:

sudo wfa images --list

Pull and save all required images to a tar file:

sudo wfa images --save

Output: /witfoo/images/{role}-images.tar

Load images from a tar file into Docker:

sudo wfa images --load

Offline Deployment Workflow

For air-gapped environments:

  1. On an internet-connected machine: sudo wfa images --save
  2. Transfer /witfoo/images/{role}-images.tar to the air-gapped node (USB, SCP, etc.)
  3. On the air-gapped node: sudo wfa images --load
  4. Start services: sudo wfa start

docs.title: wfa start
docs.text:
Starts the wfad systemd service. Enables the service if not already enabled.

sudo wfa start

docs.title: wfa stop
docs.text:
Stops the wfad systemd service and all managed containers.

sudo wfa stop

docs.title: wfa restart
docs.text:
Restarts the wfad systemd service, which triggers a full container lifecycle restart. wfad reads node.json only when it starts, so run wfa restart after you edit node.json by hand.

sudo wfa restart

docs.title: wfa enable
docs.text:
Enables the wfad service for automatic start at boot via systemctl enable wfad.

sudo wfa enable

docs.title: wfa reboot
docs.text:
Stops wfad and wfad-helper, runs system package updates (apt update and apt upgrade -y, or dnf upgrade -y on RHEL), then reboots the system. The reboot still runs if the package update fails.

sudo wfa reboot

docs.title: wfa version
docs.text:
Displays the installed WFA version, for example WFA 2.5.3.

sudo wfa version

docs.title: WFA Agent Architecture
docs.text: WFA (WitFoo Agent) is the systemd daemon that orchestrates all Conductor containers on a WitFoo Appliance. It manages the complete container lifecycle from image management through runtime monitoring.

docs.title: Container Lifecycle
docs.text:
WFA follows a deterministic startup sequence:

  1. Pull Images — Check the configured container registry for updated images, comparing SHA256 digests
  2. Create Containers — Configure each container with environment variables, volume mounts, port mappings, and network settings
  3. Start in Dependency Order — Launch containers respecting inter-service dependencies
  4. Monitor Health — Continuously check container health and restart failed services

docs.title: Dependency Order
docs.text:
broker-edge
    ├── signal-server
    ├── signal-client
    ├── signal-parser
    │       └── artifact-filter
    │               └── artifact-exporter
    └── conductor-ui

Broker Edge must be healthy before any downstream service starts. The WFA container manager polls every 60 seconds for image updates.

docs.title: Auto-Update Mechanism
docs.text:
When auto_update is enabled in node.json:

  • WFA configures Ubuntu's unattended-upgrades to include the WitFoo apt repository
  • System packages (including WFA itself) are updated hourly via systemd timer overrides
  • Container images are checked every 60 seconds against the registry
  • Updated images are pulled and containers are recreated automatically

Note

Container image updates are seamless — WFA compares SHA256 digests and only recreates containers when the image has changed. The startup dependency order is maintained during updates.

docs.title: Certificate Management
docs.text:
WFA manages TLS certificates with three source types:

Source Description Embedded Default WitFoo certificates compiled into the WFA binary Customer Customer-provided certificates configured in node.json Generated Auto-generated certificates for development environments

Certificate precedence: Customer certificates override embedded ones. The ca-bundle.crt is automatically generated combining all CA certificates.

All containers mount /witfoo/certs as /certs (read-only).

docs.title: Monitoring Integration
docs.text:
When export_metrics is enabled, WFA deploys a Grafana Agent container that:

  • Scrapes Prometheus metrics from pipeline services
  • Forwards metrics to Grafana Cloud
  • Streams service logs and journal entries

When local_metrics is enabled, WFA additionally deploys:

  • Prometheus (port 9090) — Local metrics collection with 24-hour retention
  • Grafana (port 3000) — Local dashboards for pipeline visualization

docs.title: Docker System Maintenance
docs.text: After all containers are confirmed running, WFA runs a Docker system prune in the background to reclaim disk space from stopped containers, unused networks, and old images.

docs.title: Log Shippers (Elastic Beats — OSS)
docs.text:
WitFoo Conductor accepts data from the open source (OSS) editions of Elastic Beats — Filebeat, Winlogbeat, and Packetbeat — as a push-based log source. The agents run on your endpoints and servers and stream events to the Conductor Signal Server using the Lumberjack protocol (the same wire protocol the Beats Logstash output speaks) on TCP 5044 / 5045.

This is different from the pull-based API integrations, where the Signal Client polls a vendor API. With Beats, the agent connects outbound to Conductor and pushes events as they are collected.

flowchart LR
    A["Filebeat / Winlogbeat / Packetbeat<br/>(OSS agent)"] -->|"Lumberjack · TCP 5044/5045"| B["Conductor<br/>Signal Server"]
    B -->|"artifacts.raw"| C["NATS JetStream"]
    C --> D["Signal Parser → WitFoo Analytics"]

Use the OSS (Apache 2.0) builds only

Elastic ships two distributions of Beats: the default distribution (Elastic License) and the OSS distribution (Apache License 2.0). WitFoo deployments standardize on the OSS builds.

Elastic stopped publishing OSS artifacts after the 7.x line — there are no -oss builds for 8.x or 9.x. The final OSS release line is 7.17.x (examples on these pages use 7.17.29; substitute the latest 7.17.x patch). Always install the package whose name ends in -oss (filebeat-oss, winlogbeat-oss, packetbeat-oss) or download an artifact with -oss- in the filename.

docs.title: Available Guides
docs.text: Beat Collects Platforms Guide Filebeat (OSS) Log files (syslog, app logs, auth.log, NDJSON, etc.) Linux, Windows Configure → Winlogbeat (OSS) Windows Event Logs (Security, System, Sysmon) Windows Configure → Packetbeat (OSS) Network metadata (DNS, HTTP, TLS, flows) Linux, Windows Configure →

docs.title: Step 1 — Enable the Beats listener in Conductor
docs.text:
The Beats/Logstash listener is managed on the Log Server Configuration page. It must be enabled before agents can connect:

  1. Open the Conductor UI → Admin → Settings → Log Servers
  2. Enable the Beats/Logstash connector (ports 5044–5045)
  3. The change is saved to the NATS KV SERVERS bucket and the Signal Server begins listening within seconds — no container restart required

Two ports, one protocol

Ports 5044 and 5045 both run the Lumberjack framer. Port 5044 uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node; port 5045 never uses TLS. With TLS disabled, use either one, or list both in your Beat output with loadbalance: true to spread connections across them. With TLS enabled, use 5044 alone, with ssl.

docs.title: Step 2 — Install the OSS build
docs.text:
The OSS packages are published from a dedicated Elastic oss-7.x repository and as standalone artifacts. Per-OS install commands are on each Beat's guide; the repository setup below is shared by Filebeat and Packetbeat on Linux. (Winlogbeat is Windows-only and is installed from the OSS .zip.)

Debian / Ubuntu (APT)RHEL / CentOS (YUM)Standalone artifact 
# Import the Elastic signing key
wget -qO - https://artifacts.elastic.co/GPG-KEY-elasticsearch \
  | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/elastic-7.x.gpg

# Add the OSS 7.x repository (Apache 2.0 builds only)
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/elastic-7.x.gpg] https://artifacts.elastic.co/packages/oss-7.x/apt stable main" \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/elastic-oss-7.x.list

sudo apt-get update
# then: sudo apt-get install filebeat-oss   (or packetbeat-oss)

sudo rpm --import https://artifacts.elastic.co/GPG-KEY-elasticsearch

sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/elastic-oss-7.x.repo > /dev/null <<'EOF'
[elastic-oss-7.x]
name=Elastic OSS repository for 7.x packages
baseurl=https://artifacts.elastic.co/packages/oss-7.x/yum
gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=https://artifacts.elastic.co/GPG-KEY-elasticsearch
enabled=1
autorefresh=1
type=rpm-md
EOF

# then: sudo yum install filebeat-oss   (or packetbeat-oss)

Download a specific -oss build directly (no repository required). See each Beat's guide for the exact filename, e.g.:

https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/filebeat/filebeat-oss-7.17.29-amd64.deb

docs.title: Step 3 — Point the output at Conductor
docs.text:
Every Beat ships to Conductor through the output.logstash block. Conductor is not Logstash, but its Signal Server implements the same Lumberjack protocol, so this is the correct output type:

output.logstash:
  hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
  # Load-balance across both listeners (optional; plain Beats only.
  # With TLS enabled on the node use 5044 alone, with ssl):
  # hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044", "<conductor-host>:5045"]
  # loadbalance: true

# Not shipping to Elasticsearch/Kibana — skip their setup paths.
setup.template.enabled: false
setup.ilm.enabled: false
setup.dashboards.enabled: false

Transport security (TLS)

Port 5044 follows the Conductor node's TLS setting. Port 5045 never uses TLS:

  • TLS disabled: both listeners accept plain TCP — use the configuration above with no ssl block.
  • TLS enabled (disable_tls: false on the node; the configuration wizard's default): port 5044 presents the appliance's server certificate (self-signed by default), so the Beat must connect with ssl.enabled: true. Port 5045 never uses TLS, so a Beat with ssl.enabled: true cannot use it. Do not list 5044 and 5045 in one output when TLS is enabled:
output.logstash:
  hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
  ssl.enabled: true
  # The appliance uses a self-signed certificate by default:
  ssl.verification_mode: none
  # Preferred: pin the appliance CA instead of disabling verification:
  # ssl.certificate_authorities: ["/etc/filebeat/conductor-ca.crt"]

Match the output to the node's setting — a TLS/plain mismatch shows up as a handshake error or an immediately dropped connection.

docs.title: Step 4 — Validate data flow
docs.text:
1. Validate the agent config locally (each Beat supports this):

    sudo filebeat test config -e        # syntax check
sudo filebeat test output -e        # connectivity to Conductor:5044

  2. Confirm Conductor is receiving — on the Conductor host:

    docker logs signal-server-svc --tail=50

  3. Search in WitFoo Analytics — open Signals → Search and look for artifacts from the agent's host. Filebeat/Winlogbeat events are auto-detected as Beats formats by the pipeline; Packetbeat flows arrive as Beats JSON.

docs.title: Connection refused / nothing arrives
docs.text:
• Confirm the Beats/Logstash connector is enabled in Log Servers (Step 1).
  • Verify the agent can reach the Conductor host on TCP 5044/5045 (firewall / security group).
  • Run <beat> test output -e on the agent — it reports the exact failure.

docs.title: TLS handshake error
docs.text:
• The node has TLS enabled but the Beat output has no ssl block (or vice versa). Align them (see the TLS note above). For a self-signed appliance certificate, set ssl.verification_mode: none or pin the CA.
  • A Beat with ssl.enabled: true cannot use port 5045, which never uses TLS. With TLS enabled on the node, send to 5044 only.

docs.title: Confirm you installed the OSS build
docs.text:
• The package name must end in -oss, or the artifact filename must contain -oss-. OSS builds exclude X-Pack; the output.logstash path and all core inputs used here are fully present.

See also: Signal Server · Log Server Configuration · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Filebeat (OSS)
docs.text:
Filebeat is a lightweight shipper for log files — syslog, authentication logs, web/application logs, and structured (NDJSON) logs. The OSS edition streams those events to Conductor over the Lumberjack protocol.

Category Push Ingestion (Log Shipper) Protocol Lumberjack (Beats Logstash output) Conductor Port TCP 5044 / 5045 Distribution OSS — Apache License 2.0 (filebeat-oss) OSS Release Line 7.17.x (final OSS line; examples use 7.17.29) Platforms Linux, Windows Vendor Docs Filebeat Reference 7.17

OSS only

Install filebeat-oss (Apache 2.0). There is no -oss build for 8.x/9.x — use the 7.17.x line. See the overview for the full rationale.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The Beats/Logstash listener is enabled in Conductor (Log Servers)
  • The agent host can reach the Conductor host on TCP 5044/5045
  • Root/Administrator on the host where Filebeat runs

docs.title: Step 1 — Install the OSS build
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / CentOSLinux tar.gzWindows

Using the OSS repository (see overview Step 2):

sudo apt-get install filebeat-oss

Or install a standalone artifact:

curl -L -O https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/filebeat/filebeat-oss-7.17.29-amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i filebeat-oss-7.17.29-amd64.deb

Using the OSS repository:

sudo yum install filebeat-oss

Or install a standalone artifact:

curl -L -O https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/filebeat/filebeat-oss-7.17.29-x86_64.rpm
sudo rpm -vi filebeat-oss-7.17.29-x86_64.rpm

curl -L -O https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/filebeat/filebeat-oss-7.17.29-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzvf filebeat-oss-7.17.29-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd filebeat-oss-7.17.29-linux-x86_64

# Run as Administrator
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/filebeat/filebeat-oss-7.17.29-windows-x86_64.zip -OutFile filebeat-oss.zip
Expand-Archive .\filebeat-oss.zip -DestinationPath 'C:\Program Files\'
Rename-Item 'C:\Program Files\filebeat-oss-7.17.29-windows-x86_64' 'Filebeat'
cd 'C:\Program Files\Filebeat'
.\install-service-filebeat.ps1

Confirm the OSS build installed:

filebeat version
# filebeat version 7.17.29 (amd64), libbeat 7.17.29 ...

docs.title: Step 2 — Configure filebeat.yml
docs.text:
Replace the package default at /etc/filebeat/filebeat.yml (Linux) or C:\Program Files\Filebeat\filebeat.yml (Windows) with a Conductor-focused configuration:

# ============================================================
# filebeat.yml — OSS build, ships to WitFoo Conductor
# ============================================================

# ----------------------------- Inputs -----------------------
filebeat.inputs:
  - type: filestream
    id: system-logs
    enabled: true
    paths:
      - /var/log/syslog
      - /var/log/auth.log
      - /var/log/messages
      - /var/log/secure

  # Example: a structured (NDJSON) application log
  - type: filestream
    id: app-json
    enabled: false
    paths:
      - /var/log/myapp/*.json
    parsers:
      - ndjson:
          target: ""
          add_error_key: true

# ----------------------------- Output -----------------------
# Conductor's Signal Server speaks the Lumberjack protocol used by the
# Beats Logstash output. Point output.logstash at the Conductor host.
output.logstash:
  hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
  # Spread across both listeners (optional; plain Beats only.
  # With TLS enabled on the node use 5044 alone, with ssl):
  # hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044", "<conductor-host>:5045"]
  # loadbalance: true

# If your Conductor node runs with TLS enabled, uncomment:
# output.logstash:
#   hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
#   ssl.enabled: true
#   ssl.verification_mode: none   # appliance uses a self-signed certificate
#   # ssl.certificate_authorities: ["/etc/filebeat/conductor-ca.crt"]

# Not shipping to Elasticsearch/Kibana — disable their setup paths.
setup.template.enabled: false
setup.ilm.enabled: false
setup.dashboards.enabled: false

# ----------------------------- Logging ----------------------
logging.level: info
logging.to_files: true
logging.files:
  path: /var/log/filebeat
  name: filebeat
  keepfiles: 7
  permissions: 0640

Modules are available in the OSS build

OSS Filebeat still ships the bundled modules (e.g. system, nginx, iptables). Enable them with filebeat modules enable system and add filebeat.config.modules — they ship through the same output.logstash block. Only X-Pack features are removed from the OSS distribution.

docs.title: Step 3 — Validate and start
docs.text:
# Validate configuration and connectivity
sudo filebeat test config -e
sudo filebeat test output -e        # should reach <conductor-host>:5044

# Start the service
sudo systemctl enable --now filebeat        # Linux (package install)
# Start-Service filebeat                     # Windows

Then confirm delivery:

# On the Conductor host
docker logs signal-server-svc --tail=50

Open WitFoo Analytics → Signals → Search and filter for the agent's hostname. Filebeat events are auto-detected as the filebeat log format by the pipeline.

docs.title: test output fails with connection refused
docs.text: The Beats listener is disabled or unreachable. Enable Beats/Logstash in Log Servers and confirm firewall access to TCP 5044/5045.

docs.title: TLS handshake / EOF on connect
docs.text:
The node has TLS enabled but the output is plain (or vice versa). Add the ssl.* block shown above (self-signed → ssl.verification_mode: none), or disable TLS on the node. See the TLS note.

A Beat with ssl.enabled: true cannot use port 5045, which never uses TLS. With TLS enabled on the node, send to 5044 only.

docs.title: Events collected but not searchable in Analytics
docs.text:
Check that the input paths match real files and that Filebeat has read permission. filebeat -e in the foreground prints harvester activity per file.

See also: Log Shippers overview · Winlogbeat (OSS) · Packetbeat (OSS)

docs.title: Packetbeat (OSS)
docs.text:
Packetbeat captures network metadata off the wire — DNS queries, HTTP transactions, TLS handshakes, and connection flows — and ships it to Conductor over the Lumberjack protocol. It is a passive sensor: deploy it on a host that sees the traffic you care about (a server, or a box receiving a SPAN/mirror port).

Category Push Ingestion (Log Shipper) Protocol Lumberjack (Beats Logstash output) Conductor Port TCP 5044 / 5045 Distribution OSS — Apache License 2.0 (packetbeat-oss) OSS Release Line 7.17.x (final OSS line; examples use 7.17.29) Platforms Linux (libpcap), Windows (Npcap) Vendor Docs Packetbeat Reference 7.17

OSS only

Install packetbeat-oss (Apache 2.0). There is no -oss build for 8.x/9.x — use the 7.17.x line. See the overview.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The Beats/Logstash listener is enabled in Conductor (Log Servers)
  • The sensor host can reach the Conductor host on TCP 5044/5045
  • Packet-capture support: libpcap on Linux (pulled in by the package), Npcap on Windows
  • Root (Linux) / Administrator (Windows) — raw packet capture is privileged

docs.title: Step 1 — Install the OSS build
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / CentOSLinux tar.gzWindows

Using the OSS repository (see overview Step 2):

sudo apt-get install packetbeat-oss

Or install a standalone artifact:

curl -L -O https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/packetbeat/packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-amd64.deb

Using the OSS repository:

sudo yum install packetbeat-oss

Or install a standalone artifact:

curl -L -O https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/packetbeat/packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-x86_64.rpm
sudo rpm -vi packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-x86_64.rpm

curl -L -O https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/packetbeat/packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzvf packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-linux-x86_64

Install Npcap first (WinPcap-compatible mode), then:

# Run as Administrator
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/packetbeat/packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-windows-x86_64.zip -OutFile packetbeat-oss.zip
Expand-Archive .\packetbeat-oss.zip -DestinationPath 'C:\Program Files\'
Rename-Item 'C:\Program Files\packetbeat-oss-7.17.29-windows-x86_64' 'Packetbeat'
cd 'C:\Program Files\Packetbeat'
.\install-service-packetbeat.ps1

Confirm the OSS build:

packetbeat version
# packetbeat version 7.17.29 (amd64), libbeat 7.17.29 ...

docs.title: Step 2 — Configure packetbeat.yml
docs.text:
Edit /etc/packetbeat/packetbeat.yml (Linux) or C:\Program Files\Packetbeat\packetbeat.yml (Windows):

# ============================================================
# packetbeat.yml — OSS build, ships to WitFoo Conductor
# ============================================================

# --------------------------- Capture ------------------------
# "any" captures on all interfaces (Linux). On Windows, set the device
# index from: packetbeat devices
packetbeat.interfaces.device: any

# --------------------------- Flows --------------------------
packetbeat.flows:
  timeout: 30s
  period: 10s

# ------------------------- Protocols ------------------------
packetbeat.protocols:
  - type: dns
    ports: [53]
    include_authorities: true
    include_additionals: true

  - type: http
    ports: [80, 8080, 8000, 5000]

  - type: tls
    ports: [443, 8443]

  - type: dhcpv4
    ports: [67, 68]

# ---------------------------- Output ------------------------
# Conductor's Signal Server speaks the Lumberjack protocol used by the
# Beats Logstash output. Point output.logstash at the Conductor host.
output.logstash:
  hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
  # Spread across both listeners (optional; plain Beats only.
  # With TLS enabled on the node use 5044 alone, with ssl):
  # hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044", "<conductor-host>:5045"]
  # loadbalance: true

# If your Conductor node runs with TLS enabled, uncomment:
# output.logstash:
#   hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
#   ssl.enabled: true
#   ssl.verification_mode: none   # appliance uses a self-signed certificate
#   # ssl.certificate_authorities: ["/etc/packetbeat/conductor-ca.crt"]

# Not shipping to Elasticsearch/Kibana — disable their setup paths.
setup.template.enabled: false
setup.ilm.enabled: false
setup.dashboards.enabled: false

# ---------------------------- Logging -----------------------
logging.level: info
logging.to_files: true
logging.files:
  path: /var/log/packetbeat
  name: packetbeat
  keepfiles: 7

DNS and TLS are the high-value protocols

For security telemetry, DNS, TLS (SNI/cert metadata), and flows deliver the most value at the lowest volume. Add http only where you have plaintext HTTP worth inspecting. Packetbeat records metadata, not payloads.

docs.title: Step 3 — Validate and start
docs.text:
# Validate configuration and connectivity (capture needs root)
sudo packetbeat test config -e
sudo packetbeat test output -e        # should reach <conductor-host>:5044

# List capture devices if "any" is not suitable
sudo packetbeat devices

# Start the service
sudo systemctl enable --now packetbeat        # Linux (package install)
# Start-Service packetbeat                     # Windows

Then confirm delivery on the Conductor host:

docker logs signal-server-svc --tail=50

Open WitFoo Analytics → Signals → Search and look for flow/DNS/TLS artifacts from the sensor host. Packetbeat events arrive as Beats JSON.

docs.title: No events / "no devices found"
docs.text: Run sudo packetbeat devices and set packetbeat.interfaces.device to a real interface. On Windows, install Npcap in WinPcap-compatible mode before starting the service.

docs.title: Permission denied opening interface
docs.text:
Packet capture is privileged. Run under sudo/Administrator, or grant the Linux binary capture capability:

sudo setcap cap_net_raw,cap_net_admin=eip $(which packetbeat)

docs.title: test output fails with connection refused
docs.text: Enable the Beats/Logstash connector in Log Servers and confirm firewall access to TCP 5044/5045.

docs.title: Winlogbeat (OSS)
docs.text:
Winlogbeat ships Windows Event Logs — Security, System, Application, and Sysmon channels — to Conductor over the Lumberjack protocol. It is a Windows-only agent.

Category Push Ingestion (Log Shipper) Protocol Lumberjack (Beats Logstash output) Conductor Port TCP 5044 / 5045 Distribution OSS — Apache License 2.0 (winlogbeat-oss) OSS Release Line 7.17.x (final OSS line; examples use 7.17.29) Platforms Windows Vendor Docs Winlogbeat Reference 7.17

OSS only

Install the winlogbeat-oss ZIP (Apache 2.0). There is no -oss build for 8.x/9.x — use the 7.17.x line. See the overview.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The Beats/Logstash listener is enabled in Conductor (Log Servers)
  • The Windows host can reach the Conductor host on TCP 5044/5045
  • Administrator PowerShell on the Windows host
  • (Optional) Sysmon installed for richer endpoint telemetry

docs.title: Step 1 — Install the OSS build
docs.text:
Winlogbeat is distributed only as a Windows .zip. Run an elevated PowerShell:

# Download the OSS build (7.17.x — final OSS line)
Invoke-WebRequest `
  -Uri https://artifacts.elastic.co/downloads/beats/winlogbeat/winlogbeat-oss-7.17.29-windows-x86_64.zip `
  -OutFile winlogbeat-oss.zip

# Extract and place under Program Files
Expand-Archive .\winlogbeat-oss.zip -DestinationPath 'C:\Program Files\'
Rename-Item 'C:\Program Files\winlogbeat-oss-7.17.29-windows-x86_64' 'Winlogbeat'
cd 'C:\Program Files\Winlogbeat'

# Install the Windows service (does not start it yet)
.\install-service-winlogbeat.ps1

Confirm the OSS build:

.\winlogbeat.exe version
# winlogbeat version 7.17.29 (amd64), libbeat 7.17.29 ...

docs.title: Step 2 — Configure winlogbeat.yml
docs.text:
Edit C:\Program Files\Winlogbeat\winlogbeat.yml:

# ============================================================
# winlogbeat.yml — OSS build, ships to WitFoo Conductor
# ============================================================

# --------------------------- Event Logs ---------------------
winlogbeat.event_logs:
  - name: Security
  - name: System
  - name: Application
    ignore_older: 72h

  # Sysmon — include only if Sysmon is installed
  - name: Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational

  # PowerShell script-block logging (very useful for detection)
  - name: Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational
    event_id: 4103, 4104

# ---------------------------- Output ------------------------
# Conductor's Signal Server speaks the Lumberjack protocol used by the
# Beats Logstash output. Point output.logstash at the Conductor host.
output.logstash:
  hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
  # Spread across both listeners (optional; plain Beats only.
  # With TLS enabled on the node use 5044 alone, with ssl):
  # hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044", "<conductor-host>:5045"]
  # loadbalance: true

# If your Conductor node runs with TLS enabled, uncomment:
# output.logstash:
#   hosts: ["<conductor-host>:5044"]
#   ssl.enabled: true
#   ssl.verification_mode: none   # appliance uses a self-signed certificate
#   # ssl.certificate_authorities: ["C:\\Program Files\\Winlogbeat\\conductor-ca.crt"]

# Not shipping to Elasticsearch/Kibana — disable their setup paths.
setup.template.enabled: false
setup.ilm.enabled: false
setup.dashboards.enabled: false

# ---------------------------- Logging -----------------------
logging.level: info
logging.to_files: true
logging.files:
  path: C:\ProgramData\winlogbeat\Logs
  name: winlogbeat
  keepfiles: 7

Pick channels deliberately

Security is high-volume. For most deployments Security + System + Sysmon + PowerShell/Operational give strong detection coverage without flooding the pipeline. Use event_id and ignore_older to scope each channel.

docs.title: Step 3 — Validate and start
docs.text:
# From C:\Program Files\Winlogbeat (elevated)
.\winlogbeat.exe test config -c .\winlogbeat.yml -e
.\winlogbeat.exe test output -c .\winlogbeat.yml -e   # reach <conductor-host>:5044

# Start the service
Start-Service winlogbeat

Then confirm delivery on the Conductor host:

docker logs signal-server-svc --tail=50

Open WitFoo Analytics → Signals → Search and filter for the Windows hostname. Winlogbeat events are auto-detected as the winlogbeat log format by the pipeline.

docs.title: TLS handshake / EOF on connect
docs.text:
The node has TLS enabled but the output is plain (or vice versa). Add the ssl.* block above — for a self-signed appliance certificate set ssl.verification_mode: none or pin the CA. See the TLS note.

A Beat with ssl.enabled: true cannot use port 5045, which never uses TLS. With TLS enabled on the node, send to 5044 only.

docs.title: Sysmon channel not found
docs.text:
Winlogbeat logs failed to open ... Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational. Install Sysmon, or remove that entry from winlogbeat.event_logs.

See also: Log Shippers overview · Filebeat (OSS) · Packetbeat (OSS)

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
WitFoo Conductor collects security log data from cloud platforms, endpoints, identity providers, email security, network infrastructure, and more through pull-based API integrations. The Signal Client service polls each vendor's API on a configurable schedule and publishes artifacts to the processing pipeline. The Integration Catalog lists every pull connector, parser and exporter in this release.

Looking for log shippers / agents?

For push-based collection from Elastic Beats agents (Filebeat, Winlogbeat, Packetbeat — OSS builds), see the Log Shippers (Beats) guides. Those agents stream to the Signal Server over TCP 5044/5045 rather than being polled by the Signal Client.

Security platforms that push syslog, such as Nozomi Networks and Dragos, have their own Syslog Sources guides.

Routers, switches and firewalls that export NetFlow or IPFIX send to the NetFlow/IPFIX collector on UDP 2055; see Log Server Configuration.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Ensure you have the required vendor license and API access (see each guide's Prerequisites section)
  2. Create API credentials in the vendor console
  3. Open the Conductor UI → Integrations page
  4. Select the vendor from the Add Integration dropdown
  5. Enter your credentials and enable the integration
  6. Validate data flow within 1–2 polling cycles

docs.title: Common Configuration
docs.text:
All integrations share these common behaviors:

  • Polling Interval — Built into each connector and not configurable; each guide lists its connector's interval. Splunk is the exception: its form has a Poll Interval field (seconds). The SNMP Monitoring Poller and HTTP/HTTPS Monitor set an interval for each target
  • Checkpoint Tracking — Signal Client resumes from the last successful position after restarts, avoiding duplicate collection
  • Rate Limiting — Built-in respect for vendor API quotas with exponential backoff on HTTP 429 responses
  • Retries — A transient failure is re-attempted after 5, 10, 20, 40, then 60 seconds; a failure that waiting cannot fix (a credential, a setting or an endpoint) is retried after 15 minutes
  • Enable/Disable — Each integration can be toggled without removing its configuration

Configuration changes propagate within seconds via the NATS KV watch mechanism. No container restart is required.

See also: Integration Management · Signal Client · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Abnormal Security
docs.text:
Collects threat detection data from Abnormal Security, including business email compromise (BEC), phishing, account takeover, and other advanced email threats identified by Abnormal's behavioral AI platform.

Category Email Security Connector Name signal-client.abnormal-security Auth Method API Token (Bearer) Polling Interval 10 min (threats), 15 min (cases), 6 hr (posture); built in, not configurable Multi-Instance Yes Vendor Docs Abnormal Security API

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

Active Abnormal Security subscription with API access enabled. Admin role required to generate API tokens.

  • Active Abnormal Security subscription
  • Admin access to the Abnormal Security portal
  • Network: Conductor can reach api.abnormalplatform.com on port 443

docs.title: Step 1: Create API Credentials
docs.text:
1. Log in to the Abnormal Security Portal at https://portal.abnormalplatform.com/
  2. Navigate to Settings → Integrations
  3. Select REST API
  4. Click Generate Token
  5. Copy the generated API Token

Token Expiry

Abnormal Security API tokens typically expire annually. Set a calendar reminder to rotate the token before expiry to avoid data collection interruptions.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure in Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/integrations
  2. From the Add Integration dropdown, select Abnormal Security
  3. Enter a unique name for this instance

  4. Fill in the settings form:

    Field Value Description Host api.abnormalplatform.com Abnormal API endpoint API Key <your-api-token> Bearer token from step 1

  5. Toggle Enabled to on

  6. Click Save

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
After saving, verify the integration is working:

  1. Check connection status — The integration tile should show a green status indicator within 1–2 polling cycles

  2. Check Signal Client logs:

    docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=50 | grep "abnormal"

    Look for successful poll messages:

    [INFO] abnormal-security: fetched <N> threats

  3. Check artifacts in Analytics — Navigate to WitFoo Analytics Signals → Search and search for artifacts from this source

docs.title: Authentication Failed (401)
docs.text:
• Verify the API Token is correct and has not expired
  • Regenerate the token in the Abnormal Security portal if needed
  • Ensure the token was copied completely (no trailing whitespace)

docs.title: Forbidden (403)
docs.text:
• The token may belong to a user without sufficient permissions
  • Confirm the user has Admin access in the Abnormal Security portal

docs.title: Rate Limited (429)
docs.text:
• Abnormal Security enforces API rate limits based on subscription tier
  • The polling interval is built in and cannot be changed
  • Conductor automatically implements exponential backoff on 429 responses

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the integration shows Enabled in the Conductor UI
  • Check Signal Client logs for errors: docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=100
  • Verify threats exist in the Abnormal Security console for the polling window
  • Confirm network connectivity: curl -I https://api.abnormalplatform.com

See also: Integration Catalog · Integration Management · Signal Client · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Arista AGNI
docs.text:
Collects network identity and access data from Arista AGNI (formerly CloudVision Guardian), including user sessions, client connections, and network access events.

Category Identity & Access Connector Name signal-client.arista-agni Auth Method API Key (Bearer) Polling Interval 5 min (audit), 10 min (sessions), 15 min (clients); built in, not configurable Multi-Instance Yes Vendor Docs Arista CloudVision API

docs.title: Prerequisites

Vendor Requirements

Active Arista AGNI or CloudVision deployment with API access. Admin access required to generate API keys.

  • Active Arista AGNI / CloudVision subscription

docs.title: Step 1: Create API Credentials

  2. Navigate to Settings → API Keys

  4. Copy the API Key and note the API Value (secret)
  5. Record the Organization ID from the portal settings

Store Credentials Securely

  3. Enter a unique name for this instance

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
