docs.title: SNMP Monitoring Poller
docs.text:
Polls the network devices you list over SNMP v2c or v3 for interface counters, device health and reachability.

Category Infrastructure Connector Name signal-client.snmp-poll Auth Method SNMP v2c community, or SNMP v3 user (authPriv recommended) Polling Interval Per target: 60 s by default, 30 s minimum Multi-Instance Yes (up to 5) Vendor Docs RFC 3414: SNMPv3 User-based Security Model

This connector polls devices. It is separate from the snmpd parser, which reads the log lines of the snmpd daemon sent over syslog. SNMPv1 is not supported.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

Devices that answer SNMP v2c or v3, and access to their SNMP configuration.

  • SNMP v2c or v3 enabled on each device
  • For v3: a read-only SNMP user on each device
  • Network: Conductor can reach each device on its SNMP port (UDP 161 by default)

docs.title: Step 1: Create API Credentials
docs.text:
Create read-only SNMP credentials on each device. Use SNMP v3 with authPriv where the device supports it:

Setting Supported values Security level noAuthNoPriv, authNoPriv, authPriv Authentication protocol SHA, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512 (MD5 is not offered) Privacy protocol AES, AES-192, AES-256 (DES is not offered)

For SNMP v2c, set a read-only community string, and restrict which addresses may query the device to the Conductor's address.

Read-only access

The poller only reads. Give the user or community read-only access to the MIB views it needs, never write access.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure in Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/integrations
  2. From the Add Integration dropdown, select SNMP Monitoring Poller
  3. Enter a unique name for this instance

  4. For each device, fill in a target. Click Add Target to add another:

    Field Value Description Host 192.0.2.10 or switch1.example.com IP address or DNS name only: no scheme, no :port, no credentials Port 161 SNMP port, 1–65535 SNMP Version v3 v2c or v3 Community String (community) v2c only. Never logged Security Level authPriv v3 only Security Name (User) (user) v3 only Authentication Protocol SHA-256 v3 with authNoPriv or authPriv Authentication Passphrase (passphrase) v3 with authNoPriv or authPriv. Never logged Privacy Protocol AES-256 v3 with authPriv Privacy Passphrase (passphrase) v3 with authPriv. Never logged Poll Interval (seconds) 60 Minimum 30. A lower value is raised to 30 Collect HOST-RESOURCES-MIB (CPU / memory / storage) Off Also read CPU load and memory use

  5. Toggle Enabled to on

  6. Click Save

An instance holds up to 512 targets.

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
After saving, verify the integration is working:

  1. Check connection status — The integration tile should show a green status indicator within 1–2 polling cycles

  2. Check Signal Client logs. The poller writes one summary line per cycle:

    docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=50 | grep -i "snmp"

  3. Check artifacts in Analytics — Navigate to WitFoo Analytics Signals → Search and search for artifacts of stream snmp and message type network_monitor_event

docs.title: What It Collects
docs.text:
Group Objects SNMPv2-MIB sysUpTime, sysName, sysDescr IF-MIB ifTable Interface index, description, speed, admin and operational status, octets, errors and discards IF-MIB ifXTable (preferred) Interface name, 64-bit octet counters, high speed, alias HOST-RESOURCES-MIB (optional) Processor load and memory use
  • Only interfaces that are administratively up are reported, up to 1,024 interfaces per device.
  • The first poll after start-up reports status only: utilization needs two readings.
  • When a device restarts, its counters start again and that poll reports status only.
  • Monitoring polls never create work units.

docs.title: Device Reported Down
docs.text:
• A device that does not answer is reported as device_down. Reachability is data, not a pipeline error, so the other devices are still polled
  • Check that the Conductor can reach the device on its SNMP port
  • Check the community string, or the v3 user, protocols and passphrases

docs.title: Device Reported Degraded
docs.text: • A device that answers the basic objects but fails an interface or host-resources walk is reported as device_degraded, naming the part that failed. Check the device's SNMP view

docs.title: No Utilization Values
docs.text:
• Utilization appears from the second poll onwards
  • A device that reports no interface speed has no utilization percentage

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the integration shows Enabled in the Conductor UI
  • If every target fails, the connector backs off: check the Conductor's route to the management network
  • Check Signal Client logs: docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=100

See also: Integration Catalog · Integration Management · Signal Client · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Sophos Central
docs.text:
Collects endpoint protection and security event data from Sophos Central, including malware detections, web filtering events, and endpoint inventory.

Category Endpoint Security Connector Name signal-client.sophos-central Auth Method OAuth2 Client Credentials Polling Interval 10 min (alerts, audit), 1 hr (endpoints); built in, not configurable Multi-Instance Yes Vendor Docs Sophos Central API

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

Active Sophos Central subscription. Super Admin or Admin role required to create API credentials.

  • Active Sophos Central account
  • Super Admin or Admin role
  • Network: Conductor can reach id.sophos.com and regional API endpoints on port 443

docs.title: Step 1: Create API Credentials
docs.text:
1. Log in to Sophos Central at https://central.sophos.com/
  2. Navigate to Global Settings → API Credentials Management
  3. Click Add Credential
  4. Name the credential (e.g., "WitFoo Conductor")
  5. Assign the role: Service Principal ReadOnly (minimum required)
  6. Click Add
  7. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret

Region Auto-Discovery

Sophos Central uses a /whoami endpoint to automatically determine your regional API endpoint. Conductor handles this automatically — you only need to provide the Client ID and Client Secret.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure in Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/integrations
  2. From the Add Integration dropdown, select Sophos Central
  3. Enter a unique name for this instance

  4. Fill in the settings form:

    Field Value Description Client ID <your-client-id> From step 1 Client Secret <your-client-secret> From step 1

  5. Toggle Enabled to on

  6. Click Save

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
After saving, verify the integration is working:

  1. Check connection status — The integration tile should show a green status indicator within 1–2 polling cycles

  2. Check Signal Client logs:

    docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=50 | grep "sophos"

    Look for successful authentication and poll messages:

    [INFO] sophos-central: authenticated via OAuth2
[INFO] sophos-central: fetched <N> alerts

  3. Check artifacts in Analytics — Navigate to WitFoo Analytics Signals → Search and search for artifacts from this source

docs.title: Authentication Failed (401)
docs.text:
• Verify the Client ID and Client Secret are correct
  • Ensure the credential has not been deleted in Sophos Central
  • Check that the credential role has sufficient permissions

docs.title: Forbidden (403)
docs.text:
• The API credential may have insufficient role scope
  • Verify at least Service Principal ReadOnly is assigned

docs.title: Rate Limited (429)
docs.text:
• The polling interval is built in and cannot be changed
  • Conductor automatically implements exponential backoff

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the integration shows Enabled in the Conductor UI
  • Check Signal Client logs: docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=100
  • Verify events exist in Sophos Central for the polling window
  • Confirm network connectivity to id.sophos.com

See also: Integration Catalog · Integration Management · Signal Client · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Splunk
docs.text:
Collects search results from Splunk via the REST API, providing the ability to forward Splunk search results into WitFoo Analytics for correlated analysis alongside other security data sources.

Category SIEM Connector Name signal-client.splunk Auth Method Token or Username + Password Polling Interval 5 min by default (set in seconds in the form) Multi-Instance Yes Vendor Docs Splunk REST API Reference

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

Active Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud subscription. Admin access required to create API tokens or service accounts.

  • Active Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud deployment
  • Admin or equivalent role to create tokens/users
  • Network: Conductor can reach the Splunk management port (default 8089)

docs.title: Step 1: Create API Credentials
docs.text:
Token Authentication (Recommended)Username/Password Authentication
  1. Log in to the Splunk Web UI at https://<splunk-server>:8000/
  2. Navigate to Settings → Tokens (under Data)
  3. Click New Token
  4. Configure the token:
    • User: Select a user with search permissions
    • Audience: WitFoo Conductor
    • Expiration: Set per your security policy
  5. Copy the generated Token
  1. Log in to the Splunk Web UI at https://<splunk-server>:8000/
  2. Navigate to Settings → Access Controls → Users
  3. Click New User
  4. Configure the user:
    • Username: witfoo-conductor
    • Role: Assign a role with search permissions (e.g., user)
    • Password: Set a strong password
  5. Note the Username and Password

Store Credentials Securely

Splunk credentials grant access to your indexed data. Store them securely and do not share them in tickets or email.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure in Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/integrations
  2. From the Add Integration dropdown, select Splunk
  3. Enter a unique name for this instance (e.g., "Splunk Production")

  4. Fill in the settings form:

    Field Value Description URL https://<splunk-server>:8089 Splunk REST API endpoint Username witfoo-conductor Username (if using basic auth) Password <password> Password (if using basic auth) Auth Token <token> Bearer token (if using token auth) Custom Search index=main earliest=-15m Optional: custom SPL query Poll Interval 300 Seconds between searches (default 300; a value that is not a positive number falls back to 300)

  5. Toggle Enabled to on

  6. Click Save

Custom Search Queries

Leave the Custom Search field empty to use the default search, or provide a custom SPL query. The query runs on each polling cycle.

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
After saving, verify the integration is working:

  1. Check connection status — The integration tile should show a green status indicator within 1–2 polling cycles

  2. Check Signal Client logs:

    docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=50 | grep "splunk"

    Look for successful poll messages:

    [INFO] splunk: fetched <N> events

  3. Check artifacts in Analytics — Navigate to the WitFoo Analytics Signals → Search page and search for artifacts from this source

First Poll Timing

The first search runs within the configured poll interval after saving. With the default of 300 seconds, expect results within 5 minutes.

docs.title: Authentication Failed (401)
docs.text:
• Verify the credentials (token or username/password) are correct
  • For tokens, ensure the token has not expired
  • For Splunk Cloud, verify the REST API endpoint is correct

docs.title: Forbidden (403)
docs.text:
• The user or token may lack search permissions
  • Ensure the user has a role with search capability

docs.title: Rate Limited (429)
docs.text:
• Increase the Poll Interval (for example to 1800 seconds, 30 minutes)
  • Conductor automatically implements exponential backoff on 429 responses

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the integration shows Enabled in the Conductor UI
  • Check Signal Client logs for errors: docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=100
  • Verify network connectivity: curl -k -I https://<splunk-server>:8089
  • Test the search query directly in the Splunk Web UI
  • Ensure data exists in the target index for the polling time window

See also: Integration Catalog · Integration Management · Signal Client · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: LevelBlue USM Anywhere
docs.text:
Pulls alarms and events from the LevelBlue USM Anywhere platform (formerly AT&T Cybersecurity / AlienVault) through its API 2.0, using OAuth2 client-credentials authentication. This lets an MSSP or SOC ingest a USM Anywhere tenant's detections into WitFoo by provisioning a single API client credential — the managed LevelBlue collection agents keep shipping to USM Anywhere unchanged.

Category SIEM Connector Name signal-client.usm-anywhere-events Auth Method OAuth2 Client Credentials Polling Interval About every 60 seconds (built in, not configurable) Multi-Instance One instance per Conductor (see One instance per Conductor) API Base https://<subdomain>.alienvault.cloud/api/2.0 Vendor Docs LevelBlue: API Clients

Availability

This connector was introduced in WitFoo 1.1.0. Alarm and event field extraction is built against the LevelBlue USM Anywhere API 2.0 reference. If records from your tenant classify unexpectedly, contact WitFoo support with a sample so the mapping can be confirmed.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

An active USM Anywhere subscription whose edition includes the API (LevelBlue documents the API as available in the Standard and Premium editions) and permission to create an API client in your tenant.

  • Active LevelBlue USM Anywhere subscription with API access
  • A USM Anywhere API client (Client ID + Secret)
  • Your tenant subdomain — the bare DNS label from your USM Anywhere URL https://<subdomain>.alienvault.cloud
  • Network: Conductor can reach <subdomain>.alienvault.cloud on port 443

docs.title: Step 1: Create API Credentials in USM Anywhere
docs.text:
1. Log in to your USM Anywhere tenant
  2. In the USM Anywhere web UI secondary menu, select Profile Settings, open the API Clients tab and click New Client (menu names follow the LevelBlue documentation and can change between USM Anywhere versions)

  3. Copy the generated Client ID and Client Secret

    Protect the secret

    Treat the client secret like a password. Store it in your secrets manager and do not paste it into tickets or chat.

  4. Make sure the API client is enabled — the API Clients tab shows an enable toggle for each client

  5. Note your subdomain — the label before .alienvault.cloud in your tenant URL. For https://acme-soc.alienvault.cloud/, the subdomain is acme-soc

docs.title: Step 2: Configure in Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/integrations
  2. From the Add Integration dropdown, select LevelBlue USM Anywhere
  3. Enter a unique name for this instance

  4. Fill in the settings form:

    Field JSON key Required Default Notes Subdomain subdomain Yes — Bare DNS label only — do not include https:// or .alienvault.cloud. Must match ^[a-z0-9-]{1,63}$; the request host is always composed as <subdomain>.alienvault.cloud. Client ID client_id Yes — OAuth2 client id (sent as the HTTP Basic username during the token grant). Secret secret Yes — OAuth2 client secret. Masked in the form. Collect Alarms collect_alarms No true Poll /api/2.0/alarms. Collect Events collect_events No false Poll /api/2.0/events. Event Filter event_filter No — Optional events-only filter written as a URL query string, e.g. event_category=Application. Ignored when only alarms are collected. The connector sets page, size, sort and timestamp_occured_gte itself and removes them from the filter if present.

    Enable at least one source

    At least one of Collect Alarms or Collect Events must be enabled — the connector rejects a configuration where both are off.

  5. Toggle Enabled to on

  6. Click Save

Why a subdomain, not a full URL

The connector accepts only a DNS label and always composes the request host as <subdomain>.alienvault.cloud. This prevents a mistyped or hostile value from redirecting traffic to another host (SSRF protection), so a full URL, scheme, port, or path is rejected by design.

docs.title: What Gets Collected
docs.text:
Source Toggle WitFoo Classification Alarms collect_alarms Correlated SIEM detections (see below) Events collect_events Asset inventory for the observing host

Alarms are USM Anywhere's own correlated detections. WitFoo classifies each alarm by its rule_intent (kill-chain stage):

USM rule_intent WitFoo message type Reconnaissance & Probing network_scan Exploitation & Installation exploit_attempt System Compromise / Delivery & Attack malicious_behavior Any other / unset intent (e.g. Environmental Awareness) siem_event

Events classify as asset_inventory — the source host the event was observed on becomes the inventoried asset. Both sources are tagged with the usm_anywhere stream; a recognized USM record is never dropped as unknown.

Alarms feed work units

Because USM Anywhere alarms are the SIEM's own detections, WitFoo's default lead rules treat every collected alarm as a lead — including alarms that fall to the siem_event floor — and leads feed the incident correlation engine that builds work units. Events (asset inventory) match no default lead rule. If alarm volume is high, tune the alarm scope in USM Anywhere or collect events only.

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
After saving, verify the integration is working:

  1. Check connection status — The integration tile should show a green status indicator within a couple of minutes of saving

  2. Check Signal Client logs:

    docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=50 | grep "usm-anywhere"

  3. Check artifacts in Analytics — Navigate to WitFoo Analytics Signals → Search and filter for the usm_anywhere stream

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Polling — Each poll reads every enabled source (alarms, events). The next poll starts about 60 seconds after the previous one finishes. The interval is built in; there is no polling-interval setting for this connector
  • Checkpoint resume — At the end of a poll the connector saves its position for each source: an inclusive timestamp_occured watermark plus the UUIDs of the records already delivered at that timestamp. The next poll re-fetches from the watermark and skips those UUIDs, so a record that was already delivered is not delivered again. The position is saved when a poll ends, so a restart in the middle of a poll can deliver that poll's records again
  • Rate limiting and errors — On HTTP 429 the connector waits for the server's Retry-After time (kept between 1 second and 15 minutes) before its next poll. With no usable Retry-After, and after other temporary errors, it waits a random time that grows with each consecutive failure, up to 10 minutes
  • Per-poll page cap — A poll reads at most 500 pages (100 records each) for each enabled source. If a source is further behind than that, the connector logs a warning and the next poll resumes from the checkpoint; the cap delays records, it does not drop them
  • Redirect safety — All HTTP redirects are refused; the request host is always <subdomain>.alienvault.cloud

docs.title: One instance per Conductor
docs.text: The Conductor UI lets you add more than one instance of this connector, but every instance saves its position (its checkpoint) in the same file on the Conductor and loads that file when it starts. With two or more instances, an instance can start from another tenant's position, so records can be skipped or fetched again. Add one USM Anywhere instance per Conductor; an MSSP with several tenants should use a separate Conductor for each tenant.

docs.title: Coexistence With LevelBlue Agents and Beats
docs.text:
This connector pulls from the USM Anywhere API. It does not change how any data reaches USM Anywhere:

  • LevelBlue managed agents keep shipping to USM Anywhere unchanged. The connector reads the resulting alarms and events from the API — there is no need to re-point the managed collection agents
  • Beats / Windows Event Forwarding are unaffected. If you already forward logs to Conductor with OSS Filebeat / Winlogbeat or Windows Event Forwarding, that continues to work alongside this connector

Distinct from the USM Anywhere exporter

This ingest connector (usm-anywhere-events) is separate from the WitFoo outbound exporter integrations (usm-anywhere / alien-vault), which send WitFoo artifacts to an external system. Enabling this connector does not enable any exporter.

docs.title: Authentication Failed (401 or 403)
docs.text:
• Verify the Client ID and Secret were copied completely
  • Confirm the API client is still enabled in USM Anywhere (Profile Settings → API Clients) and has not been deleted
  • If in doubt, create a new API client in USM Anywhere and update the Conductor settings with its credentials

docs.title: Subdomain Rejected
docs.text:
• The Subdomain must be a bare DNS label (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) — do not include https://, a port, a path, or .alienvault.cloud
  • Example: for https://acme-soc.alienvault.cloud/, enter acme-soc

docs.title: Checkpoint Not Advancing
docs.text:
• Confirm records exist in USM Anywhere for the polled source in the current window
  • Check Signal Client logs for a page-cap warning — a large backlog drains over several polls by design
  • Verify the tenant clock and record timestamps are sane (a zero or missing timestamp_occured record is skipped)

docs.title: Rate Limited (429)
docs.text:
• The connector already waits for the server's Retry-After value before its next poll
  • Reduce the load: turn off Collect Events if you only need alarms, or narrow events with the Event Filter
  • If 429 responses continue, ask LevelBlue about the API rate limits for your tenant

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the integration shows Enabled in the Conductor UI
  • Confirm at least one of Collect Alarms / Collect Events is on
  • Verify the tenant subdomain is correct and reachable on port 443
  • Check Signal Client logs: docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=100

Credentials in logs

The connector's logger never writes the Client ID, Secret, or bearer token. If you enable the shared low-level request-tracing mode (DEBUG=1) for deep diagnostics, request headers may be written to disk — use it only in a controlled environment and clear the output afterward.

See also: Integration Catalog · Integration Management · Signal Client · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Zscaler ZIA
docs.text:
Collects web security and threat event data from Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), including web transactions, firewall logs, DNS logs, and threat events.

Category Network Security Connector Name signal-client.zscaler-zia Auth Method API Key + Admin Credentials Polling Interval 10 min (web), 15 min (firewall); built in, not configurable Multi-Instance Yes Vendor Docs Zscaler ZIA API

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

Active Zscaler Internet Access subscription. Admin access to ZIA Admin Portal. API access must be enabled for your organization.

  • Active ZIA subscription
  • Admin access to ZIA Admin Portal
  • API key from ZIA administration
  • Network: Conductor can reach your ZIA admin portal on port 443

docs.title: Step 1: Create API Credentials
docs.text:
1. Log in to the ZIA Admin Portal at https://admin.zs<cloud>.net/
  2. Navigate to Administration → API Key Management
  3. Copy the API Key displayed
  4. Note your admin email and password (used for API authentication)

ZIA Cloud Identifiers

Zscaler uses cloud-specific admin portal URLs. Select the correct base URL:

Cloud Admin URL Zscaler admin.zscaler.net ZscalerOne admin.zscalerone.net ZscalerTwo admin.zscalertwo.net ZscalerThree admin.zscalerthree.net ZscalerBeta admin.zscloud.net Zscaler Gov admin.zscalergov.net

Check your Zscaler documentation or account team if unsure which cloud you are on.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure in Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/integrations
  2. From the Add Integration dropdown, select Zscaler ZIA
  3. Enter a unique name for this instance

  4. Fill in the settings form:

    Field Value Description Base URL admin.zscaler.net ZIA admin portal URL (see table) API Key <your-api-key> From API Key Management Username <admin-email> Admin account email Password <admin-password> Admin account password

  5. Toggle Enabled to on

  6. Click Save

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
After saving, verify the integration is working:

  1. Check connection status — The integration tile should show a green status indicator within 1–2 polling cycles

  2. Check Signal Client logs:

    docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=50 | grep "zscaler"

    Look for successful poll messages:

    [INFO] zscaler-zia: authenticated, fetching events

  3. Check artifacts in Analytics — Navigate to WitFoo Analytics Signals → Search and search for artifacts from this source

docs.title: Authentication Failed (401)
docs.text:
• Verify the API Key, Username, and Password are correct
  • Ensure the admin account is not locked or disabled
  • Zscaler uses timestamp obfuscation for authentication; Conductor handles this automatically

docs.title: Wrong Cloud
docs.text:
• If you see connection errors, verify the Base URL matches your Zscaler cloud (see table above)
  • The base URL is different from the user-facing ZIA service URL

docs.title: Forbidden (403)
docs.text:
• The admin account may not have API access enabled
  • Contact your Zscaler admin to verify API access permissions

docs.title: Rate Limited (429)
docs.text:
• The polling interval is built in and cannot be changed
  • Conductor automatically implements exponential backoff

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the integration shows Enabled in the Conductor UI
  • Check Signal Client logs: docker logs signal-client-svc --tail=100
  • Verify web traffic is flowing through ZIA (check ZIA dashboard)
  • Confirm the admin portal URL is correct

See also: Integration Catalog · Integration Management · Signal Client · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Syslog Sources
docs.text:
Some security platforms push their events to WitFoo Conductor as syslog instead of being polled through an API. They send to the Conductor Signal Server, which listens for syslog on TCP and UDP 514 and on port 6514. Port 6514 uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node (the configuration wizard's default); plain TCP otherwise (see Log Server Configuration).

This is different from the pull-based API integrations, where the Signal Client polls a vendor API. With a syslog source, the platform connects to Conductor and pushes events as they happen.

flowchart LR
    A["OT security platform<br/>(Nozomi Networks, Dragos)"] -->|"CEF over syslog · TCP/UDP 514, 6514"| B["Conductor<br/>Signal Server"]
    B -->|"artifacts.raw"| C["NATS JetStream"]
    C --> D["Signal Parser → WitFoo Analytics"]

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Source Format Guide Nozomi Networks (Guardian, CMC) CEF over syslog Set up → Dragos Platform CEF over syslog Set up →

Prefer TCP or TLS

UDP syslog can drop messages under load because it has no delivery guarantee. Use TCP 514 or 6514 for alerts you need to keep.

See also: Signal Server · Log Server Configuration · Parser Catalog · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Dragos
docs.text:
Sends Dragos Platform notifications to WitFoo Conductor in Common Event Format (CEF) over syslog, so Dragos OT detections appear in WitFoo Analytics alongside the rest of your security data.

Category OT Security Collection Push: CEF over syslog Parser Dragos Platform parser Conductor Listener Syslog TCP or UDP 514, or Secure Syslog TLS 6514 Vendor Docs Dragos Platform Syslog Integration Guide, in the Dragos Customer Portal

Parser availability

This guide applies to a Conductor that has the WitFoo parser update which includes the Dragos Platform parser (stream name dragos_platform). A Conductor without it still receives these messages but does not parse them.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

A Dragos Platform deployment (SiteStore) and an account that can manage integrations and notification rules.

  • Access to the Dragos Platform Admin and Notification pages
  • Network: the Dragos Platform can reach Conductor on TCP 514 (or 6514). OT and IT networks are often separated by firewalls, so check the path first
  • The matching listener is enabled on the Conductor Log Server page

docs.title: Step 1: Enable the Syslog Listener on Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/log-servers
  2. Make sure Syslog TCP (port 514) is enabled. For encrypted transport, enable Secure Syslog TLS (port 6514). Port 6514 uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node (the configuration wizard's default); plain TCP otherwise

docs.title: Step 2: Add Conductor as a Syslog Server in Dragos
docs.text:
1. In the Dragos Platform, navigate to Admin → Integrations
  2. In the Syslog section, select LAUNCH
  3. Select ADD NEW SERVER, then enter Conductor's IP address or host name, the port of the listener you enabled in Step 1 and its protocol
  4. For TCP and TLS, set the message delimiter to newline. Conductor's TCP 514 and 6514 listeners read one record per line
  5. Select NEXT
  6. For the Message Template, use a CEF template whose header names Dragos and Platform as the vendor and product (CEF:0|Dragos|Platform|...), as in Dragos's own CEF examples. WitFoo recognizes Dragos messages by that header. The CEF text must start the message, after at most one standard syslog header, so do not add text of your own in front of it. A key=value or LEEF template is not recognized
  7. Select SAVE

docs.title: Step 3: Create a Notification Rule
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Notification → RULES and select NEW RULE
  2. Choose the notifications to forward, for example all detections, or detections above a severity you choose
  3. Set the action to send to the syslog server you added in Step 2
  4. Save the rule

docs.title: Step 4: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Wait for the next notification that matches the rule
  2. In Admin → Integrations, check that the syslog server shows as Connected
  3. In WitFoo Analytics, open Signals → Search and search for artifacts from the Dragos Platform's IP address, or for stream_name=dragos_platform (use the equals sign: a colon is a text match that can miss a quiet source on a busy system)

docs.title: What You Will See
docs.text:
• Each forwarded notification becomes an artifact. It records the assets the notification names, with an address, MAC address or host name where the notification gives exactly one value for it, the notification's summary as the rule name, and its severity, detection type and ATT&CK text as tags.
  • When the Conductor's optional deduplication is on, notifications that are alike (same sender, endpoints, type and severity) are combined, so there can be fewer artifacts than notifications.
  • A notification about one asset records that asset on the graph, when the notification gives an address for it. A connection between two assets appears only when the notification names both, each with an address.
  • Indicator, Modeling and Threat Behavior notifications are recorded as intrusion detection events, which WitFoo's detection rules score and can open work units from. A work unit opens only when the notification names both assets, each with an address, and the rule's conditions are met. On a licensed appliance those conditions include a syslog severity of 0 to 4 in the priority the Dragos syslog settings write; the common default (priority 134, severity 6) does not qualify. Configuration notifications are recorded as network monitoring events, which no built-in detection rule keys on, and are kept for search.
  • Other notifications, for example the platform's own sign-in notices, are recorded as generic events and kept for search.
  • Asset inventory, vulnerability and zone data from the Dragos Platform are not collected over syslog.

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• In Admin → Integrations, check that the syslog server shows as Connected
  • Check that the notification rule's criteria match the notifications you expect, and that its action sends to the Conductor server
  • Confirm the listener is enabled on the Conductor Log Server page and that the port is open between the OT network and Conductor

docs.title: Messages Arrive but Are Not Parsed
docs.text:
• Check that your Conductor has the parser update that includes the Dragos Platform parser
  • Check that the message template keeps the CEF header CEF:0|Dragos|Platform|... (see Step 2) and that nothing but one standard syslog header comes before it. A syslog header written without its structured-data field (RFC 5424 puts a - there) is not recognized either
  • If the messages that reach Conductor start with a number and a space (for example 123 <134>), the sender is framing records by length. Set it to end each record with a newline instead, or ask WitFoo support which listener to use
  • If the messages pass through a relay or log forwarder, send them straight from the Dragos Platform instead

Unrecognized log lines

By default, WitFoo appliances send log lines they cannot parse to WitFoo, redacted according to the appliance's redaction setting, to help build new parsers. Dragos messages that no parser recognizes, including all of them on a Conductor without the Dragos Platform parser, are such lines. If you do not want them sent, contact WitFoo support before you point the Dragos Platform at Conductor. A licensed appliance that is not in Offline mode also asks WitFoo for queued support jobs every 60 seconds; the released version has no setting specific to that channel.

See also: Syslog Sources · Signal Server · Log Server Configuration · Parser Catalog · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Nozomi Networks
docs.text:
Sends alerts, health events and audit events from Nozomi Networks Guardian sensors or the Central Management Console (CMC) to WitFoo Conductor in Common Event Format (CEF) over syslog. Conductor parses them with the nozomi_n2os parser, so OT alerts appear in WitFoo Analytics alongside the rest of your security data.

Category OT Security Collection Push: CEF over syslog Parser nozomi_n2os Conductor Listener Syslog TCP or UDP 514, or Secure Syslog TLS 6514 Vendor Docs Nozomi Networks: Common Event Format (CEF)

Parser availability

This guide applies to a Conductor that has the WitFoo parser update which includes the nozomi_n2os parser. A Conductor without it still receives these messages but does not parse them.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Vendor Requirements

A Nozomi Networks Guardian sensor or CMC running N2OS, and an administrator account on it.

  • Administrator access to the Guardian or CMC web console
  • Network: the Guardian or CMC can reach Conductor on TCP 514 (or 6514). OT and IT networks are often separated by firewalls, so check the path first
  • The matching listener is enabled on the Conductor Log Server page

docs.title: Step 1: Enable the Syslog Listener on Conductor
docs.text:
1. Open the Conductor UI at https://<conductor-ip>/admin/settings/log-servers
  2. Make sure Syslog TCP (port 514) is enabled. For encrypted transport, enable Secure Syslog TLS (port 6514). Port 6514 uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node (the configuration wizard's default); plain TCP otherwise

Prefer TCP or TLS

UDP syslog can drop messages under load. Use TCP 514 or 6514 for alerts you need to keep.

docs.title: Step 2: Add a CEF Endpoint in Nozomi
docs.text:
1. In the Guardian or CMC web console, select the gear icon in the top navigation bar to open Administration
  2. Under Settings, select Data integration
  3. In the top right, select Add
  4. From the Choose a configuration list, select CEF
  5. Enter Conductor's IP address or host name and the port of the listener you enabled in Step 1
  6. For encrypted transport, select TLS. To have the sensor check Conductor's certificate against a certificate authority, also select CA-emitted TLS certificate
  7. Save the endpoint

Send straight to Conductor

The parser reads CEF records as N2OS sends them, with or without a standard syslog header (RFC 3164 or RFC 5424). A relay or log forwarder that adds its own header or prefix in front of the record stops the parser from recognizing it. Point the Guardian or CMC directly at Conductor.

docs.title: Step 3: Validate Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Wait for the next alert or health event from the sensor
  2. In WitFoo Analytics, open Signals → Search and search for artifacts from the Guardian or CMC IP address, or for stream_name=nozomi_n2os (use the equals sign: a colon is a text match that can miss a quiet source on a busy system)
  3. Open an alert artifact and check that the source and destination assets, the rule name and the severity are filled in

docs.title: What You Will See
docs.text:
• Alerts become artifacts with the source and destination assets (IP address, port, MAC address and host name where Nozomi sends them), the protocol, the rule name and a severity derived from Nozomi's risk score. Nozomi's MITRE ATT&CK technique and tactic labels are kept as tags.
  • Audit events record the user name N2OS sends as the acting user and the appliance; what was changed stays in the message text.
  • Health events record the sensor's own status.
  • Alerts that Nozomi marks as security alerts are recorded as intrusion detection events, which WitFoo's detection rules score and can open work units from. Other alerts, such as a learned-behavior change or a link check, are recorded as network monitoring events, which no built-in detection rule keys on, and are kept for search. An alert that names only one node is recorded as that node, with no connection.
  • Audit and health events are kept for search; they do not open work units by themselves.
  • Asset inventory and vulnerability data from Nozomi's API are not collected over syslog.

docs.title: No Data Appearing
docs.text:
• Confirm the CEF endpoint is saved on the Guardian or CMC
  • Confirm the listener is enabled on the Conductor Log Server page and that the port is open between the OT network and Conductor
  • For TLS 6514 with CA-emitted TLS certificate selected, Conductor's certificate must be issued by a certificate authority the sensor trusts

docs.title: Messages Arrive but Are Not Parsed
docs.text:
• Check that your Conductor has the parser update that includes nozomi_n2os
  • If the messages pass through a relay or log forwarder, send them straight from the sensor instead (see Step 2)
  • Only one standard syslog header may come before the CEF text. A second header, a date written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, and a syslog header without its structured-data field (RFC 5424 puts a - there) are not recognized
  • If the messages that reach Conductor start with a number and a space (for example 123 <134>), the sender is framing records by length. Set it to end each record with a newline instead, or ask WitFoo support which listener to use

Unrecognized log lines

By default, WitFoo appliances send log lines they cannot parse to WitFoo, redacted according to the appliance's redaction setting, to help build new parsers. Nozomi messages that no parser recognizes, including all of them on a Conductor without the nozomi_n2os parser, are such lines. If you do not want them sent, contact WitFoo support before you point the sensor at Conductor. A licensed appliance that is not in Offline mode also asks WitFoo for queued support jobs every 60 seconds; the released version has no setting specific to that channel.

See also: Syslog Sources · Signal Server · Log Server Configuration · Parser Catalog · Common Troubleshooting

docs.title: Conductor UI Overview
docs.text: The Conductor UI is a web-based management interface for configuring and monitoring the Conductor pipeline. It provides real-time dashboards, service configuration, user management, and system health monitoring.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
The Conductor UI runs internally on port 8000 and is served externally via an HTTPS reverse proxy on port 443.

https://<conductor-hostname>/

Default Credentials

The default administrator account is:

  • Email: admin@witfoo.com
  • Password: F00theN0ise!

Change the default password immediately after first login via Account Settings (/account).

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text: Component Technology Frontend SvelteKit with Carbon Design System Backend Go with Echo framework Database SQLite (embedded) Real-time WebSocket with HTTP polling fallback (5-second interval) Session Encrypted cookies

docs.title: Route Table
docs.text: Route Purpose / Dashboard (4 tabs: Overview, Pipeline, Service Status, Container Status) /auth/login Authentication /account User profile and password settings /admin/users User Management /admin/settings/processors Parser Configuration /admin/settings/integrations API Integration Management /admin/settings/artifact-exporters Export Destination Configuration /admin/settings/log-servers Log Server Configuration /admin/settings/notifications Notification Management

docs.title: Real-Time Updates
docs.text:
The dashboard uses WebSocket connections for real-time metric streaming. A pulsating dot indicator in the UI shows the WebSocket connection status:

  • Green (pulsating) — WebSocket connected, receiving live updates
  • Gray — Disconnected, automatic fallback to HTTP polling at 5-second intervals

The UI implements automatic WebSocket reconnection with metrics throttling (250 metric cap) to prevent UI flooding during high-throughput periods.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
URL: /

The Dashboard provides real-time visibility into the Conductor pipeline through four tabs. All metrics update in real time via WebSocket connection, with automatic fallback to HTTP polling at 5-second intervals.

docs.title: Overview Tab
docs.text:
The Overview tab displays system-level health indicators:

  • Host Gauges — CPU core count, memory usage percentage, and disk usage percentage
  • Message Throughput — Counters showing messages processed per pipeline stage
  • Pipeline Stage Health — Status indicators for each stage (ingestion, parsing, filtering, export)

docs.title: Pipeline Tab
docs.text:
The Pipeline tab provides detailed pipeline performance metrics:

  • Time-Series Charts — Visualizations of pipeline_stage_count metrics over time
  • Message Flow — Real-time message flow through the pipeline
  • Stage Filters — Filter views by pipeline stage:
    • source_client — Ingestion stage
    • broker — Message broker
    • filter — Artifact filtering
    • export — Export stage

docs.title: Service Status Tab
docs.text:
The Service Status tab shows the health of each Conductor service:

  • Per-Service Health — Status derived from WFA report events
  • Error Indicators — Warning and error counts per service
  • Service Uptime — Time since last restart

docs.title: Container Status Tab
docs.text:
The Container Status tab displays Docker container metrics:

  • Per-Container CPU Usage — CPU utilization percentage for each container
  • Per-Container Memory Usage — Memory consumption for each container
  • Container Uptime — How long each container has been running
  • Container State — Running, stopped, or restarting status

docs.title: WebSocket Connection
docs.text: A pulsating dot indicator shows the real-time connection status. When the WebSocket connection drops, the UI automatically falls back to HTTP polling at 5-second intervals and attempts to re-establish the WebSocket connection.

docs.title: Exporter Configuration
docs.text:
URL: /admin/settings/artifact-exporters

The Exporter Configuration page manages the destinations where processed artifacts are delivered. Multiple exporters can be active simultaneously, each with independent configuration.

docs.title: Export Destinations
docs.text:
Exporter What it does WitFoo Analytics (HTTP) Sends artifacts over HTTP to the artifact receiver of a WitFoo Analytics appliance, each batch signed with an HMAC-SHA256 secret. On an all-in-one Conductor it is configured automatically Analytics Reporter (WebSocket) Sends artifacts to a WitFoo Analytics appliance over a secure WebSocket (TLS) connection Splunk Sends to a Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) endpoint OpenSearch Sends to an OpenSearch endpoint Microsoft Sentinel Sends to a Microsoft Sentinel workspace through the Data Collector API CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM Sends to CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM through an HEC / HTTP Event Data Connector USM Anywhere Sends batched JSON by webhook to LevelBlue USM Anywhere S3 Object Storage Writes compressed NDJSON objects to S3-compatible object storage Azure Blob Storage Writes compressed NDJSON blobs to Azure Blob Storage Google Cloud Storage Writes compressed NDJSON objects to Google Cloud Storage SCP Transfer Writes files up to a size limit and transfers them over SSH UDP Syslog Sends to a syslog server over UDP Local Filesystem Writes files up to a size limit to another directory or mount on the same machine

The Integration Catalog lists every exporter in this release.

Two ways to reach Analytics

WitFoo Analytics (HTTP) and Analytics Reporter (WebSocket) both deliver to a WitFoo Analytics appliance. Enable one or the other for an appliance: with both enabled, each artifact is delivered twice unless their filters or artifact sources differ. The page shows a warning when two enabled exporters deliver to the same host. It compares host names only, so two names for one machine are not caught.

docs.title: Enable/Disable Per Exporter
docs.text: Each exporter has an independent toggle. Multiple exporters can be active simultaneously to send artifacts to multiple destinations. An exporter you remove stays removed.

docs.title: STIX Enrichment Toggle
docs.text: A global toggle enables STIX threat intelligence enrichment for all exported artifacts. When enabled, the Artifact Filter's STIX enrichment stage adds threat indicator metadata before export.

docs.title: Filter Configuration
docs.text: Predicate-based filter rules can be configured to control which artifacts reach each exporter. This allows different destinations to receive different subsets of the artifact stream.

docs.title: OCSF 1.8 Export
docs.text:
The S3 Object Storage, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage and OpenSearch exporters have an Export Format field under Export Encoding:

Export Format Output Artifact JSON (default) The native WitFoo artifact shape, unchanged OCSF 1.8 Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework 1.8.0 class objects, for data lakes and SIEMs (for example AWS Security Lake, Tenzir and Splunk)

The OCSF mapping is applied when the artifact is exported. It does not change the artifact in the pipeline. An artifact that cannot be mapped is still exported, as an OCSF Base Event carrying the raw data.

docs.title: OpenSearch Auth Modes
docs.text: Mode Fields Required Basic Username, password API Key API key value None No authentication

docs.title: SCP Transfer
docs.text: Field Description Host Remote server hostname or IP Path Remote directory for file delivery Credentials SSH key or password Row Limits Maximum rows per exported file

docs.title: UDP Syslog
docs.text:
The syslog exporter sends over UDP only in 1.2.0. TCP and TLS syslog export are not available in this release.

All configuration changes are saved to the NATS KV EXPORTERS bucket and propagate to the Artifact Exporter service within seconds. The USM Anywhere, Azure Blob Storage and Google Cloud Storage settings save numbers and switches in the form their exporters read.

docs.title: Connector Health and Retries
docs.text:
The retry rules apply to the exporters and to the pull connectors of the Signal Client.

  • Transient failures are retried quickly. A connector whose run ends for a transient reason (the destination is down or busy, an HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx, a failed connection) is re-attempted after 5, 10, 20, 40, then 60 seconds. The ladder starts again after a run of 5 minutes.
  • Permanent failures wait 15 minutes. A failure that waiting cannot fix (a credential, a setting or an endpoint) is retried after 15 minutes.
  • The status says the real wait, for example re-attempting in ~40s. "Verify credentials/permissions" appears only for a failure that waiting cannot fix.
  • A busy receiver is waited for. When the Analytics receiver answers the two WitFoo Analytics exporters busy (503, 429 or another 5xx), the exporter waits, honouring Retry-After up to 30 seconds, and does not count it as a connector failure.
  • Refused batches are split. When the Analytics receiver refuses a batch from one of the two WitFoo Analytics exporters for what it holds (400, 413 or 422), the exporter divides the batch until it finds the artifact the receiver refuses. Three refused flushes in a row stop the instance with the receiver refuses every artifact it is sent; nothing is discarded.

docs.title: The decode_error Health Code
docs.text:
A connector that cannot decode what it was given reports the health code decode_error. It is a transient code: the connector keeps retrying. The Conductor UI explains it as follows:

The provider answered successfully but WitFoo could not decode the response — a WitFoo bug or a provider format change, NOT a credential or permission problem. No operator action: the connector keeps retrying. Report it if it persists across an upgrade.

The connector's own message is shown in the detail. A connector whose saved settings cannot be decoded (for example the SCP Transfer, Local Filesystem, Reporter or Abnormal Security settings) also reports decode_error, although no provider was contacted and the settings are not retried: read the connector's own message, which names the settings, and correct them.

docs.title: Integration Management
docs.text:
URL: /admin/settings/integrations

The Integration Management page configures pull-based API integrations for the Signal Client service. Each integration connects to an external cloud or security platform to collect log data on a scheduled basis.

Looking for step-by-step setup instructions?

See the Integration Guides for vendor-specific prerequisites, credential creation walkthroughs, and troubleshooting for the supported pull connectors.
