docs.text:
Vendor Integrations Microsoft Azure Security, Microsoft Sentinel, MS Defender Vulnerability Mgmt, Azure VNet Flow Logs Amazon Web Services AWS GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS VPC Flow Logs Google Cloud Google Cloud SCC, GCP VPC Flow Logs Oracle Cloud OCI VCN Flow Logs Cloudflare Cloudflare Cisco AMP, Duo, Meraki, Secure Access, Umbrella CrowdStrike Falcon Palo Alto Cortex Proofpoint CASB, Protect Deep Instinct Deep Instinct Druva Druva LimaCharlie LimaCharlie Mimecast Mimecast Netskope Netskope Okta Okta Splunk Splunk (search-based collection) Stealthwatch Stealthwatch Tenable Tenable DNS DNS Zone Transfer Monitoring SNMP Monitoring Poller, HTTP/HTTPS Monitor

The Integration Catalog lists every pull connector in this release.

docs.title: New in 1.2.0
docs.text:
Seven pull connectors are new, each with its own form on this page:

Connector Guide Cloudflare Cloudflare AWS VPC Flow Logs AWS VPC Flow Logs Azure VNet Flow Logs Azure VNet Flow Logs GCP VPC Flow Logs GCP VPC Flow Logs OCI VCN Flow Logs OCI VCN Flow Logs SNMP Monitoring Poller SNMP Monitoring Poller HTTP/HTTPS Monitor HTTP/HTTPS Monitor

The four flow-log connectors summarize flow records into network conversations with the same flow engine as the NetFlow/IPFIX collector on the Log Servers page.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Each integration has a dedicated settings form with vendor-specific fields:

docs.title: Common Fields
docs.text:
Field Description Enable/Disable Toggle Activate or deactivate the integration

Polling intervals are built into each connector and cannot be changed. The Splunk form is the exception: it has a Poll Interval field (seconds). The SNMP Monitoring Poller and HTTP/HTTPS Monitor forms also have a Poll Interval (seconds) field for each target.

docs.title: Authentication Fields (varies by vendor)
docs.text: Field Used By API Key / Token CrowdStrike, Mimecast, Netskope, Okta, Tenable, Cloudflare Client ID / Client Secret Microsoft, Cisco Duo, Cisco AMP, Proofpoint Tenant ID Microsoft integrations Workspace ID Microsoft Sentinel

docs.title: Connector Changes in 1.2.0
docs.text:
• Cisco Meraki — The connector reads events in the format Meraki documents, follows its paging, keeps its progress when a pass runs out of time, reports rate limits, and keeps going when one organization's networks are refused. A redirect is followed only over HTTPS on port 443, to one of the documented Meraki API hosts or a meraki.com subdomain.
  • DNS Zone Transfer — The connector asks the DNS server for each zone's SOA serial and transfers a zone only when the serial changed, could not be read, or the zone was last sent 12 hours ago or more. It polls every 60 minutes and transfers each zone over its own connection. A restart of the connector transfers every zone again. If the artifact filter's deduplication window is 12 hours or more, the 12-hour re-send is dropped as a duplicate.
  • One artifact per record — Connectors that pull a page or a poll of records (Cisco AMP, Umbrella and Meraki, Azure Security, Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk and Stealthwatch) give every record its own artifact id, so records that arrive together are no longer collapsed into one.
  • Rejected API keys — When a provider rejects the API key a connector sends (HTTP 401), the Signal Client reports the failure on that connector and keeps running.
  • Retries — A transient failure is re-attempted after 5, 10, 20, 40, then 60 seconds; a permanent one after 15 minutes. See Exporter Configuration.

Upgrade separate Conductors with Analytics

A Conductor on 1.1.5 or older sending to 1.2.0 Analytics keeps only about one record per page or poll for Azure Security, Microsoft Sentinel, Cisco AMP, Cisco Umbrella, Cisco Meraki, Splunk and Stealthwatch. Upgrade every Conductor at the same time as Analytics or before it.

docs.title: Status Tracking
docs.text:
Each integration displays:

  • Connection status — Whether the last poll was successful
  • Last poll time — When data was last collected
  • Error details — Description of any failures (authentication errors, rate limiting, connectivity issues), and a health code such as auth_failed, rate_limited or decode_error

Changes are saved to the NATS KV INTEGRATIONS bucket and take effect within seconds.

docs.title: Feed Approval
docs.text:
When a Conductor sends its first batch to Analytics, Analytics records it as a pending feed for an administrator to approve or reject.

  • An organization holds at most 1,000 pending feeds. A registration that would make the 1,001st is dropped; the feed registers again once feeds are decided or deleted.
  • A pending feed expires after 7 days and registers again, as a new one, when its Conductor next sends a batch.
  • Approving or rejecting a feed keeps the decision with no expiry. Pending feeds written by an earlier release have no expiry and stay until an administrator decides or deletes them.
  • The approval page lists at most 2,000 feeds of an organization. Delete old feeds to see the rest.
  • A decision on a feed that has expired answers 404.

docs.title: Log Server Configuration
docs.text:
URL: /admin/settings/log-servers

The Log Server Configuration page manages push-based log ingestion listeners for the Signal Server service. Each listener accepts incoming log data on a specific protocol and port.

docs.title: Log Server Connectors
docs.text:
Connector Port Protocol Description UDP/514 (Syslog) 514 UDP Standard syslog over UDP, in RFC 3164 or RFC 5424 format, one message per datagram. Each datagram is read whole. No delivery guarantee. TCP/514 (Syslog) 514 TCP Standard syslog over TCP, in RFC 3164 or RFC 5424 format, newline terminated. Reliable delivery with connection tracking. TCP/6514 (Syslog over TLS) 6514 TCP or TLS Syslog over TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node (the configuration wizard's default); plain TCP otherwise. Required for compliance environments. TCP/7514 (Syslog RFC6587) 7514 TCP or TLS Syslog with RFC 6587 octet counting: each message is sent as its length in bytes, a space, then the message, with no line ending between messages. Uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the node, as 6514 does. TCP/5044 (Beats with TLS), TCP/5045 (Beats No TLS) 5044–5045 TCP or TLS Elastic Beats and Logstash Lumberjack protocol for agent-based collection. Port 5044 uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node; port 5045 never uses TLS. UDP/2055 (NetFlow / IPFIX) 2055 UDP Binary flow records (NetFlow v5, v7, v9 and IPFIX) from routers, switches and firewalls. Off until you enable it. HTTP/8008 (Artifact Receiver) 8008 HTTP A WebSocket endpoint that receives artifacts from another Conductor. Off until you enable it.

Help text corrected in 1.2.0

The help text of the TCP/7514 listener now says it reads octet-counted frames. Earlier releases said its logs must be newline terminated, which was wrong. The UDP/514 help text no longer says logs must be newline terminated: each datagram is read whole.

docs.title: NetFlow and IPFIX Collector
docs.text:
The UDP/2055 (NetFlow / IPFIX) listener receives binary NetFlow v5, v7, v9 and IPFIX records. It decodes them, removes duplicates seen by several exporters, and summarizes them into one conversation artifact per client and server pair for every 60-second window. It is separate from the cisco_netflow and netflow_optimizer parsers, which read flow data sent as text over syslog.

To start collecting flows:

  1. Open Log Servers in the Conductor UI and enable UDP/2055 (NetFlow / IPFIX).
  2. Point your flow exporters at the appliance's UDP port 2055.

Things to know:

  • It is off by default. A new node leaves UDP/2055 and HTTP/8008 off. A node upgraded from 1.1.x has no NetFlow record, so UDP/2055 stays off until you switch it on.
  • No TLS or authentication. NetFlow over UDP is unauthenticated by protocol, the same trust posture as syslog on UDP/514. Restrict who can reach the port at your firewall.
  • Reachability on WFA appliances. WFA 2.5.1 and later publish 2055/udp on Conductor and AIO + Conductor appliances and open it in the host firewall. Under WFA 2.4.x the port is not published: upgrade WFA to 2.5.3, or publish it by hand.
  • Docker Compose. The compose files do not publish 2055/udp. Add 2055:2055/udp to the signal server's ports.
  • After a NATS data clear, the NetFlow listener is not restored. Enable it again under Log Servers.
  • Enable it after the node has started. If the NetFlow listener is the only enabled server when the node first starts, the classic syslog and Beats servers are not set up.
  • After a restart with a full flow-state store, the collector can read stale flow baselines.

HTTP/8008 on upgraded nodes

Releases before 1.2.0 turned HTTP/8008 on automatically, so a node upgraded from 1.1.x keeps it listening. The signal server logs opt-in module is enabled by its KV record at every start for such a listener. Switch HTTP/8008 off under Log Servers if nobody uses it.

docs.title: Enable/Disable Toggles
docs.text: Each log server connector has an independent toggle. Disabled connectors stop listening on their respective ports.

docs.title: Masquerading Options
docs.text:
Log server connectors support protocol masquerading, which allows a listener to accept data in one format and tag it as another protocol type. This is useful when:

  • Network devices send non-standard syslog formats
  • Protocol conversion is needed at the ingestion point
  • Legacy devices use unexpected port/protocol combinations

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Changes are saved to the NATS KV SERVERS bucket and propagate to the Signal Server service within seconds. No container restart is required.

Tip

For most deployments, enable UDP/514 (Syslog) for general syslog collection and TCP/6514 (Syslog over TLS) for devices that support encrypted transport. Port 6514 uses TLS when TLS is enabled on the Conductor node (the configuration wizard's default); plain TCP otherwise. Use the Beats listeners (ports 5044–5045) for environments with Elastic Beats agents deployed on endpoints.

docs.title: Sending from Elastic Beats
docs.text: To stream data from the OSS editions of Filebeat, Winlogbeat, or Packetbeat into the Beats/Logstash listener, see the Log Shippers (Beats) guides. They cover installing the OSS (Apache 2.0) builds and the example output.logstash configuration for each agent.

docs.title: Sending Syslog Out
docs.text: The syslog exporter (UDP Syslog on the Exporters page) sends over UDP only in 1.2.0. See Exporter Configuration.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
URL: /admin/settings/notifications

The Notifications page manages alerting channels and rules for Conductor system events. Configure email, Slack, and webhook destinations to receive automated alerts when pipeline issues occur.

docs.title: Notification Channels
docs.text: Channels define where notifications are delivered. Multiple channels can be active simultaneously.

docs.title: Email (SMTP)
docs.text: Setting Description SMTP Host Mail server hostname SMTP Port Mail server port (25, 465, 587) Username SMTP authentication username Password SMTP authentication password From Address Sender email address From Name Sender display name TLS Mode None, StartTLS, or TLS (minimum TLS 1.2) Recipients Comma-separated email addresses

docs.title: Slack
docs.text: Setting Description Webhook URL Slack incoming webhook URL Channel Target channel (e.g., #alerts) Username Bot display name

docs.title: Webhook
docs.text:
Setting Description URL HTTP endpoint for notification delivery Method HTTP method (POST, PUT, PATCH) Auth Type None or Bearer token Auth Token Bearer token value (when auth type is Bearer) Headers Custom HTTP headers as key-value pairs

Testing Channels

Click Test on any channel to send a test notification and verify connectivity before creating rules.

docs.title: Notification Rules
docs.text: Rules define which system events trigger notifications and to which channels they are routed.

docs.title: Event Types
docs.text: Event Description parser.failure Signal parser encountered a processing error exporter.failure Artifact exporter failed to deliver to destination system.capacity_warning Pipeline approaching capacity limits system.service_down A Conductor service is unreachable system.cert_expiring TLS certificate nearing expiration auth.failure Authentication attempt failed system.config_changed System configuration was modified

docs.title: Rule Configuration
docs.text:
Field Description Name Human-readable rule name Description Purpose of the rule Event Types One or more events that trigger this rule Channels One or more channels to notify Cooldown Minimum minutes between repeated notifications (default: 15) Enabled Toggle rule on/off

Cooldown

The cooldown period prevents notification storms. If the same rule fires multiple times within the cooldown window, only the first notification is sent. Subsequent events are recorded in the history as skipped.

docs.title: Notification History
docs.text:
The History tab displays a log of all notification attempts with:

Column Description Timestamp When the notification was attempted Event Type The triggering event Channel Target channel name Rule Rule that triggered the notification Status sent, failed, or skipped Message Event details or error message

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints require session authentication.

Method Endpoint Description GET /api/v1/notifications/channels List all channels POST /api/v1/notifications/channels Create a channel GET /api/v1/notifications/channels/:id Get channel by UUID PUT /api/v1/notifications/channels/:id Update a channel DELETE /api/v1/notifications/channels/:id Delete a channel POST /api/v1/notifications/channels/:id/test Send test notification GET /api/v1/notifications/rules List all rules POST /api/v1/notifications/rules Create a rule GET /api/v1/notifications/rules/:id Get rule by UUID PUT /api/v1/notifications/rules/:id Update a rule DELETE /api/v1/notifications/rules/:id Delete a rule GET /api/v1/notifications/history List notification history

Sensitive Fields

Channel credentials (passwords, tokens, webhook URLs) are redacted in API responses. To update credentials, include the new value in the PUT request body.

docs.title: Parser Management
docs.text:
URL: /admin/settings/processors

The Parser Management page provides control over the 200+ log parsers in the Conductor pipeline. Parsers can be individually enabled or disabled, and a master switch toggles all parsers at once.

docs.title: Master Switch
docs.text: A global toggle at the top of the page enables or disables all parsers simultaneously. When disabled, no log parsing occurs and all messages route to the artifacts.unknown stream.

docs.title: Individual Parser Toggles
docs.text: Each parser has a checkbox toggle for independent enable/disable control. Parsers are organized by category (firewall, IDS/IPS, authentication, DNS, cloud, endpoint, email, network, system).

docs.title: Parser Settings
docs.text:
• Settings are preserved when toggling parsers on and off
  • Changes propagate to the Signal Parser service within seconds via the NATS KV PARSERS bucket
  • No container restart is required for configuration changes

Race Condition Guard

The UI implements a guard against rapid clicks on parser toggles. This prevents race conditions where multiple configuration updates could conflict during propagation to the NATS KV bucket.

docs.title: Parser Categories
docs.text:
Parsers are displayed in a searchable, filterable table organized by:

  • Vendor — The product vendor (Cisco, Palo Alto, Microsoft, etc.)
  • Product — The specific product or log source
  • Status — Enabled or disabled

For a complete list of available parsers, see the Parser Catalog.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
URL: /admin/users

The User Management page provides administration of Conductor UI user accounts. On an all-in-one node, the page is reached at /conductor/admin/users through the Analytics web UI.

docs.title: Creating Users
docs.text:
New users are created with:

  • Username — The login identifier
  • Password — For local accounts
  • Display Name — Shown in the UI
  • Email — The account's email address
  • Role — Superuser, Admin, Staff or User
  • Auth Source — Local (password), SAML (SSO) or LDAP. The form defaults to Local (password)
  • Is Active — Whether the account can sign in

docs.title: Editing Users
docs.text:
Administrators can modify:

  • Display name
  • Email address
  • Role assignment
  • Auth Source
  • Is Active

The Users page lists each account's Auth Source in the Auth Mode column.

docs.title: Who Can Change Whom
docs.text:
• Only a Superuser can give an account the Admin or Superuser role, or deactivate an Admin or Superuser account.
  • No one can deactivate their own account.
  • A Superuser can edit any account except the one they are signed in to. An Admin can edit only Staff and User accounts.
  • The New User and Edit forms offer only the roles the signed-in user may give. A refused change shows the service's message and keeps the form open.

docs.title: Deactivating and Reactivating Users
docs.text:
Users are soft-deleted (deactivated) rather than permanently removed. The page provides two tabs:

Tab Content Active Currently active accounts with pagination Inactive Deactivated accounts that can be reactivated, with separate pagination

Saving a user as Inactive deactivates the account and ends the sessions it holds. Saving it Active again reactivates it. Inactive users cannot sign in.

docs.title: Authentication Modes
docs.text:
The Conductor UI supports four authentication modes, set under Conductor Admin > Settings > General in Authentication Mode:

Mode Description Local Users sign in only with their local credentials Local/LDAP (Mixed) Users sign in with their local or LDAP credentials SAML SSO Users sign in only through SAML single sign-on. Local sign-in is disabled Local/SAML (Mixed) Users sign in with their local credentials or through SAML single sign-on

docs.title: SAML Sign-In in 1.2.0
docs.text:
From release 1.2.0, Conductor UI SAML sign-in signs in only accounts whose Auth Source is SAML (SSO). An account whose Auth Source is Local or LDAP is refused, and the browser returns to the sign-in page with a generic SSO error.

This applies to a Conductor node that serves its own sign-in page. On an all-in-one node, Analytics signs users in, and this page does not apply.

How SAML sign-in finds the account:

  • The account is found by username: the identity provider's username attribute or, when the assertion carries none, the part of the e-mail address before @.
  • When the identity provider states an e-mail address and the account stores one, the two must match (case is ignored). Otherwise the sign-in is refused.
  • A username with no account creates a new SAML account with the Staff role.

Nodes in SAML SSO mode: convert accounts before you upgrade

In SAML SSO mode the server refuses every local sign-in. After the upgrade, an account left on Local or LDAP cannot sign in at all, a local administrator included. Convert the accounts before you upgrade a node whose Authentication Mode is SAML SSO.

docs.title: Before You Upgrade
docs.text:
On each Conductor node whose Authentication Mode is SAML SSO:

  1. Open Conductor Admin > Users.
  2. For each Local or LDAP account that signs in through SAML, edit the account, set Auth Source to SAML (SSO), and save. Converting an account does not stop it signing in by SAML on the release you are upgrading from.
  3. Make the Email stored on each of those accounts the address the identity provider asserts for that person. After the upgrade, a sign-in whose stated address differs from the stored address is refused.
  4. After each save, check that the account's Auth Mode column reads SAML.
  5. Deal with the Superuser accounts. The Users page does not let a Superuser change their own Auth Source, so a Superuser account is converted by a different Superuser. If the only Superuser is an account that signs in through SAML, do one of the following:
    • Create a second Superuser with the SAML (SSO) Auth Source and the username that SAML sign-in derives for another person. Sign in as that person and convert the first account.
    • Or set Authentication Mode to Local/SAML (Mixed) until the accounts are converted. In this mode an account that is still Local, and whose password you know, can sign in. Return to SAML SSO once the accounts are converted.

To pre-create an account for SAML sign-in, choose SAML (SSO) as the Auth Source in the New User form.

Converted accounts and passwords

An account converted from Local keeps its old password hash, but that password is not accepted while the account's Auth Source is SAML or LDAP, in every mode. Converting the account back to Local makes the old password valid again, so set a new password when you convert an account back.

docs.title: If the Node Was Upgraded First
docs.text:
If the node was upgraded before the accounts were converted, and no Superuser or Admin can sign in, the product offers no way back in through the UI. The way back is to change the Conductor UI database on the node:

  • The database is the SQLite file /data/local/collector.db on the host (/data/collector.db inside the Conductor UI container, which has no shell or SQLite client). Confirm the path on your node before you edit it, and back up the file first.
  • The edit needs an SQLite client on the host, and normally root.
  • Setting an account's auth_mode to saml in the users table converts it, and the change applies at once.
  • Setting auth_mode to mixed_saml in the system_settings table allows local sign-in again within 30 seconds, without a restart.
  • Setting an account's auth_mode back to local makes the password hash still in its row valid again. Set a new password afterwards.

docs.title: Account Settings
docs.text:
URL: /account

Individual users can manage their own account:

  • Profile Editing — Update display name and email
  • Password Change — Change password (local accounts only)

docs.title: Session Management
docs.text:
Sessions are managed via encrypted cookies. The session encryption key is configured via the SECRET_KEY environment variable.

SECRET_KEY values refused from 1.2.0

The Conductor UI refuses to start when SECRET_KEY holds a value an earlier release carried, the value the Console's example deployment files showed, or a value that is not a usable key. Before you upgrade, either unset SECRET_KEY, so the program keeps a key of its own in .secret_key beside its database, or set it to 64 hexadecimal characters (for example the output of openssl rand -hex 32). Keep .secret_key with the database: without it, the program generates a new key, which ends every session.

docs.title: WitFoo Console
docs.text: The WitFoo Console is the centralized management interface for multi-appliance WitFoo deployments. It provides fleet-wide visibility, appliance registration, and configuration management.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Component Technology Frontend SvelteKit with Carbon Design System Backend Go with Echo framework Database SQLite (embedded) Real-time WebSocket

docs.title: Appliance Management
docs.text:
• Register and monitor Conductor and Analytics appliances
  • View real-time health status across the fleet
  • Approve or reject appliance registration requests

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
• Local and LDAP authentication
  • Role-based access control (Administrator, Analyst, Viewer)
  • Session-based security with encrypted cookies

docs.title: Disconnected Network Support
docs.text:
• Self-hosted IBM Plex fonts for air-gapped deployments
  • No external CDN dependencies
  • All static assets bundled locally

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
The Console runs on the designated Console node and is accessed via HTTPS:

https://<console-hostname>/

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The Console is deployed as a Docker container managed by WFA:

ghcr.io/witfoo-dev/console-ui:main

For deployment configuration, see the WFA Integration guide.

docs.title: Configuration Generator
docs.text: The Configuration Generator is a secure, wizard-driven interface in the WitFoo Console for creating and provisioning initial appliance configurations. It provides a streamlined path for customers to generate custom configurations without direct access to configuration files, with all sensitive data encrypted and protected.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Configuration Generator reduces operational friction by automating the multi-step configuration process through an intuitive web interface. Generated configurations are delivered via secure, single-use URLs that expire after 72 hours, with additional protections including TLS-only transport, rate limiting, and encrypted storage.

docs.title: Key Benefits
docs.text:
• Simplified Workflow: Replace manual sudo wfa configure with a guided web wizard
  • Secure Delivery: Single-use URLs with 72-hour expiration and TLS encryption
  • Centralized Management: Administrators create configurations in the Console for remote appliances
  • Audit Trail: All generated configurations are logged and auditable
  • Error Prevention: Built-in validation ensures configurations are syntactically correct

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• User Role: ORG_ADMIN or above (to generate configurations)
  • WFA Version: 2.2.0 or later
  • Console Access: Web UI with HTTPS connectivity

docs.title: Configuration Wizard
docs.text: The Configuration Generator guides you through six sequential steps to define your appliance configuration.

docs.title: Step 1: Basics
docs.text:
Establish the foundation for your appliance.

Fields:

Field Type Example Required Organization Name Text Acme Corporation Yes Appliance Name Text analytics-prod-01 Yes Node Role Select Conductor / Analytics / Console Yes Deployment Type Select On-Premises / Cloud / Bare Metal No

Guidance:

  • Use descriptive appliance names that reflect the node's purpose and environment
  • Node role selection determines which services are installed and configured
  • Appliance names must be unique within your organization

docs.title: Step 2: Licensing
docs.text:
Choose your licensing model.

Options:

Trial License (15-day):

  • No license key required
  • Automatically generated during configuration
  • Expires after 15 days
  • Full feature access during trial period
  • Use case: Evaluation, proof of concept, testing

Existing License:

  • Paste your organization's WitFoo license key
  • Validates key format and expiration
  • Required for production deployments
  • Multiple keys can be imported for different appliances

Selection Process:

  1. Choose Trial or Existing License
  2. For existing licenses, paste the full license key (including -----BEGIN LICENSE----- markers)
  3. Console validates the key and displays license details: organization, expiration date, feature entitlements
  4. If validation fails, you can correct the key or switch to trial mode

docs.title: Step 3: Product & Role
docs.text:
Configure role-specific features and integrations.

For Conductor Nodes:

Feature Options Signal Parser Enable / Disable Parser Catalog Standard / Extended Artifact Exporter Enable / Disable Exporters Splunk / Elasticsearch / Syslog / Custom

For Analytics Nodes:

Feature Options Data Node (Cassandra) Primary / Replica / Disable Data Node Commitment Confirm storage and cluster participation AI/Chat Integration Enable / Disable Auditor Module Enable / Disable CyberGrid Integration Enable / Disable

For Console Nodes:

Feature Options Authentication Backend Local / LDAP / Okta High Availability Single-node / Multi-node cluster Backup Integration Enable / Disable

Selection Process:

  1. Review the available options for your selected node role
  2. Enable or disable optional features based on your deployment
  3. For integrations, select the relevant platforms you plan to use
  4. Proceed to the next step

docs.title: Step 4: Network & Features
docs.text:
Define network configuration and optional features.

Network Configuration:

Field Type Example Required Appliance Hostname FQDN analytics-01.corp.example.com Yes IPv4 Address IP 10.20.30.40 Yes IPv4 Gateway IP 10.20.30.1 Yes IPv4 Netmask Netmask 255.255.255.0 Yes DNS Servers IP (comma-separated) 8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4 Yes NTP Servers FQDN (comma-separated) ntp.ubuntu.com, ntp1.example.com Yes

Optional Features:

Feature Description Impact TLS Certificates Upload custom certificates or use self-signed Security, trust model HTTP Proxy For outbound connections in restricted networks Network connectivity Monitoring Enable Prometheus metrics export Observability Syslog Forwarding Forward logs to centralized syslog server Operational visibility High Availability Configure cluster mode (for Console) Redundancy, failover

Configuration:

  1. Enter your network details
  2. For security-critical deployments, upload custom TLS certificates
  3. Enable monitoring and logging features as needed
  4. Configure proxy settings if the appliance is behind an HTTP proxy
  5. Proceed to review step

docs.title: Step 5: Review
docs.text:
Verify all configuration details before generation.

Review Checklist:

  • Confirm organization and appliance names
  • Verify node role and role-specific features
  • Check all network parameters (hostname, IP, gateway, DNS)
  • Validate optional features are as intended
  • Ensure license is correctly selected

Actions:

  • Back: Return to previous steps to make changes
  • Edit [Step]: Jump to a specific step to modify details
  • Generate: Proceed to configuration generation

Configuration Validation

The Console performs comprehensive validation during review: - Hostname resolves correctly (for on-premises deployments) - IP address is valid and not already in use - Network parameters are consistent (CIDR notation verified) - License is valid and not already assigned - No conflicting configurations exist in the organization

docs.title: Step 6: Publish
docs.text:
Generate and deliver the configuration via a secure URL.

Generation Process:

  1. Configuration is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM
  2. A single-use URL is generated with 72-hour expiration
  3. The token is hashed before storage (plaintext not retained)
  4. Rate limiting (10 downloads per token) is applied
  5. TLS is enforced for all downloads

Output:

You receive:

  • Configuration URL: A secure, single-use link
  • Token Expiration: Exact time when the URL expires (72 hours)
  • QR Code: For easy sharing to the target appliance
  • Configuration Checksum: SHA-256 hash for integrity verification

Sharing the Configuration:

# Option A: Download and scp to target appliance
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://console.example.com/api/config/download/<config-id> > node.json
scp node.json witfooadmin@<target-appliance>:/tmp/

# Option B: Provide customer with URL for automated fetch
# See "Customer Deployment: wfa fetch" below

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: The Configuration Generator implements multiple layers of security to protect sensitive configuration data.

docs.title: URL Security
docs.text: Layer Implementation Benefit Single-Use Token valid for exactly one download; subsequent attempts fail Prevents credential leakage from URL logs 72-Hour TTL URL expires automatically; no manual cleanup required Limits exposure window for compromised URLs TLS-Only HTTP requests are rejected; HTTPS mandatory Encrypts data in transit Rate Limiting Maximum 10 downloads per token (covers retries/failures) Prevents brute force enumeration Rate Limiting (IP) Max 100 requests per IP per minute across all endpoints Prevents DoS attacks

docs.title: Data Protection
docs.text: Layer Implementation Benefit Encryption at Rest AES-256-GCM encryption of configuration files Protects data if database is compromised Token Hashing Tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes, not plaintext Even Console administrators cannot retrieve tokens Admin Password Collected locally on appliance, never sent to Console Admin credentials never traverse network Audit Logging All configuration generation/downloads logged with timestamp and IP Forensic trail for security reviews

docs.title: Client-Side Security
docs.text:
The appliance retrieves its configuration locally using the secure URL:

  1. Appliance downloads configuration file
  2. Configuration is verified against provided checksum (SHA-256)
  3. Encryption key is derived locally (never transmitted)
  4. Configuration file is written to /witfoo/configs/node.json
  5. WFA daemon validates syntax before activation

docs.title: Customer Deployment: wfa fetch
docs.text: Customers who receive a Configuration Generator URL can deploy it using the wfa fetch command.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Fresh appliance with WFA installed
  • Network access to the Console (HTTPS port 443)
  • SSH access to the appliance

docs.title: 1. Receive Configuration URL from Administrator
docs.text:
The administrator provides:

  • Secure configuration URL (valid for 72 hours)
  • QR code (optional, for mobile use)
  • Configuration checksum (for verification)

Example URL:

https://console.example.com/api/config/download/abc123xyz789

docs.title: 2. SSH to the Appliance
docs.text: ssh witfooadmin@<appliance-ip>

docs.title: 3. Run wfa fetch
docs.text: sudo wfa fetch https://console.example.com/api/config/download/abc123xyz789

docs.title: 4. Respond to Prompts
docs.text:
The wfa fetch command prompts for:

Prompt Input Notes Admin Email admin@example.com Default admin account for web UI Admin Password SecurePassword123! Stored locally; never sent to Console Confirm Network Settings yes/no Review auto-detected network config Confirm Role & Features yes/no Verify services to be installed

docs.title: 5. Configuration Validation
docs.text:
The appliance:

  • Downloads the configuration file over HTTPS
  • Verifies the checksum (SHA-256) matches
  • Validates syntax and references
  • Applies the configuration
  • Starts all services for the selected role

Sample Output:

$ sudo wfa fetch https://console.example.com/api/config/download/abc123xyz789
Downloading configuration...
Verifying checksum...
Parsing configuration...
Admin Email: admin@example.com
Admin Password: ••••••••••••
Confirm network: eth0 (10.20.30.40/24)? [yes/no] yes
Confirm role: Analytics with data node? [yes/no] yes
Applying configuration...
Starting services...
Configuration applied successfully. Access UI at https://10.20.30.40/

docs.title: 6. Complete Web UI Onboarding
docs.text:
Once wfa fetch completes:

  1. Navigate to https://<appliance-ip>
  2. Log in with the admin email and password from step 4
  3. Complete the 12-step onboarding wizard

docs.title: For Administrators: Creating a Configuration
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Configuration Generator
  2. In Console, go to Admin > Configuration

  3. Click Create New Configuration

  4. Complete the Wizard

  5. Step 1: Enter organization, appliance name, role
  6. Step 2: Choose trial or existing license
  7. Step 3: Select role-specific features
  8. Step 4: Enter network details and optional features
  9. Step 5: Review all settings

  10. Step 6: Generate and publish

  11. Distribute the URL

  12. Copy the secure URL or QR code
  13. Share with customer or deployment team

  14. Communicate expiration time (72 hours)

  15. Track Configuration

  16. Navigate to Admin > Configurations
  17. View list of generated configurations with status
  18. See download history and timestamps

docs.title: For Customers: Deploying a Configuration
docs.text:
1. Receive Configuration URL
  2. Administrator provides secure URL and expiration time

  3. Verify URL is from trusted Console instance

  4. SSH to Appliance

  5. Deploy a fresh WFA appliance image

  6. Connect via SSH as witfooadmin

  7. Run wfa fetch

  8. Execute sudo wfa fetch <url>
  9. Answer prompts for admin credentials and network confirmation

  10. Command downloads, validates, and applies configuration

  11. Access Web UI

  12. Open browser to https://<appliance-ip>
  13. Log in with admin credentials from wfa fetch

  14. Complete onboarding wizard

  15. Connect to Console

  16. Navigate to Appliance > Console Connection
  17. Follow prompts to establish trust and pair with Console
  18. Appliance appears in Console's Admin > Nodes after pairing

docs.title: Security Admonition
docs.text:
Configuration Generator Security Considerations

  • URL Expiration: Shared URLs expire after 72 hours. Keep administrative contact information current to ensure timely re-generation if needed.

  • Admin Password: The appliance collects and stores the admin password locally during wfa fetch. The password is never transmitted to the Console. Change this password immediately after first login to the web UI.

  • URL Sharing: Treat Configuration Generator URLs as sensitive as passwords. Do not share via unencrypted email or public channels. Use encrypted communication or QR codes.

  • Token Hashing: Even Console administrators cannot retrieve original tokens. If a URL is compromised, request the administrator generate a new one; the old URL automatically expires.

  • Audit Trail: Enable Console audit logging to track all configuration generations. Review logs periodically for unauthorized access attempts.

  • Air-Gapped Networks: For disconnected deployments, use the wfa configure command instead of wfa fetch. Configuration Generator requires HTTPS connectivity to the Console.

docs.title: URL Expiration
docs.text:
Problem: "This configuration URL has expired"

Solution:

  1. Contact your administrator
  2. Request a new configuration be generated
  3. Use the new URL within 72 hours
  4. Ensure system clocks are synchronized between Console and appliance

docs.title: Checksum Mismatch
docs.text:
Problem: "Configuration checksum verification failed"

Solution:

  1. Verify the configuration URL is correct (copy-paste carefully)
  2. Check for network interruptions during download
  3. Retry the wfa fetch command
  4. If problem persists, request a new configuration from administrator

docs.title: Network Configuration Errors
docs.text:
Problem: "Network configuration invalid: gateway not reachable"

Solution:

  1. Verify appliance network connectivity: ping <gateway-ip>
  2. Confirm IP address is not already in use: arp-scan -l
  3. Check DNS resolution: nslookup <hostname>
  4. In wfa fetch, select "no" at the network confirmation prompt and retry

docs.title: TLS Certificate Errors
docs.text:
Problem: "Cannot download configuration: certificate validation failed"

Solution:

  1. Verify Console's TLS certificate is valid and not expired
  2. Ensure appliance can reach Console's hostname (DNS resolution)
  3. For self-signed certificates, configure appliance to trust the certificate
  4. Contact your administrator for certificate troubleshooting

docs.title: Remote Node Lifecycle Management
docs.text: The WitFoo Console provides remote lifecycle management capabilities for Analytics and Conductor nodes directly from the web interface. This feature enables administrators to perform essential maintenance operations such as starting, stopping, restarting, upgrading, and pulling container images without direct SSH access to the appliances.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Remote node management is a key administrative feature that allows ORG_ADMIN and above to control node operations from a centralized location. This is particularly useful in multi-appliance deployments where direct access to individual nodes may be restricted or inconvenient.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• User Role: ORG_ADMIN or above
  • WFA Version: 2.2.0 or later
  • Node Status: Connected to the Console
  • Network: Bidirectional connectivity between Console and target node

docs.title: Accessing Node Management
docs.text:
To manage a node's lifecycle:

  1. Navigate to Admin > Nodes
  2. Click on the target node to open its details panel
  3. Select the Node Actions tab
  4. Choose the desired action from the available options

docs.title: Start Node
docs.text:
Starts a stopped or halted node.

  • Use case: Bringing a node back online after maintenance or planned downtime
  • Impact: Node services initialize and become available
  • Duration: Typically 2-5 minutes depending on role and configuration

docs.title: Stop Node
docs.text:
Gracefully stops all services on the node.

  • Use case: Planned maintenance or taking a node offline temporarily
  • Impact: All services shut down; node becomes unavailable
  • Duration: 30-60 seconds for graceful shutdown

docs.title: Restart Node
docs.text:
Performs a graceful restart of all services on the node.

  • Use case: Applying configuration changes or recovering from service issues
  • Impact: Temporary service interruption (2-5 minutes)
  • Cluster Impact: For Analytics data nodes, temporary Cassandra quorum adjustment during restart

docs.title: Upgrade Node
docs.text:
Upgrades the node to a new WFA version.

  • Use case: Deploying security patches, feature updates, or bug fixes
  • Impact: Services restart with new version; configuration is preserved
  • Duration: 5-10 minutes depending on services and role
  • Version Check: Console validates compatibility before upgrade

docs.title: Pull Images
docs.text:
Pulls the latest container images for all services on the node.

  • Use case: Ensuring the node has the most recent image builds without restarting
  • Impact: New images are downloaded; running services continue until explicitly restarted
  • Duration: 2-5 minutes depending on image sizes and network bandwidth

docs.title: Data Node Cluster Considerations
docs.text:
Data Node (Cassandra) Restart Impact

When restarting or upgrading an Analytics node configured as a data node (Cassandra), the following applies:

  • Quorum Impact: The node temporarily leaves the Cassandra cluster, reducing quorum availability
  • Confirmation Required: You must confirm cluster impact before proceeding with the restart or upgrade
  • Cluster Validation: The operation checks that the cluster can tolerate the node's absence
  • Multi-Node Clusters: In clusters with 3+ data nodes, quorum is maintained; in 2-node clusters, operations require explicit confirmation

docs.title: Job Result Tracking
docs.text:
Each remote management action creates a job that can be tracked in real-time:

  1. After initiating an action, a notification appears with a job ID
  2. Navigate to Admin > Jobs or Health > Jobs to view job status
  3. Click the job to view:
  4. Current status (Running, Completed, Failed)
  5. Start and end times
  6. Detailed logs from the WFA daemon
  7. Any warnings or errors encountered

docs.title: Job States
docs.text: State Description Running Action is in progress on the node Completed Action finished successfully Failed Action encountered an error; check logs for details Timeout Action did not complete within expected time window

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Maintenance Windows: Schedule node operations during low-traffic periods
  • Data Nodes: In production Cassandra clusters, coordinate data node restarts to maintain quorum
  • Sequential Operations: Allow previous operations to complete before starting new ones on the same node
  • Monitor Health: Check the Health dashboard after operations complete
  • Backup: For critical operations like upgrades, ensure recent backups are available

docs.title: Node Appears Disconnected
docs.text:
If a node shows as disconnected and you cannot perform actions:

  1. Verify network connectivity between Console and node
  2. Check the node's WFA daemon status: sudo wfa health
  3. Review Console logs for connection errors
  4. Restart the Console if the node remains unreachable

docs.title: Action Fails With Timeout
docs.text:
If an action times out:

  1. Check the node's actual status via SSH: sudo wfa [role] status
  2. Review the job logs in the Console for specific error messages
  3. Verify the node has sufficient disk space and resources
  4. Retry the operation during a lower-load period

docs.title: Cassandra Quorum Warnings
docs.text:
If you see quorum warnings when restarting a data node:

  1. Verify all other data nodes are healthy
  2. Ensure bidirectional connectivity between data nodes
  3. Check Cassandra cluster status via nodetool on one of the data nodes
  4. In 2-node clusters, explicitly confirm the restart operation

docs.title: Deployment Overview
docs.text: WitFoo Analytics is a containerized security analytics platform deployed via Docker Compose or the WFA (WitFoo Appliance) CLI. This section covers all deployment methods, service configuration, monitoring, TLS, and the Conductor signal pipeline.

docs.title: Supported Environments
docs.text:
OS Version Architecture WFA package Ubuntu 24.04 LTS amd64 .deb Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 amd64 .rpm Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 amd64 .rpm

Hardware Requirements

Minimum hardware depends on the deployment role. See the WFA Deployment page for per-role specifications. An Analytics AIO + Conductor node needs at least 6 CPUs, 28 GB RAM and 200 GB of disk; an Analytics AIO node needs at least 4 CPUs, 20 GB RAM and 200 GB of disk.

docs.title: Upgrading to 1.2.0
docs.text:
Release 1.2.0 has steps to take before you upgrade:

  • Docker Compose and standalone stacks must set AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the key that seals stored secrets. No default ships, and every docker compose command refuses to run until it is set.
  • WFA-managed appliances update the Analytics images to 1.2.0 first, then install WFA 2.5.4 (or 2.5.3, which shipped with 1.2.0) soon after. On an appliance WFA owns the encryption key, so do not edit it by hand.
  • Separate Conductor nodes are upgraded with Analytics or before it.

See Upgrading to 1.2.0 for every step and the known limitations.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
The standard deployment method for development and production environments. Several compose files support different deployment topologies.

# All-in-One (most common for single-node deployments)
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.aio.yml up -d --build

See Docker Compose Reference for full details on all compose files and service definitions.

docs.title: WFA CLI
docs.text:
The WFA (WitFoo Appliance) CLI automates installation, configuration, and upgrades for appliance-based deployments.

sudo wfa configure
sudo wfa analytics install

wfa configure asks for the role and writes the node's configuration; wfa analytics install checks the host against the role's minimum hardware. See WFA Deployment for the interactive configuration wizard and all CLI commands.

docs.title: Deployment Roles
docs.text:
WitFoo Analytics supports four deployment roles that scale from a single node to a distributed cluster.

Role Description Services Use Case AIO All-in-One 11 Analytics services Single-node deployments AIO + Conductor All-in-One with signal pipeline 11 Analytics services plus the Conductor services Single-node with log collection Data Node Cassandra storage node Cassandra only Distributed storage cluster Processing Node Application services 10 services (no local Cassandra) Connects to external data nodes

docs.title: Single-Node Architecture
docs.text:
The AIO role runs all services on a single machine. This is the simplest deployment and suitable for most organizations.

Browser --> Reverse Proxy (443/8081) --> API (8080) --> Incident Engine (8082)
                                    --> UI (3000)
                                    --> Dispatcher (8003): /mcp, /ws/chat and the other WebSockets

docs.title: Distributed Architecture
docs.text:
For larger deployments, separate data nodes (Cassandra) from processing nodes (application services).

Processing Node                    Data Node(s)
+-------------------+             +-------------------+
| API, UI, Engine   |  ------->  | Cassandra (9042)  |
| Proxy, Dispatcher |             +-------------------+
| NATS, Ingestion   |             +-------------------+
| Graph Processor   |  ------->  | Cassandra (9042)  |
| Prometheus, Grafana|            +-------------------+
+-------------------+

One Processing node per Data cluster

One Analytics Processing node per organization and Data cluster is supported in 1.2.0.

docs.title: Service Overview
docs.text:
WitFoo Analytics consists of the following core services:

Service Port Description reverse-proxy 443, 8081 HTTPS/HTTP entry point, routes to all backend services api 8080 REST API, authentication, user management incident-engine 8082 Incident analysis, work units, reporting dispatcher 8003 WebSockets, the MCP endpoint and background job orchestration artifact-ingestion 8090, 8443 Receives security artifacts over HTTP (8090) and HTTPS (8443) graph-processor -- Background processor for graph node/edge creation ui 3000 Svelte 5 web application cassandra 9042 Primary data store (Cassandra 5.0) nats 4222 Internal message broker prometheus 9090 Metrics collection and storage grafana 3001 Metrics dashboards and visualization

On a WFA appliance running WFA 2.5.1 or later, the api (8080) and incident-engine (8082) ports are not published on the host, and NATS is published on 127.0.0.1 only. See Architecture for the published ports of each deployment.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and ensure Docker is installed.

  2. Set AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY in the root .env file to a random 32-byte value, base64-encoded:

    openssl rand -base64 32

    The key is part of your data: back it up with the database and store the two apart. The provided launch scripts generate a key when none is set.

  3. Start all services with the AIO compose file:

    cd docker
docker compose -f docker-compose.aio.yml up -d --build

  4. Wait for all health checks to pass (approximately 2-3 minutes):

    docker compose -f docker-compose.aio.yml ps

  5. Access the web UI at https://localhost or http://localhost:8081.

Default Credentials

The default administrator account is admin@witfoo.com / F00theN0ise!. Change this password immediately after first login.

docs.title: Production Readiness Checklist
docs.text: Before deploying WitFoo Analytics to production, verify the following:

docs.title: Load Balancer Configuration
docs.text:
• HSTS headers enabled on the load balancer or reverse proxy (Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains)
  • SSL termination configured with valid TLS certificates
  • Health check endpoint configured (e.g., /api/v1/status)

docs.title: Trusted Proxies
docs.text:
• Declare each load balancer in front of the reverse proxy: WF_TRUSTED_PROXIES on Docker Compose (comma-separated addresses or CIDRs), or trusted_proxies in node.json on a WFA appliance (WFA 2.5.1 or later)
  • Make sure the load balancer sends X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto. The reverse proxy does not read X-Real-IP
  • On a WFA appliance, add trusted_proxies again after every wfa configure or wfa fetch re-run: a re-run writes node.json without it

See TLS Configuration for what the reverse proxy trusts when the list is unset.

docs.title: Security Headers
docs.text:
The reverse-proxy automatically applies 7 OWASP security headers to all responses:

Header Value X-Content-Type-Options nosniff X-Frame-Options DENY X-XSS-Protection 0 Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin Content-Security-Policy Restrictive default policy Permissions-Policy Restrictive feature policy Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

docs.title: Database Credentials
docs.text:
• Cassandra credentials are auto-generated per node during WFA installation -- do not use default credentials in production
  • Verify Cassandra is not exposed on public network interfaces

docs.title: Network Hardening
docs.text:
• On Docker Compose, INTERNAL_LISTEN_IP (default 127.0.0.1) publishes NATS, the api, incident-engine, the dispatcher, the UI, Prometheus and Grafana. LISTEN_IP still publishes Cassandra (9042, 9160), the artifact receiver (8090, 8443) and the edge (443, 8081), so restrict Cassandra's ports at the host firewall
  • Only expose the reverse-proxy port (443) to users, and the artifact receiver (8443) to your Conductors
  • Configure firewall rules to limit inter-node communication to required ports

Environment Variables

See the Environment Variables reference for all security-related configuration options including WF_TRUSTED_PROXIES, AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and WF_JWT_SECRET.

docs.text:
