docs.text:
Port Protocol Service Published on Description 443 HTTPS Reverse Proxy / Console / Conductor UI All interfaces Web UI, API and /mcp access (the port is set in wfa configure) 8081 HTTP Reverse Proxy All interfaces Plain-HTTP listener of the reverse proxy 8444 HTTPS Reverse Proxy (MCP exposure listener) All IPv4 interfaces Optional; off unless mcp_http_enabled and mcp_exposure_enabled are both set 8443 HTTPS Artifact Ingestion All interfaces Artifacts from Conductors 8090 HTTP Artifact Ingestion All interfaces Artifacts from the local Conductor on an AIO + Conductor node 9042 TCP Cassandra All interfaces Database; needed between Processing and Data nodes. Restrict it at the host firewall 4222, 8222 TCP NATS (Analytics) 127.0.0.1 only Internal message bus and its monitoring port 4223 TCP Broker Edge (Conductor) 127.0.0.1 only Conductor message broker 9090 HTTP Prometheus 127.0.0.1 only Metrics 3001 HTTP Grafana 127.0.0.1 only Dashboards 514 TCP, UDP Signal Server All interfaces Syslog 6514, 7514 TCP Signal Server All interfaces Syslog over TLS; syslog RFC 6587 5044, 5045 TCP Signal Server All interfaces Beats (5044 with TLS, 5045 without) 2055 UDP Signal Server All interfaces NetFlow v5/v7/v9 and IPFIX, on Conductor and AIO + Conductor nodes; off until enabled under Log Servers

The api (8080), incident-engine (8082), dispatcher (8003) and UI (3000) ports are not published on the host. Reach them through the reverse proxy.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
On Docker Compose, INTERNAL_LISTEN_IP (default 127.0.0.1) publishes the internal services: NATS (4222, 8222), the api (8080), incident-engine (8082), the dispatcher (8003), the UI (3000), Prometheus (9090) and Grafana (3001). LISTEN_IP publishes Cassandra (9042, 9160), the artifact receiver (8090, 8443) and the edge (443, 8081).

The compose files do not publish 2055/udp. To receive NetFlow on a compose stack, add 2055:2055/udp to the signal server's ports.

The development compose file docker/docker-compose.yml also runs the responder engine: its API (8084) is not published, and its metrics port (9094 by default, 9095 in that compose file) is published on INTERNAL_LISTEN_IP.

Minimal Firewall Configuration

For a single Analytics node deployment, only port 443 needs to be open to users. Open 8443 to your Conductor nodes, and on a Conductor open the Signal Server ports your data sources use. Open 8444 only if you use the MCP exposure listener, and restrict its sources at your perimeter.

docs.title: Deployment Roles
docs.text: WitFoo Appliances support three node roles, each designed for a specific function within your security operations infrastructure. This page helps you understand each role and choose the right deployment topology.

docs.title: Role Overview
docs.text: Role Purpose Typical Deployment Conductor Data ingestion and signal processing Remote offices, network segments, cloud VPCs Console Centralized management and monitoring Headquarters or management network Analytics Security analytics, investigation, and reporting SOC or data center

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text: The Analytics node is the primary WitFoo platform. It performs security investigation, incident correlation, compliance reporting, and provides the main user interface for security analysts.

docs.title: Purpose and Use Case
docs.text:
• Core security operations platform for your SOC
  • Receives processed artifacts from Conductor nodes (or ingests directly)
  • Correlates events into incidents using the knowledge graph and incident engine
  • Generates compliance reports, executive summaries, and operational metrics
  • Provides the web UI for analysts, investigators, and management

docs.title: Hardware Requirements
docs.text: Resource Minimum Recommended CPU 8 cores 16 cores RAM 12 GB 32 GB Disk 220 GB 1 TB

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
The Analytics node runs the full service stack:

Service Description Cassandra Primary data store and knowledge graph NATS Internal message bus Artifact Ingestion Receives and normalizes artifacts Graph Processor Builds the security knowledge graph Incident Engine Correlates events into scored incidents API Service REST API with authentication and RBAC Dispatcher Real-time WebSocket notifications Reverse Proxy TLS termination and request routing Web UI Analyst-facing user interface Prometheus Metrics collection Grafana Metrics visualization

docs.title: When to Choose Analytics
docs.text:
• Always — Every WitFoo deployment requires at least one Analytics node
  • You need a single-node deployment for evaluation or small environments
  • You are building a SOC and need investigation, correlation, and reporting capabilities

Start Here

If you're deploying WitFoo for the first time, start with a single Analytics node. You can add Conductor and Console nodes later as your deployment grows.

docs.title: Conductor
docs.text: The Conductor node handles data ingestion and signal processing. It collects signals from data sources, parses them into structured artifacts, and forwards them to the Analytics node for analysis.

docs.title: Purpose and Use Case
docs.text:
• Deployed at the network edge or in remote locations where data sources reside
  • Collects syslog, API feeds, and agent data from firewalls, IDS/IPS, endpoints, and cloud services
  • Parses and normalizes raw signals before forwarding to Analytics
  • Reduces bandwidth by processing data locally and sending only structured artifacts

docs.title: Hardware Requirements
docs.text: Resource Minimum Recommended CPU 4 cores 8 cores RAM 8 GB 16 GB Disk 220 GB 500 GB

docs.title: Services
docs.text: Service Description NATS Broker Message broker for signal ingestion (ports 4223, 4443) Signal Server Receives raw signals from data sources Signal Parser Parses and normalizes signals into artifacts Artifact Exporter Forwards processed artifacts to Analytics via NATS leaf Broker Edge Manages broker cluster connectivity

docs.title: When to Choose Conductor
docs.text:
• You have data sources in remote offices, branch locations, or separate network segments
  • You want to process and filter data locally before sending it to Analytics
  • You need to collect data from cloud VPCs (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud)
  • You want to reduce WAN bandwidth usage between sites

Multiple Conductors

Deploy one Conductor per network segment or remote location. All Conductors forward their processed artifacts to a central Analytics node.

docs.title: Console
docs.text: The Console node provides a centralized management and monitoring interface for your entire WitFoo deployment. It is a lightweight, single-container deployment.

docs.title: Purpose and Use Case
docs.text:
• Centralized dashboard for monitoring the health and status of all Conductor and Analytics nodes
  • Remote configuration and management of appliances
  • Deployment oversight for multi-site environments

docs.title: Hardware Requirements
docs.text: Resource Minimum Recommended CPU 4 cores 4 cores RAM 8 GB 8 GB Disk 220 GB 220 GB

docs.title: Services
docs.text: Service Description Console Single container providing management UI and API (port 443)

docs.title: When to Choose Console
docs.text:
• You manage multiple Conductor and/or Analytics nodes across different sites
  • You need centralized visibility into appliance health and configuration
  • You want a single pane of glass for deployment management

Console Is Optional

The Console node is not required for single-site deployments. A single Analytics node (or Analytics + Conductor) works without a Console. Add a Console when you manage three or more appliances.

docs.title: Single Node (Evaluation / Small)
docs.text:
Deploy a single Analytics node for evaluation, lab environments, or small organizations.

[Data Sources] → [Analytics]
  • Simplest deployment
  • All ingestion and analysis on one node
  • Recommended hardware: 16 CPU, 32 GB RAM, 1 TB disk

docs.title: Two Nodes (Small / Medium)
docs.text:
Deploy a Conductor for data collection and an Analytics node for analysis.

[Data Sources] → [Conductor] → [Analytics]
  • Separates ingestion from analysis
  • Conductor can be placed in a DMZ or remote network
  • Analytics node is dedicated to processing and UI

docs.title: Multi-Site (Enterprise)
docs.text:
Deploy Conductors at each site, a central Analytics node, and a Console for management.

[Site A Sources] → [Conductor A] ──┐
[Site B Sources] → [Conductor B] ──┤→ [Analytics] ← [Console]
[Cloud Sources]  → [Conductor C] ──┘
  • Conductors at each remote site or cloud VPC
  • Central Analytics node for correlation and reporting
  • Console for centralized management of all nodes

docs.title: Hardware Summary
docs.text:
Role CPU (min) RAM (min) Disk (min) Conductor 4 8 GB 220 GB Console 4 8 GB 220 GB Analytics 8 12 GB 220 GB

Right-Sizing Your Deployment

Start with the minimum requirements and scale up based on data volume. Monitor resource usage from the Admin > Health dashboard (Analytics) or Grafana (if local metrics are enabled on Conductor). The recommended specs for Analytics (16 CPU, 32 GB RAM, 1 TB disk) support most production workloads.

docs.title: First Login
docs.text: After deploying and configuring your WitFoo Appliance, this page guides you through your first login, changing default credentials, and completing the 12-step onboarding wizard.

docs.title: Default Credentials
docs.text:
Change All Default Passwords Immediately

WitFoo Appliances ship with default credentials that are publicly documented. You must change these immediately after first login to prevent unauthorized access.

docs.title: SSH Access
Web UI Access
docs.text:
Field Value URL https://<appliance-ip> Email admin@witfoo.com Password F00theN0ise!

The web UI is accessible via HTTPS on port 443.

Self-Signed Certificate Warning

If you are using the default self-signed certificates, your browser will display a security warning. Accept the warning to proceed, and plan to install trusted certificates for production use.

docs.title: Changing the Web UI Password
docs.text:
1. Open your browser and navigate to https://<appliance-ip>.
  2. Log in with the default credentials (admin@witfoo.com / F00theN0ise!).
  3. The onboarding wizard will appear on first login. Step 1 (Create Admin) prompts you to create a new admin user with a secure password.
  4. After creating your admin account, log out and log back in with your new credentials.
  5. Optionally, disable or delete the default admin@witfoo.com account from Admin > Users.

docs.title: Onboarding Wizard
docs.text: On first login to an Analytics node, a full-screen onboarding wizard guides you through initial platform configuration. The wizard consists of 12 steps organized by priority.

docs.title: Step Categories
docs.text:
Category Meaning Critical Must be completed for the platform to function correctly Recommended Strongly suggested for production deployments Optional Enhance functionality but can be configured later

Flexible Completion Order

Steps can be completed in any order — use the step navigation on the left side of the wizard to jump between steps. However, Critical steps (0–3) should be completed before using the platform for security operations.

Persistent Reminders

If you skip steps and close the wizard, a persistent banner appears after login reminding you of incomplete configuration. All settings can be changed later from the Admin panel.

docs.title: Step Overview
docs.text:
Step Name Category Description 0 Welcome Critical Organization settings and preferences 1 Create Admin Critical First admin user account 2 Feature Selection Critical Enable/disable platform modules 3 Data Retention Critical Data lifecycle policies 4 CyberGrid Optional Threat intelligence sharing 5 General Settings Review Recommended Confirm organization settings 6 Business Metrics Optional ROI and cost reporting inputs 7 Compliance Frameworks Recommended Regulatory framework selection 8 Authentication Recommended Identity provider configuration 9 Notifications Optional Email and Slack alerting 10 AI Capabilities Optional AI assistant configuration 11 Summary — Completion checklist and launch

Configure Integrations After Onboarding

Once onboarding is complete, connect your security tools using the Integration Enablement Guides. The Integration Catalog lists every integration an operator can enable in this release.

docs.title: Step 0: Welcome (Critical)
docs.text:
Configure your organization's basic settings and preferences.

Field Description Organization Name Display name for your organization (pre-populated from wfa configure) Timezone Primary timezone for date/time display across the platform Date/Time Format Choose between 12-hour and 24-hour formats, and date ordering (MM/DD/YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD) Enable Notifications Toggle platform-wide notification delivery

Timezone Matters

The timezone setting affects how timestamps are displayed throughout the platform, including in reports and incident timelines. Choose the timezone where your primary SOC operates.

docs.title: Step 1: Create Admin (Critical)
docs.text:
Create the first administrative user account. This replaces the default admin@witfoo.com account for day-to-day use.

Field Description Full Name Administrator's display name Email Login email address (must be unique) Password Minimum 8 characters; strong password recommended

If an admin user already exists (e.g., from a previous configuration), this step is automatically skipped.

Create a Personal Admin Account

Always create a named admin account for audit trail purposes. The default admin@witfoo.com account should be disabled after your personal account is created.

docs.title: Step 2: Feature Selection (Critical)
docs.text:
Toggle platform modules between three states:

State Behavior Full Module is fully enabled with UI navigation, background processing, and API access Background Module runs background processing but is hidden from the UI navigation Disabled Module is completely disabled — no processing, no UI, no API

Available modules:

Module Description Search Signal search, graph exploration, and artifact investigation Observer Real-time monitoring dashboards and alert management Reporter Compliance reports, executive summaries, and operational metrics CyberGrid Threat intelligence sharing and IOC enrichment Responder Incident response workflows and playbook automation AI AI-powered analysis assistant and natural language queries

The wizard automatically resolves dependencies between modules. For example, enabling Reporter requires Search to be at least in Background mode.

docs.title: Step 3: Data Retention (Critical)
docs.text:
Configure how long different categories of data are retained in the database. Set retention periods between 1 and 365 days for each feature area.

Data Type Default Description Artifacts 7 days Raw ingested data (logs, events, signals) Work Units 365 days Incidents, investigations, cases Work Collections 365 days Grouped work items and campaigns Reports 1,825 days (5 years) Generated compliance and operational reports

Disk Space Planning

Longer retention periods require more disk space. Monitor disk usage from the Admin > Health dashboard and adjust retention policies as needed. For high-volume environments, start with shorter artifact retention and increase as you understand your storage consumption.

docs.title: Step 4: CyberGrid (Optional)
docs.text:
Configure participation in WitFoo's CyberGrid threat intelligence network.

Mode Description Consumer Receive threat intelligence from the CyberGrid network Contributor Share anonymized threat data and receive intelligence Full Full bidirectional sharing with attribution

Select your participation level or skip this step to disable CyberGrid.

docs.title: Step 5: General Settings Review (Recommended)
docs.text:
A read-only confirmation screen displaying the settings configured in Step 0 (Welcome). Review your organization name, timezone, date/time format, and notification preferences.

No input is required — confirm the settings are correct and proceed.

docs.title: Step 6: Business Metrics (Optional)
docs.text:
Provide business context for ROI calculations and executive reporting. These values are used by the Reporter module to generate cost-savings and efficiency reports.

Field Description FTE Annual Cost Fully loaded cost per full-time security employee Annual Revenue Organization's annual revenue (for risk calculations) Annual Security Spend Total annual security operations budget Mean Time to Detect Average time to detect a security incident (hours) Mean Time to Respond Average time to respond to a security incident (hours)

Estimate If Unsure

These values are used for reporting only and can be updated at any time. Reasonable estimates are better than skipping this step entirely, as they enable ROI dashboards from day one.

docs.title: Step 7: Compliance Frameworks (Recommended)
docs.text:
Enable the compliance frameworks relevant to your organization and designate a primary framework.

Available frameworks include industry standards such as:

  • CIS Controls (CSC v7, CSC v8)
  • NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF)
  • NIST 800-53
  • ISO 27001
  • PCI DSS
  • HIPAA
  • SOC 2

Toggle each framework on or off, then select one as your primary framework. The primary framework determines the default compliance view in Reporter dashboards.

docs.title: Step 8: Authentication (Recommended)
docs.text:
Configure how users authenticate to the platform.

Method Description Local Username/password stored in the WitFoo database LDAP Authenticate against an LDAP or Active Directory server SAML SSO Single sign-on via a SAML 2.0 identity provider Mixed Local accounts for admins, LDAP/SAML for standard users

For LDAP and SAML configurations, the wizard provides Test Connection buttons to validate connectivity before saving.

LDAP Fields Description Server URL LDAP server address (e.g., ldaps://ldap.mycompany.com:636) Bind DN Distinguished name for LDAP binding Bind Password Password for the bind DN Search Base Base DN for user searches User Filter LDAP filter for user lookup SAML Fields Description IdP Metadata URL URL to the identity provider's SAML metadata Entity ID Service provider entity ID ACS URL Assertion Consumer Service URL (auto-populated)

docs.title: Step 9: Notifications (Optional)
docs.text:
Configure notification channels for alerts, incident updates, and system events.

SMTP Email:

Field Description SMTP Server Mail server hostname and port From Address Sender email address Username SMTP authentication username Password SMTP authentication password Use TLS Enable TLS encryption

Slack Webhook:

Field Description Webhook URL Slack incoming webhook URL Default Channel Channel for notifications (overridden by webhook config)

Both channels provide a Test Send button to verify configuration before saving.

docs.title: Step 10: AI Capabilities (Optional)
docs.text:
Configure the AI assistant for natural language investigation queries and automated analysis.

Field Description AI Provider Disabled (no AI), Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, IBM watsonx.ai, or Ollama (Local) API Key Your API key for the selected provider (not asked for Ollama) Model ID The model to use; the field suggests a default for each provider Base URL Ollama only: the address of the Ollama server (default http://localhost:11434) Max Tokens Maximum response length (default 4096) Temperature Response creativity, from 0 to 2 (default 0.7)

Ollama runs on your own network, so the whole AI loop stays local; it suits air-gapped deployments.

AI API Keys

The cloud providers need an API key. Your API key is encrypted at rest and never shared. You can change providers or disable AI at any time from Settings > General Settings > AI Setup.

docs.title: Step 11: Summary
docs.text:
The final step displays a progress checklist showing the completion status of all previous steps.

Element Description Step Checklist Each step shown with ✅ (complete) or ⚠️ (skipped/incomplete) Completion Percentage Overall configuration progress Launch Platform Button to close the wizard and enter the platform

Clicking Launch Platform closes the wizard and takes you to the main dashboard. Any incomplete steps will trigger a persistent banner reminder.

All Settings Are Editable

Every setting configured in the onboarding wizard can be modified later from the Admin panel. The wizard is a convenience for initial setup — it does not lock in any configuration permanently.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This guide covers deploying a WitFoo Appliance (WFA) — the production deployment method for WitFoo Analytics. The WFA daemon manages containers, configuration, and lifecycle for all node roles.

Upgrading an existing deployment?

Read Upgrading to 1.2.0 before you upgrade. It gives the order for WFA appliances and the steps that need action.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Network access to the target host via SSH (port 22) and HTTPS (port 443)
  • A WitFoo license key, or plan to request a 15-day trial during configuration
  • Hardware meeting the minimum requirements for your chosen deployment role

docs.title: Hardware Requirements
docs.text:
Each role has its own minimum RAM and CPU (logical CPUs), which the configuration wizard checks:

Role CPU (min) RAM (min) Disk (min) Analytics AIO + Conductor 6 28 GB 200 GB Analytics AIO 4 20 GB 200 GB Analytics Processing Node 2 6 GB 100 GB Analytics Data Node 2 12 GB 500 GB Conductor 2 8 GB — Console 1 4 GB —

For production, 16 CPU cores, 32 GB RAM and 1 TB of disk is recommended. See WFA Deployment for details.

docs.title: Installation Overview
docs.text:
Deploying WitFoo Analytics follows three steps regardless of your infrastructure:

  1. Deploy a WitFoo Appliance image or run an install script
  2. Configure the appliance role with sudo wfa configure
  3. Access the web UI via HTTPS (port 443) and complete the onboarding wizard

docs.title: Step 1: Deploy a WitFoo Appliance
docs.text: Choose the deployment method that matches your infrastructure. All appliance images and scripts are available from the witfoo-appliances repository.

docs.title: Option A: On-Premises VM
docs.text:
Pre-built Ubuntu 24 virtual machine images are available for the following hypervisors:

  1. Download the appropriate image from github.com/witfoo/witfoo-appliances:

    • VMware — OVA format
    • Hyper-V — VHDX format
    • QEMU/KVM — QCOW2 format

  2. Import the image into your hypervisor and allocate resources according to the hardware requirements for your intended role.

  3. Boot the virtual machine. The appliance will start with a default network configuration using DHCP.

  4. Connect via SSH to the appliance:

    ssh witfooadmin@<appliance-ip>

Change Default Credentials Immediately

The default SSH credentials are witfooadmin / F00theN0ise!. Change these immediately after first login. See First Login for details.

docs.title: Option B: Cloud Marketplace
docs.text:
WitFoo Appliances are available on major cloud marketplaces:

  1. Launch a WitFoo Appliance instance from your cloud provider's marketplace:

    • AWS Marketplace — Search for "WitFoo Appliance"
    • Azure Marketplace — Search for "WitFoo Appliance"
    • Google Cloud Marketplace — Search for "WitFoo Appliance"

  2. Select an instance size that meets the hardware requirements for your intended role.

  3. Configure your security group or firewall rules to allow:

    • Port 22 — SSH (administration)
    • Port 443 — HTTPS (web UI)

  4. Connect via SSH using your cloud provider's key pair or the default credentials.

Cloud Instance Sizing

An Analytics AIO + Conductor node needs at least 6 vCPUs and 28 GB RAM; an Analytics AIO node needs at least 4 vCPUs and 20 GB RAM. For production workloads, 16 vCPUs and 32 GB RAM with 1 TB disk is recommended.

docs.title: Option C: Bare Metal
docs.text:
Install the WitFoo Appliance directly on a physical or virtual server using the provided install scripts:

Ubuntu 24:

  1. Start with a fresh Ubuntu 24 server installation.

  2. Download and run the install script:

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/witfoo/witfoo-appliances/main/ubuntu-install.sh -o ubuntu-install.sh
chmod +x ubuntu-install.sh
sudo ./ubuntu-install.sh

  3. The script installs all dependencies, creates the witfooadmin user, and installs the WFA daemon.

RHEL 10:

  1. Start with a fresh RHEL 10 server installation.

  2. Download and run the install script:

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/witfoo/witfoo-appliances/main/rhel-install.sh -o rhel-install.sh
chmod +x rhel-install.sh
sudo ./rhel-install.sh

  3. The script installs all dependencies, creates the witfooadmin user, and installs the WFA daemon.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure the Appliance
docs.text:
Once the appliance is deployed, run the interactive configuration wizard to select a role and configure services:

sudo wfa configure

The wizard walks you through licensing, product and role selection, networking, certificates, the administrator account, and optional features. Your organization is taken from the license. It generates the configuration file at /witfoo/configs/node.json.

For a detailed walkthrough of every prompt and option, see WFA Configure Wizard.

docs.title: Step 3: Access the Web UI
docs.text:
After configuration completes, the WFA daemon starts all services for your selected role. For Analytics nodes:

  1. Open a web browser and navigate to:

    https://<appliance-ip>

  2. Log in with the web UI administrator account:

    • Email: admin@witfoo.com
    • Password: F00theN0ise!, the shipped default, unless WFA has already applied the password from the wizard's Admin Account step (below)

  3. Complete the onboarding wizard to configure your organization, users, and integrations.

See First Login for detailed instructions on the onboarding process.

Change Default Passwords

Both the SSH and web UI default passwords must be changed immediately after first login. See First Login for instructions.

WFA 2.5.1 and later may set the administrator password

On the first start of WFA 2.5.1 or later, if admin@witfoo.com still has the shipped default password and the password file from the wizard's Admin Account step is still on the node, WFA applies that password to the account. If you cannot sign in, run sudo wfa user-reset on the node. See WFA Configure Wizard.

docs.title: Verifying the Installation
docs.text:
After completing configuration, verify that services are running:

sudo wfa analytics status

This command lists the services the role runs. To see their state, run sudo wfa status and sudo docker ps. All services should be running within a few minutes of configuration completing.

Cassandra Startup Time

The Cassandra database may take 2–5 minutes to fully initialize on first boot. Other services will wait for Cassandra before becoming available.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Choose a deployment role if you haven't already
  • Walk through the configure wizard in detail
  • Complete first login and onboarding
  • Understand the architecture
  • Upgrade an existing deployment to 1.2.0

For Developers

This guide covers production deployment via WitFoo Appliances. If you are a developer working on WitFoo Analytics itself, see the Deployment section of the documentation for Docker Compose development workflows.

docs.title: WFA Configure Wizard
docs.text: The sudo wfa configure command launches an interactive wizard that configures a WitFoo Appliance for its intended role. This page documents every step of the wizard in WFA 2.5.3, the WFA release that ships with WitFoo Analytics 1.2.0, including the prompts, options, and role-specific differences.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The wizard generates the configuration file /witfoo/configs/node.json, which the WFA daemon uses to determine which services to run and how to configure them. For Analytics roles it also writes /witfoo/configs/analytics.json. Run the wizard as root:

sudo wfa configure

The wizard writes node.json with mode 0600, readable by root only. Press Ctrl+C at any time to cancel.

Retention, UI modules and CyberGrid

The wizard no longer asks for data retention, UI modules or CyberGrid. It sets defaults, and you change them in the Onboarding Wizard of the Analytics web UI. See First Login.

docs.title: Step Applicability by Role
docs.text:
Not every step applies to every role. Use this table as a quick reference:

Step Conductor Console Analytics 1. License Configuration ✅ ✅ ✅ 1b. Product Selection ✅ ✅ ✅ 2. Node Role Selection ✅ ✅ ✅ 3. Appliance ID ✅ ✅ ✅ 4. Network Configuration ✅ ✅ ✅ 5. Certificate Configuration ✅ ✅ ✅ 6. Web UI Port & Protocol ✅ ✅ ✅ (not on a Data Node) 7. Admin Account ✅ ✅ ✅ 8. Optional Features ✅ ✅ ✅ 9. Staff-Requested Jobs ✅ ✅ ✅ 10. Remote Console URL ✅ — ✅ 11. Analytics Endpoint ✅ — — 12. Clustering Configuration — — Processing and Data Nodes 13. Review and Save ✅ ✅ ✅

The broker ports (client port 4223, leaf port 4443, maximum data 1024 MB) and the container registry are set automatically. The wizard does not ask for them.

docs.title: Step 1: License Configuration
docs.text:
A WitFoo license is required to pull container images and activate services. The organization ID and organization name are assigned from the license; the wizard does not ask for them.

Cloud deployments (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud marketplace instances): the wizard detects the cloud deployment and fetches the license automatically.

On-premises deployments:

  1. I have a license key — enter it manually
  2. Request a 15-day trial — free, no credit card required

Select option (1-2):

Option 1 — Enter license key. License keys are UUID-formatted strings provided by WitFoo:

Enter your license key: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
  Verifying license with WitFoo licensing service...
  ✓ License verified and configured

Option 2 — Request 15-day trial. Accept the WitFoo End User License Agreement, then enter:

Company name: My Company Inc.
Contact name: Jane Smith
Contact email: jane@example.com

The wizard prints the trial license key and its expiry date.

Trial Licenses

Trial licenses provide full functionality for 15 days. Contact WitFoo sales to convert to a permanent license before the trial expires.

docs.title: Step 1b: Product Selection
docs.text: Select the WitFoo product and tier your license covers, for example Conductor Lite, Pro or Max, Analytics Lite, Pro or Max, Reporter Lite or Pro, or Console. The product decides which roles the next step offers.

docs.title: Step 2: Node Role Selection
docs.text:
Select the role this appliance will perform in your deployment. The menu shows only the roles your product allows. Type b to go back to product selection.

# Role Description 1 Analytics AIO + Conductor Everything on one server: signal collection, analytics, UI and database. Recommended for most users 2 Analytics AIO Analytics without Conductor; signals come from a separate Conductor node 3 Conductor Signal collection and forwarding only 4 Analytics Processing Node API, UI and processing services; connects to external Cassandra data nodes 5 Analytics Data Node Dedicated Cassandra database storage 6 Console Central management dashboard for WitFoo appliances

After selection, the wizard checks the host against the role's minimum RAM and CPU (logical CPUs):

Role RAM (min) CPU (min) Analytics AIO + Conductor 28 GB 6 Analytics AIO 20 GB 4 Conductor 8 GB 2 Analytics Processing Node 6 GB 2 Analytics Data Node 12 GB 2 Console 4 GB 1

If the host does not meet the minimum, the wizard shows a warning with the required and detected values and asks Continue anyway? (yes/no).

Choosing a Role

  • Analytics is the primary platform — choose this for investigation, correlation, and reporting.
  • Conductor handles data ingestion from remote networks and forwards signals to Analytics.
  • Console provides centralized management of multiple Conductor and Analytics nodes.

See Deployment Roles for detailed guidance.

docs.title: Step 3: Appliance ID
docs.text:
An Appliance ID uniquely identifies this node. It is used for license binding, Console registration, and NATS authentication. If the node already has one, the wizard offers to keep it:

  Found existing: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
Use existing appliance ID? (Y/n):

Otherwise it generates a new UUID. On Analytics roles, the wizard also generates a random 32-character Cassandra password.

docs.title: Step 4: Network Configuration
docs.text:
Configure the network identity of this node.

Node Hostname: wfa-analytics-01.example.local

Node IP [auto-detect]:
  ✓ Auto-detected: 192.0.2.50
  • Node Hostname — Used to identify this node in the cluster and for TLS certificate validation. Use the machine's FQDN if available.
  • Node IP — The address other nodes use to reach this machine. Press Enter to auto-detect it from the primary network interface, or type an address.

Static IP Recommended

For production deployments, assign a static IP address to the appliance before running the wizard. DHCP-assigned addresses may change, breaking inter-node communication.

docs.title: Step 5: Certificate Configuration
docs.text:
Configure TLS certificates for secure communication between WitFoo nodes. Press Enter at each prompt to use the default path. If you have no certificates yet, the defaults are fine: WFA generates self-signed certificates on first deployment.

Prompt Default Client cert /witfoo/certs/client.crt Client key /witfoo/certs/client.key Server cert /witfoo/certs/server.crt Server key /witfoo/certs/server.key CA cert /witfoo/certs/ca.crt

Production TLS

Self-signed certificates are suitable for evaluation only. For production deployments, provide certificates signed by your organization's certificate authority or a trusted public CA.

docs.title: Step 6: Web UI Port & Protocol
docs.text:
Configure the port and protocol for the web UI on this node. This step is skipped on a Data Node.

Web UI protocol [https]:
Web UI port [443]:
  • Protocol — https (TLS-encrypted, recommended) or http (unencrypted, for development and testing only).
  • Port — Defaults to 443 for https and 80 for http.

docs.title: Step 7: Admin Account
docs.text:
Set up the initial administrator account for the web UI.

Admin email [admin@witfoo.com]:
Enter admin password: ********
Confirm admin password: ********
  ✓ Admin credentials saved
  • Admin email — Asked on Analytics roles only. It is the login username of the Analytics web UI's initial administrator. Other roles use admin as the login username.
  • Password — At least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes, with no white space at the start or the end. Input is masked and must be entered twice.
  • The password is saved, readable by root only, to /data/local/.passwd.

WFA 2.5.1 and later may apply this password to the Analytics administrator

On the first start of WFA 2.5.1 or later, if the Analytics web UI administrator (admin@witfoo.com) still has the shipped default password:

  • When the password file from this step is still on the node, WFA applies it as the Analytics administrator password and signs that administrator's current sessions out.
  • When the file is no longer there, WFA leaves the password as it is and logs a warning that names wfa user-reset.

A password anyone has already set, in the web UI or with wfa user-reset, is never changed. This can take up to an hour while the database starts. Before you upgrade, make sure you know the password last entered here, and update any script or integration that signs in as admin@witfoo.com with the default password. If you cannot sign in after the upgrade, run sudo wfa user-reset.

WFA 2.5.3 removes the password file once the Analytics administrator's password is no longer the seeded default.

docs.title: Step 8: Optional Features
docs.text: The wizard presents role-specific optional features.

docs.title: Conductor and Analytics Options
docs.text:
Enable local metrics? (y/n) [n]:
Enable offline mode? (y/n) [n]:
Send operational metrics and status logs from this appliance to WitFoo? ... (y/n):
Enable auto update? (y/n) [y]:
  • Local metrics — Expose a local Prometheus metrics endpoint and Grafana dashboards for monitoring node performance.
  • Offline mode — Prevent this node from making any outbound internet connections. Only enable this for air-gapped or isolated environments. It disables auto-updates, cloud licensing, Intel API sync and CyberGrid.
  • Metrics export — Send operational metrics (CPU, disk, memory, container and service health, runtime counters) and status logs to WitFoo's monitoring service. This question has no default: answer y or n. Choosing No does not affect the appliance's own monitoring.
  • Auto-update — Automatically apply software updates and security patches. Disable only if you require manual change control.

docs.title: Console and Data Node Options
docs.text:
A Console node and a Data Node ask only for offline mode ([n]) and auto-update ([y]).

FIPS Compliance mode

WFA 2.5.1 and later do not offer FIPS Compliance mode, and the wizard no longer asks about it.

docs.title: Step 9: Staff-Requested Jobs
docs.text:
Allow WitFoo support staff to request jobs on this appliance? ... (y/n) [n]:

Staff-requested jobs are support packs, log collection, diagnostics, update-and-reboot and trust reset. Choosing n stops every job WitFoo staff request. Support packs you create and send yourself are not affected. The default is n on a new appliance; a re-run offers the answer node.json already holds. Change it later with sudo wfa staff-jobs off or sudo wfa staff-jobs on. See WFA CLI Reference.

docs.title: Step 10: Remote Console URL
docs.text: If you have a WitFoo Console node for centralized management, enter its root URL, for example https://console.example.com. This node then sends health and status reports to that Console. Leave it empty if you have no Console or will configure it later. This step is skipped on a Console node.

docs.title: Step 11: Analytics Endpoint (Conductor Only)
docs.text:
Enter the URL of the Analytics receiver, so this Conductor can send artifacts to the Analytics node. Port 8443 is the TLS ingestion port:

Analytics endpoint [none]: https://<analytics-host>:8443

Leave it empty if you will configure the exporter in the Conductor UI later.

docs.title: Step 12: Clustering Configuration
docs.text:
Distributed deployments need the nodes to know about each other. On a Data Node this step comes right after the Admin Account step; on a Processing Node it comes after the Remote Console URL.

  • Analytics Processing Node — Enter the data node addresses as comma-separated IP:port pairs (for example 192.0.2.10:9042,192.0.2.11:9042), then the Cassandra password that was generated on your Data Node.
  • Analytics Data Node — Enter the seed node IPs of every data node in the Cassandra cluster, including this node's own IP, and the listen address Cassandra binds to (Enter uses the node IP).

docs.title: Step 13: Review and Save
docs.text:
The wizard displays a summary of all configured settings and asks Save this configuration? (y/n). After you confirm, it:

  1. Writes /witfoo/configs/node.json (and analytics.json on Analytics roles).
  2. Starts the wfad service.
  3. Shows the initialization progress: image pulls (up to 8 minutes), container health (up to 2 minutes), then the web UI address.

Monitoring is non-fatal: if the containers take longer, the wizard prints a warning with manual checks (docker ps, docker images | grep witfoo).

docs.title: Re-running the Wizard
docs.text:
You can re-run sudo wfa configure (or sudo wfa fetch) to change settings.

  • The MCP settings are kept. A re-run keeps mcp_http_enabled, mcp_exposure_enabled, mcp_public_url, mcp_oauth_ui_url, mcp_oauth_cimd and the relay's mcp_relay_ fields. A value that cannot be read is named and left out, and the old file is kept beside the new one as node.json.unreadable-<time>.bak.
  • Your staff-jobs choice is kept.
  • Other settings that no prompt asks for are not kept. This includes trusted_proxies.

Add trusted_proxies again after every re-run

A re-run of wfa configure or wfa fetch (including wfa configure --license-file) writes node.json without trusted_proxies. Add it again after each re-run, then run sudo wfa restart. See TLS Configuration.

The wizard does not set the MCP keys. To turn on MCP, add them to node.json by hand and run sudo wfa restart. They need WFA 2.5.1 or later. See MCP Configuration.

docs.title: What Happens Next
docs.text:
After the wizard completes:

  1. The WFA daemon pulls container images from the configured registry
  2. Services start in dependency order (Cassandra first, then dependent services)
  3. For Analytics nodes, the web UI becomes available on port 443 within a few minutes
  4. Proceed to First Login to change default passwords and complete the onboarding wizard

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Version history for WitFoo products.

docs.title: v1.2.0 (2026-11-08)
docs.text: Minor release that completes the MCP connector and the controls around it. AI clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor and Claude Code connect with a personal key each user creates, or by signing in through the appliance's own OAuth 2.1 authorization server; every connection acts as a real user with that user's permissions. Also new: an optional AI-connector relay, user disable and enable with session controls, tighter published ports, Signal Search filters that apply to the whole time range, a Vrax threat-intelligence import, and seven new Conductor pull connectors with a NetFlow and IPFIX collector. Action required before upgrading a Docker Compose stack: set AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Upgrade from 1.1.5; ships alongside WFA 2.5.3, Conductor 1.10.0 and Console 1.10.0 (Conductor nodes run the 1.2.0 images). Full release notes.

docs.title: MCP connector
docs.text:
• Personal MCP keys — each user who holds the new Connect MCP (mcp:connect) permission creates keys under Profile → Security → MCP connections. Keys last 1–365 days (default 90), can be rotated and revoked, and a user holds at most 5 active keys. A connected client reaches only the tools its user's permissions allow
  • App sign-in with OAuth 2.1 — apps sign in through the appliance's own authorization server, with a consent page, read access by default and write as a separate option. Users see and revoke their apps under Profile → Security → Connected apps; administrators register clients and set the policy for other apps
  • Off by default — the organization's mode under AI Setup → MCP Authentication and the appliance's HTTP transport (mcp_http_enabled) are both closed until you open them
  • Licensed — MCP is included with Analytics Pro, Analytics Max and Reporter Pro
  • Exposure listener — an optional listener on port 8444 serves /mcp, the sign-in discovery documents and /oauth/token and nothing else, for marketplace clients
  • 44 tools — each marked read-only (28) or state-changing (16), with its title in both places a client reads it. Seven tools that always failed are removed. ChatGPT can now connect; verified against a test rig, not yet against a live 1.2.0 appliance
  • Org-wide keys retired — wfmcp_ keys no longer authenticate; administrators can list them and revoke them all at once

docs.title: AI-connector relay
docs.text:
• Reach the appliance without an inbound port — an optional relay gives an AI marketplace or MCP client an address that reaches the appliance's MCP endpoint through WitFoo. Off by default for every organization and appliance; an operator turns it on with wfa mcp-relay enable (WFA 2.5.1 or later), reads the notice, types ENABLE and runs wfa restart
  • Status on AI Setup — a read-only relay card shows the address and state while the relay is enabled; wfa mcp-relay status, ack and off manage it on the appliance

docs.title: Users and sessions
docs.text:
• Disable and enable — in User Management, Delete is now Disable, and a disabled user can be enabled again. There is no permanent delete. An administrator cannot disable their own account
  • Sessions end when they should — disabling a user, suspending or deleting a tenant, or resetting a password ends the user's sessions within seconds and open live connections within a minute
  • Everyone signs in again once — upgrading changes the session key
  • Plain account addresses — an address typed for an account must be one plain address

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
• In-app assistant permissions — Read AI (ai:read) and Write AI (ai:write) gate the AI assistant; every built-in role has both, and existing custom roles receive both once at upgrade
  • Dashboards write permission — creating, updating, deleting and cloning dashboards need dashboards:write; each dashboard widget is also checked against its own data
  • Stricter checks — the setup wizard's AI, DNS, frameworks and CyberGrid steps, classification rules, enrichment settings, compliance frameworks and the CyberGrid API now check permissions
  • Admin-only user and role pages — User Management and Role Management open only for the Administrator permission

docs.title: Signal Search
docs.text:
• Filters apply to the whole time range — contains, not-equal, numeric comparisons, Client IP and Server IP (IPv4 or IPv6), Location and free-word filters narrow the result list, timeline and facet counts across the range, not only the newest events
  • Says when it read part of the range — a warning above the results, a line under the timeline and a plus sign on facet counts; API callers get meta.scan
  • Clear refusals — a filter the search cannot apply is refused with "The search was not accepted as typed"
  • Timeline grouping by IP groups by the real addresses, and clicking anywhere in a row opens it

docs.title: Work Units
docs.text:
• Triage summary — the detail page opens on a summary header with the response actions in a bar visible on every tab
  • Replay — a full-screen view rebuilds a work unit in the order it was observed
  • Growing relationship graph — Show 5 more adds relationships on request, up to 200 nodes
  • Redesigned edge and signal windows, and the Work Units page fills its node data columns and applies the filters you set

docs.title: Vrax
docs.text: • Vrax threat-intelligence import — connect a Vrax login on Signals, Node Enrichment; the appliance pulls the reports Vrax holds for its industry and region on a schedule and shows the ones that mention a node in its detail window. Nothing from your data is sent to Vrax

docs.title: Conductor
docs.text:
• Seven new pull connectors — Cloudflare, VPC flow logs from AWS, Azure, GCP and OCI, SNMP (v2c and v3) and an HTTP poll
  • NetFlow and IPFIX collector — NetFlow v5, v7 and v9 and IPFIX on UDP 2055 and HTTP 8008, off until enabled under Log Servers
  • OCSF 1.8.0 encoding in the artifact exporter
  • Faster connector retries — a transient failure is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40, then 60 seconds instead of 15 minutes

docs.title: Receiver capacity
docs.text:
• Body profiles — a default and a small profile, chosen from the container's memory budget or WF_INGEST_PROFILE
  • Connection limits — per-listener caps and a per-source share, set with WF_CONN_MAX, WF_CONN_MAX_TLS, WF_CONN_MAX_PER_SOURCE and WF_CONN_TRUSTED
  • Message limit — the largest artifact is 9.5 MiB; batches over 1,000 artifacts are refused

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Required encryption key — Docker Compose stacks must set AUTH_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY; the old shipped default is refused
  • Tighter edge and ports — internal services publish on INTERNAL_LISTEN_IP, a TLS edge trusts no forwarder unless WF_TRUSTED_PROXIES names it, and the reverse proxy no longer serves /ingestion/
  • Platform administrators and SSO — an organization's SAML or LDAP no longer signs in platform administrators unless the operator names that organization
  • Session keys — Conductor UI and Console UI refuse a SECRET_KEY that shipped with an earlier release or an example file
  • Signed images — keyless signatures you can check with cosign verify

docs.title: Upgrade Notes
docs.text: • Read the upgrade guide first — the order for WFA appliances (images to 1.2.0, then WFA 2.5.3, then wfa restart), the encryption-key steps for Docker Compose, single sign-on changes, custom-role changes and the known limitations are in Upgrading to 1.2.0

docs.title: v1.1.5 (2026-09-19)
docs.text: Maintenance release for the 1.1.x line. Most of it closes defects where the product reported something other than what it was doing. Full release notes.

docs.title: AI assistant
docs.text:
• OpenAI and Google Gemini now work — both providers had been placeholders that answered every question with fixed text. They are fully implemented, including tool use. If you used either before 1.1.5, re-review work units the AI agent auto-resolved, and expect real provider charges
  • Tools on a local model — with Ollama, the assistant now runs the full loop of question, data lookup and answer on the appliance
  • Safer auto-resolve — a work unit auto-resolves only on an AI analysis that is verifiably complete
  • Manage AI required — AI provider configuration endpoints now require the Manage AI permission

docs.title: MCP
docs.text: • Streamable HTTP transport — Claude Desktop, Cursor and Claude Code can connect over the transport they speak natively. Off by default

docs.title: Also fixed
docs.text:
• Search returned fewer results than it found for sparse filters
  • Arista Wi-Fi events were discarded; LimaCharlie authentication failures were silent; a Zscaler connector queried an endpoint that no longer exists
  • Deduplication memory grew without bound on long-running appliances

docs.title: v1.1.4 (2026-09-17)
docs.text: Maintenance release on the 1.1.x line with customer-visible fixes. Full release notes.

docs.title: v1.1.2 (2026-08-13)
docs.text: Maintenance release focused on event-time search correctness and a broad data-onboarding expansion. Drop-in upgrade from any 1.1.x; no configuration or schema changes. Full release notes.

docs.title: Search timing
docs.text:
• Artifacts are searched by event time — when a parser reads the event's own timestamp, timelines, windows and drill-downs use it, so telemetry arriving minutes or hours late (relayed Zeek/Corelight sensors, store-and-forward syslog, pull connectors) lands in the window where an analyst will look. Timestamps are sanity-bounded (≤30 days late, ≤1 hour skew); out-of-bounds values and pre-1.1.2 records fall back to arrival time
  • Fixed: timeline showed records but filters returned no rows for lagging sources (observed live on a relayed Corelight feed ~3.5h behind)
  • "Filter for" pivots use exact matching, mirroring the facet panel and running faster server-side

docs.title: Data onboarding
docs.text:
• Zeek / Corelight full extraction — ISO 8601 timestamps (Corelight default) previously fell to a generic classification with no client/server addresses; all timestamp forms now handled, log types routed by _path, Corelight extensions (L2 addresses, VLAN, app tags, shunt counters) captured
  • Cisco Secure Network Analytics (Stealthwatch) 7.x CEF alarms fully parsed as security signal; legacy format unchanged
  • Palo Alto PAN-OS SYSTEM logs (device telemetry, URL-database updates and other operational subtypes) recognized on current PAN-OS releases
  • Microsoft Graph: alerts from all Defender workloads (was Office 365 only) + Secure Score posture snapshots
  • VMware: vCenter SSO auth failures (expired/locked accounts), NSX-T DFW packet logs on ESXi 8, NSX network-operations agent, ESXi 8 system services, VxRail manager services, ESXi Envoy proxy
  • New sources: Lantronix (Uplogix) Local Manager, Cisco AP watchdog telemetry, HPE ProLiant Management Agent storage events

docs.title: Pipeline reliability
docs.text: • Automated parser-coverage pipeline correctly recognizes already-handled formats; appliance-internal service chatter classified as diagnostics (never false security signal); advisory-scan and release-tag CI hardening

docs.title: v1.1.1 (2026-08-10)
docs.text: Maintenance release covering everything since 1.1.0 — appliance reliability, broader VMware and Azure onboarding coverage, reporter and demo-data corrections, the WitFoo Console deployment option, and a security pass. Drop-in upgrade from 1.1.0; ships alongside WFA 2.4.13. Full release notes.

docs.title: Appliance reliability
docs.text:
• Role changes complete cleanly — reconfiguring an appliance from one role to another (e.g. Conductor → All-in-One) previously left the old role's containers running and holding their ports, so the new role's web front end could not start ("port is already allocated"). The agent now reclaims the previous role's containers before starting the new stack and on each reconcile pass, matching only WitFoo's own container names so anything else on the host is untouched. Requires WFA 2.4.13
  • Shutdown attempts every container and reports all failures together, instead of abandoning the remainder at the first problem
  • Unused images and orphaned broker data reclaimed automatically after upgrades or re-identification
  • Support packages now capture the Conductor UI and both message brokers, and no longer include configuration secrets
  • All-in-One + Conductor appliances report pipeline health — that role previously emitted no pipeline metrics in status reports
  • Disk-capacity enforcement clamped to warnings while the measurement basis is corrected; alerts still fire
  • wfa user-reset heals an older-install schema difference

docs.title: Data onboarding
docs.text:
• Widened VMware ESXi / vCenter / NSX / vSAN and Dell VxRail coverage from live unrecognized-traffic analysis
  • New coverage for Arista flow control, Stealthbits Activity Monitor, and CalPrivate
  • Corrected stream and event classifications for the 2026-08 device batch
  • Azure / Microsoft connector resilience — Sentinel, Graph, Defender for Vulnerability Management and LimaCharlie now decode authentication token responses robustly
  • Log framing corruption fixed for newline-delimited TCP; byte-window framing corruption is now classified as a transport problem rather than an unknown device type

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: • WitFoo Console deployment option — selectable as a node role during appliance configuration, licensed as its own no-cost option

docs.title: Reporter
docs.text:
• Report generation and date-range queries no longer hit the short request timeout that returned errors or empty pages; generation is restricted to administrators
  • Demo cost-savings report no longer shows all zeros

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Report access enforces role permissions — the reporting endpoints checked authentication and organization but not the caller's role, so any signed-in organization member could read report snapshots and export CSV, including roles intended to have no reporting access. Every reporting route now requires the appropriate read or export permission, with an automated check preventing recurrence. Organization scoping was always enforced, so no cross-organization exposure was possible. Upgrade recommended
  • gRPC dependency updated to its patched release (high-severity advisory)
  • Container build no longer fetches a CLI tool over the network during the image build
  • All open code-scanning findings reviewed — fixed or documented with a specific justification, with residual items owned rather than untriaged

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
• Fleet-outage detection no longer depends on the telemetry an outage suppresses; alert thresholds count unbroken failure streaks; probes blocked by an intermediary report as unverified rather than healthy
  • Approved device parsers propagate to customer-production images automatically

docs.title: v1.1.0 (2026-07-14)
docs.text: Feature release on the 1.0.0 GA line — from signal to evidence and decisive action. Sharper investigations, the new Certify compliance-certification capability, scheduled report delivery, broader data onboarding, and a hardened, verified multi-tenant foundation. A recommended, drop-in upgrade for all 1.0.x deployments. Watch the 1.1.0 tour.

docs.title: Investigation
docs.text:
• One-click CVE explanations — click any CVE in a report or on a host for a plain-language explanation (severity, description, weakness type), served offline from a committed CVE library with no internet calls
  • Exploitability-aware threat scoring — a live vulnerability on a host connected to an outside asset now raises incident suspicion and flags attacker and victim, with a new "Weak Edge" view (CVE × technique × attacker × victim) alongside Attack Chain
  • Verdict-first entity detail — the node/entity panel leads with a clear verdict ("Suspicious · 39% · Medium") then why-flagged / where-who / related / activity, values humanized, raw JSON and schema behind an Advanced disclosure
  • In-panel relationship pivoting — search all of an entity's relationships from its panel with a "Top relationships" shortlist (internal users first)
  • The true target of an attack is always visible — the internal host under attack is no longer missing from a work unit's evidence and graph; attacker→victim is correctly linked

docs.title: Asset & Identity
docs.text:
• Accurate internal-user classification — a user counts as internal/managed only when sourced from a real identity system (Entra ID, AD, Okta, Ping…); log noise and failed logins no longer inflate the count
  • Open-port visibility on assets — assets carry the observed network services (open ports), searchable and filterable from asset search
  • Full-scope range filtering — min/max filters for an asset's port, vulnerability, and product counts now narrow the entire dataset, not just the rows on screen

docs.title: Compliance & Certify
docs.text:
• Certify — audit certification packages (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / CMMC) — build an audit submission inside WitFoo with guided questions, malware-scanned attachments, and live-data auto-population, exported as one integrity-hashed package (report + attachments + manifest) streamed on demand (Pro/Max tiers)
  • One Auditor, many frameworks — adds PCI DSS v4.0 and Essential Eight mappings beyond CIS Controls
  • ISO 27001 updated to the 2022 standard — built-in ISO 27001 moves to the current :2022 Annex A (93 controls)
  • Honest compliance-readiness score — partial control coverage now counts as partial, so the readiness percentage reflects reality

docs.title: Reporting & Data
docs.text:
• Scheduled report delivery — schedule reports and dashboards as offline PDFs delivered on a cadence to notification channels (email attaches the PDF; Slack and webhook get a link and summary)
  • Retention-ceiling visibility — the health dashboard charts the oldest record's age against the enforced retention limit, per data type

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
• LevelBlue / USM Anywhere ingest — pull LevelBlue (AlienVault) USM Anywhere alarms and events via one API credential per tenant, with no endpoint or agent changes
  • VMware NSX-T log coverage — recognizes and classifies NSX-T log sources that had been flooding the unknowns bucket
  • Accurate Integration Health — a raw log-server listener is no longer shown as an API-pull integration; only genuine integrations appear
  • Self-monitoring of ingestion quality — automated monitoring flags data-classification anomalies and opens a tracked issue on its own
  • vCenter Broker telemetry parser — added, queued for human sign-off before activation

docs.title: Reliability & Demo
docs.text:
• Dependable operations dashboard — the Conductor dashboard no longer hangs on endless spinners; it shows data fast, fills charts from the last known-good view, marks stale data, and offers Retry on failure
  • Realistic, story-driven demo — a coherent scenario around a believable regional-healthcare organization facing technique-mapped attacks replaces random demo noise

docs.title: Trust & Quality
docs.text:
• Tamper-proof cross-cluster threat intel — shared threat-intel messages between clusters are cryptographically sealed end to end (body, not just labels), rolled out to keep mixed-version clusters working during upgrades
  • Verified access-control enforcement — automated safeguards confirm every part of the platform enforces the correct permissions; remaining gaps were closed
  • New permissions reach upgraded customers — new permissions (Certify, graph, automation) converge to already-deployed environments on upgrade, with no admin hand-editing of roles
  • Quality & multi-tenant isolation hardening — a structured program closed test-suite blind spots (notably one-tenant-cannot-see-another isolation) plus coverage, mobile, accessibility, and resilience checks
  • Delivery-pipeline hardening — recurring release-process risks turned into automated guardrails (git-enforced pre-commit hooks, static guards, contract tests), with the release test suite rescoped to run reliably in CI while exhaustive validation continues on live lab and beta appliances

docs.title: v1.0.0 (2026-06-30)
docs.text: General-availability (GA) release. Builds on the 0.9.8 baseline with two new executive reports, a major step up in AI provider control and cost governance, a real collaboration layer, responsive mobile/tablet support, and a dedicated pre-1.0 full code review. Ships alongside WitFoo Management Console 1.9.0, Conductor 1.8.0, and WFA 2.4.2. Upgrade recommended.

docs.title: Reporting & Compliance
docs.text:
• Vulnerability Management report — hosts ranked by severity-weighted exposure, with host↔CVE drill-down, all server-paginated for large estates
  • Threat Model report — your security controls mapped against the MITRE ATT&CK matrix from real audit findings, with per-cell drill-down and an optional AI narrative
  • Reporter improvements — correct dark-theme charts, interactive drill-down and paging on the threat and vulnerability views, and a reorganized Reporter navigation

docs.title: AI & Automation
docs.text:
• AI Provider Enhancement — per-provider model catalogs with best-practice defaults and an economy tier; pre-save live model interrogation (your key is validated, never logged); and a best/economy AI profile that auto-routes each purpose to an appropriate model, preserving operator pins
  • Improved AI tooling — the assistant can use read-only platform tools to ground answers in your live data
  • MCP Authentication — optional per-organization bearer/API-key auth for the Model Context Protocol integration (default off; keys hashed at rest, shown once)
  • AI summary caching — on-demand summaries (including Auditor findings) cached per organization to cut cost and latency

docs.title: Collaboration & Profile
docs.text:
• User Profile — self-hosted avatar upload, self-service password and locale, presence and author cards, and one-click "message a user"
  • Chat Upgrade — file attachments, emoji reactions, and a more robust realtime connection
  • CyberGrid community — share Work Units and Work Collections to the community directory, a within- and cross-cluster User Directory, and a durable, self-healing directory-submission pipeline that reports its true status

docs.title: Detection & Pipeline
docs.text:
• Azure Email Security — Microsoft Defender for Office 365 phishing email and phishing-click signals now produce Work Units
  • VMware NSX-T parsing — NSX-T operational and degraded-service events classified and actionable instead of landing in unknown
  • Conductor visibility — per-agent up/down/health for Beats agents, expanded Integration Health detail, the Conductor link hidden on non-Conductor nodes, and corrected Cisco Umbrella configuration fields
  • Search & collections — Work Unit search on client IP across source and destination addresses; Work Collections on hostnames, URLs, file names, and file hashes; plus facet, Client-IP-search, and pagination fixes

docs.title: Platform & Operations
docs.text:
• Mobile & tablet support — responsive Analytics, Conductor, and Console UIs with drawer navigation and touch-friendly controls below desktop widths
  • Sign-in — the login page defaults to SAML single sign-on when enabled (local login always reachable); Azure/SAML SSO reliability fixes
  • Health dashboard — a Data Retention card showing the actually-enforced retention, a corrected host Total Memory gauge, and a per-node Cassandra health view
  • Improved automated monitoring — telemetry redacted at the source under a configurable policy (off/standard/strict); opt-in, PII-free cluster-problem reporting
  • Console node management — Analytics nodes managed from the Console with an accurate last-seen-based online/offline indicator

docs.title: Infrastructure & Hardening
docs.text:
• Pre-1.0 full code review — external-dependency and vulnerability verification, Cassandra optimization (including a 5.0.8 upgrade with a per-node health monitor), an adversarial re-review of the entire 0.9.8→1.0.0 change set, deeper test and docker-log coverage, documentation accuracy, and an expanded certification curriculum
  • Continued supply-chain and CI security-gate hardening (secret scanning, static analysis, dependency and image scanning, log-injection and SSRF call-site gates)

docs.title: v0.9.8 (2026-06-23)
docs.text: Operational-resilience, AI-cost, and pipeline-coverage release with broad security hardening. Ships alongside WitFoo Management Console 1.8.0, Conductor 1.7.0, and WFA 2.3.0. Upgrade recommended.

docs.title: Security & Hardening
docs.text:
• Resolved a class of log-injection and outbound-request (anti-rebinding / SSRF) hardening findings across the platform and the management console; outbound connections now validate the destination host before any credentials are attached
  • Tightened per-route access controls across the incident and configuration APIs, with a build-time guard that fails the pipeline on any newly ungated route
  • Stronger TLS/certificate validation on appliance-to-Conductor health checks
  • Refreshed dependency tree and supply-chain updates, plus new recurring-vulnerability prevention gates (secret scanning, app/image SAST, signed images and SBOMs) added to the build pipeline
  • Azure / SAML single sign-on reliability — assertion-replay handling bounded to the provider acceptance window and request-binding fixes, so a valid login is no longer falsely rejected as a replay

docs.title: Operational Resilience
docs.text:
• Compliance Readiness no longer strands at 0% after a redeploy — a snapshot guard preserves the last healthy compliance figure and a startup probe waits for data readiness before regenerating, so a restart can never serve a collapsed 0% snapshot
  • AI cost optimization — Anthropic prompt caching, a cheaper model tier for report and on-demand summaries, and demo-mode containment dramatically cut AI spend
  • Production Dashboards — Custom Dashboard widgets now show real production data or an explicit empty state, never placeholder sample data in a live tenant (sample data renders only in the editor preview or under demo mode)
  • Monorepo consolidation — one codebase with change-detected image builds for faster, more reliable releases and independent per-product versioning (no customer-visible behavior change)
  • WFA broker-startup deadlock resilience — a node can no longer get permanently wedged during service initialization; the startup gate is now bounded, observable, and self-creating of its broker objects

docs.title: Conductor & Pipeline
